86:### 9.9 The month-end run, in order (from 12 October 2026)
### 9.9 The month-end run, in order (from 12 October 2026)

Section 9.8 describes the one-off bootstrap. Every month-end after that follows the steps below, in this order, for the month being closed (September 2026 in the examples). Each step can be run from its screen or by the command shown; a step that lacks its input refuses with the reason named rather than writing a partial result. Anything that changes a governed figure (a loan book build, a fit, a scenario set, a qualitative trigger, an overlay) is proposed by one person and approved by another.

| # | Step | Screen | Command |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Land the E-Banker pack (dates in `yyyy-mm-dd`, row counts in the manifest) | Customer & Loan Data, Imports & Feeds, E-Banker Loads | `php artisan eir:land-pack <folder> --user=<id>` (route 2: the scheduler polls the feed folder at 06:30 each day) |
| 2 | Build the month's loan book; a second person approves | Imports & Feeds, Loan Book Builds | `php artisan eir:build-loan-books 2026-09` |
| 3 | Trial balance and any change to the prime lending rate | Imports & Feeds; EIR Data, Reference Rates | `php artisan eir:import-trial-balances <folder>`; `php artisan eir:import-reference-rates <file> --user=<id>` |
| 4 | Raise or close qualitative SICR triggers for the month (watch-list, restructuring, drought, covenant breach...) | IFRS 9 Model Setup, Staging & SICR Rules, SICR Trigger Alerts | (screen only, maker-checker) |
| 5 | Stage the book: days past due against the governed thresholds, the missed-instalment trigger, then the approved qualitative triggers | Staging & SICR Rules | `php artisan eir:stage 2026-09 --user=<id>` |
| 6 | PD and LGD by segment on the governed basis (Governance Centre, PD & LGD segments) | PD Model; LGD Model | `php artisan ifrs9:segment-parameters 2026-09 --user=<id>` |
| 7 | Scenario set for the period (quarterly, or when the outlook changes): seed, review, approve, lock | Scenarios & Overlays, Scenario Sets | `php artisan scenario:sets 2026-09 --seed`, then approve on the screen |
| 8 | Forward-looking model: the correlation sweep as at the month-end, a fit proposed and approved, the route applied to every loan | Forward-Looking Model, Correlation Finder and Regression (FLI Adjustments) | `php artisan fli:correlate 2026-09`; propose and approve the fit on the Regression screen; `php artisan fli:apply 2026-09 --user=<id>` |
| 9 | Expected credit loss for every portfolio, on the post-FLI PD | ECL Processing, ECL Calculation | `php artisan ifrs9:segment-ecl 2026-09 --pd=pd_post_fli` |
| 10 | EIR revenue roll-forward | EIR & Revenue Recognition, EIR Calculations | `php artisan eir:run-revenue 2026-09 --user=<id>` |
| 11 | Mega Farm programme | ECL Processing, Mega Farm Programme | `php artisan megafarm:ecl 2026-09 --user=<id>` |
| 12 | Review: the Workspace close checklist, the dashboard (ECL build-up), the Reports hub (IFRS 9 note, RBM return, reconciliations) | Workspace; Dashboard; Reports | (screens) |
| 13 | Management sign-off and the period lock: no later build restates a locked month | Workspace | `php artisan eir:lock-period 2026-09 --user=<id> --reason="September 2026 close"` |

**Order matters.** A new PD run (step 6) clears the post-FLI PD of the month, because that PD was built on the old one; steps 8 and 9 must follow it. Re-staging a month (step 5) likewise requires steps 6, 8 and 9 again. The ECL run (step 9) refuses when any loan with exposure has no stage, PD or LGD, and names the loans.

**The scheduler.** Run `php artisan schedule:run` every minute (Windows Task Scheduler or cron, chapter 7). It polls the E-Banker feed folder each morning and imports the World Bank macro series on the second day of each month.

**Before a month is presented.** The forward-looking result rests on a short history (the PLR against the Stage 3 share, about two years of monthly data); the segment PDs on small portfolios take the pooled book's PD under the governed thin-segment rule, recorded per cell; sectors coded 4290 by E-Banker are held apart as an unverified default code; write-offs follow specification v4 section 3.8 (status H and the 29 June 2026 transfer to GL 1064).

18	            'body' => '<p>IFRS 9 asks you to measure expected credit losses using not only what has happened, but what is likely to happen in the economy. The platform calls this forward-looking information, or FLI. This article explains the whole chain from the economic numbers you type in to the adjusted probability of default (PD) that the ECL run finally uses. Risk and finance staff who own the IFRS 9 model read this once; everyone else can go straight to the page they need. All of the pages sit in the sidebar under Financial Modelling (the staging and SICR rules under Governance Centre; Macro Statistics under Data Foundation), in two groups: Forward-Looking Model and Management Overlays.</p><h4>What you see on the screen</h4><ul><li><b>Forward-Looking Model</b> in the sidebar holds six pages, in the order you normally use them: Macro Elements, Scenario Profiles, Weighted Forecast, Credit Loss Data, Adjusted Forecast and Regression Analysis.</li><li><b>Management Overlays</b> holds three pages: Economic Scenarios, External Calculations and Calculation History. An overlay is a management decision applied on top of the model output; here it is the step that actually writes the adjusted PD onto the loan book.</li></ul><h4>The chain, step by step</h4><ol><li><b>Macro elements and their values.</b> A macro element is one economic series, such as inflation, the exchange rate or GDP growth. On Macro Elements you define each series once (name, code, unit, frequency, source) and then enter its values month by month. Each value is marked either Historical (what actually happened) or Forecast (what you expect), and a forecast value is tagged to a scenario inside a scenario profile.</li><li><b>Scenario profiles and their weights.</b> A scenario profile is a named set of economic outlooks, normally a base case, an upside and a downside. Each scenario carries a probability, which is its weight. The Status tick on the Scenario Profiles list turns green only when the weights inside the profile add up to exactly 100 percent.</li><li><b>Weighted forecast.</b> The Weighted Forecast page multiplies each forecast value by its scenario weight and adds the results together, giving one probability-weighted number per macro element per month. This is done by <code>MacroForecastWeightedService</code>: for every macro element it collects the forecast months tagged to the profile you chose, and for each month adds up value times probability divided by 100 across the scenarios. The answer is stored twice: as a new macro value with the source Weighted Calculation, and as a row on the Weighted Forecast list.</li><li><b>Credit loss data.</b> Regression needs a history of what you are trying to predict. Credit Loss Data holds observed monthly metrics per portfolio, such as PD, LGD, ECL, EAD or the non-performing loan (NPL) figure, entered by hand or imported from a CSV file.</li><li><b>Regression.</b> Regression is a statistical method that finds the straight-line relationship between one thing you want to predict (the dependent variable, for example NPL) and one or more things you can observe (the independent variables, your macro elements). Regression Analysis trains such a model with <code>RegressionService</code>: it lines up the months where the credit loss metric and every chosen macro element all have historical values, solves for an intercept and one coefficient per macro element, and reports R squared (how much of the movement the model explains), adjusted R squared, standard errors, t-statistics and p-values. You then Activate and Approve the model.</li><li><b>Adjusted forecast.</b> The Adjusted Forecast page is a calculator. You give it the intercept and coefficient from a regression, a baseline value and the macro forecasts per scenario with their weights; it shows the weighted macro path and the forecast value for each year, and the percentage change from the baseline.</li><li><b>Economic scenario set and external calculation.</b> On Economic Scenarios you record the scenario set (names and weights that must sum to 100 percent) that management has approved for the reporting period. On External Calculations you enter the reporting period, the base values, the regression slope and intercept and the weighted macro value for each future month. The page works out a predicted value per month and an FLI adjustment, which is the predicted value divided by the base predicted value, minus one. For example, a predicted value of 0.055 against a base of 0.050 gives an adjustment of plus 10 percent.</li><li><b>Post-FLI PD on the loan book.</b> When you click Update Loanbook, every loan in the reporting period is read. Stage 1 loans use the adjustment for the 12-month window; Stage 2 loans use the window closest to their remaining term; Stage 3 loans are set to a PD of 100 percent. Each loan\'s post-FLI PD is its pre-FLI PD multiplied by one plus the adjustment, floored at 0 percent and capped at 100 percent, and the adjustment itself is stored on the loan as <code>fli_adj</code>.</li></ol><h4>What happens next</h4><p>On Financial Modelling, the ECL Calculation form has a PD Type choice: PD Before FLI or PD After FLI. Choose PD After FLI to use the post-FLI PD written by step 8. The loan book screen and the forward-looking reports read the same column, so the figure you see on the Loan Book is the one used in the run. The ECL run never writes the post-FLI PD back; only the External Calculations page owns it.</p><h4>Common problems</h4><ul><li><b>The Status column on Scenario Profiles shows a red cross.</b> The weights in the profile do not add to 100 percent. Open the profile with the eye icon and correct the probabilities.</li><li><b>Regression fails with "Insufficient overlapping data".</b> The credit loss metric and every chosen macro element must share the same historical months. Check both pages for gaps.</li><li><b>Update Loanbook says "No loans found for reporting period".</b> Import the loan book for that month first (Data Foundation, Imports), then run the update again.</li></ul>',

<?php

/*
|--------------------------------------------------------------------------
| User Manual: Financial Modelling (second half), Forward-Looking Information
|--------------------------------------------------------------------------
| The forward-looking module as rebuilt on 13 October 2026 (FLI module
| specification v1): the month-end Overview and Impact Analysis, Macro
| Statistics with the scenario assumptions, the model and its versions, the
| scenarios and the overlays. The article titles are kept from the earlier
| chapter so the seeder refreshes them in place; the first half of the
| chapter (staging, PD and LGD) lives in a sibling file.
*/

return [
    'Financial Modelling' => [

        'Forward-looking information: how it works' => [
            'body' => '<p>IFRS 9 asks for expected credit losses that look ahead: a probability-weighted amount over a range of economic outcomes, using information available at the reporting date. In this system that is the <b>Forward-Looking Information</b> entry in the sidebar. It has four parts, used in this order.</p><ol><li><b>FLI Month-End</b>: the <b>Overview</b> walks a month through its ten steps and runs them; <b>Impact Analysis</b> shows what the forward-looking information did to the ECL.</li><li><b>Macro Statistics</b>: the economic variables and their values, and the <b>Scenario Assumptions</b> (the weight of each scenario and the shocks that move each variable).</li><li><b>Forward-Looking Model</b>: the credit-loss history, the Correlation Finder and Regression that fit the model, the <b>Model Versions</b> in force, the Adjusted Forecast (the PD year by year under each scenario) and the Weighted Forecast.</li><li><b>Scenarios &amp; Overlays</b>: Scenario Profiles (templates), Scenario Sets (propose and approve), Economic Scenarios (the workbench), Manual Overlays, External Calculations and Calculation History.</li></ol><h4>How the figure is made</h4><p>The model links one economic variable to one credit-loss measure, for example the prime lending rate nine months earlier to the share of accounts in Stage 3. For each scenario of the approved set, the model predicts the measure from that scenario\'s path and compares it with the prediction from today\'s value; the ratio, less one, moves each loan\'s PD. The ECL is measured under each scenario and weighted by the scenario weights; the PD the system books on each loan is the one whose ECL equals that weighted ECL. Stage 3 loans are not moved by the scenarios.</p><h4>What changes when</h4><ul><li><b>Every month-end</b>: the model version in force is applied; nothing is re-fitted.</li><li><b>Every quarter</b>, or when the outlook moves: a new scenario set, proposed by one person and approved by another.</li><li><b>Once a year</b>, or after an event that breaks the relationship (a devaluation, a drought): the model is recalibrated and approved as a new version.</li></ul><h4>Common problems</h4><ul><li><b>The Overview says no model version is in force.</b> Approve a fit on Regression; approval publishes it as the version in force from that month.</li><li><b>The ECL step refuses.</b> A new PD run clears the post-FLI PD; run the forward-looking route again (the Overview does it for you).</li><li><b>Weighted ECL does not tie to the booked ECL.</b> The ECL was calculated before the route last ran: calculate it again, then record the month.</li></ul>',
            'images' => ['fli' => 'The Forward-Looking Information entry in the sidebar'],
            'routes' => ['fli.overview', 'fli.impact'],
        ],

        'Macro elements' => [
            'body' => '<p><b>Macro Statistics</b> holds the economic variables the model reads. Open Forward-Looking Information, Macro Statistics. It has five tabs.</p><ul><li><b>Dashboard</b>: one card per variable with how many values it holds and where the last came from. Click a card to see its values.</li><li><b>Variables</b>: the list of variables with their unit, frequency, source and source codes (WB: the World Bank code, IMF: the WEO code). <b>Add variable</b> at the top right opens a window: a code in capitals (for example MAIZE_PRICE), a name, unit, frequency, source and the codes. The pencil edits a variable; the bin deletes one, and the system refuses while it still holds values or a model or a scenario uses it, saying which.</li><li><b>Data Entry</b>: the values of one variable. <b>Add value</b> at the top right takes the period, the value, whether it is a forecast, the date the publisher released it, and a reason. The pencil corrects a value (with a reason; the old value stays in the audit log); the bin deletes one.</li><li><b>Scenario Assumptions</b>: the weights and shocks of the scenario sets; see the article on scenario assumptions.</li><li><b>Import / Export</b>: the history of every load. <b>Import</b> at the top right opens a window with four sources: your own file (any variable, in the layout series_code, period, value, is_forecast, source, published_at), the World Bank (fetched live), the IMF World Economic Outlook file and the Reserve Bank policy-rate file. Press Preview, check the rows, then Import. <b>Export CSV</b> downloads every value in the same layout, so you can export, edit and import back.</li></ul><h4>Why the release date matters</h4><p>A figure is read for a month only if it was published by the end of that month. A forecast released in October never changes a figure for March.</p>',
            'steps' => [
                'Open Forward-Looking Information, Macro Statistics, Variables, and use Add variable for a new series.',
                'Open Data Entry, choose the variable and use Add value; or use Import at the top right for many values.',

                'Correct a wrong value with the pencil and a reason; never delete and retype.',
            ],
            'images' => ['macro-elements' => 'Macro Statistics, Variables, with Add variable at the top right'],
            'routes' => ['macro-statistics.index', 'macro-statistics.variables.store', 'macro-statistics.variables.update', 'macro-statistics.variables.destroy', 'macro-statistics.observations.update', 'macro-statistics.observations.destroy', 'macro-statistics.manual', 'macro-statistics.csv-preview', 'macro-statistics.csv-commit', 'macro-statistics.export'],
        ],

        'Scenario profiles' => [
            'body' => '<p>A <b>scenario profile</b> is a reusable template: the scenarios (for example Base, Upside, Downside, Severe), their weights, what each is anchored to and the shocks each applies. Open Forward-Looking Information, Scenarios &amp; Overlays, Scenario Profiles.</p><ul><li><b>Add the standard profile</b> creates MAIIC four scenarios: Base 50, Upside 15, Downside 25 and Severe 10, each anchored to a Malawi episode (the 2021 recovery, the 2023 devaluation, the 2016 drought).</li><li><b>Profile</b> and <b>Scenario</b> at the top right create your own; the eye opens a profile\'s scenarios and the pencil edits it.</li><li><b>Start a set</b>, with the month chosen at the top of the list, creates a <b>draft</b> scenario set for that month from the profile. A draft reaches no loan: you set its weights and shocks on Macro Statistics, Scenario Assumptions, then propose it on Scenario Sets, and a second person approves it.</li></ul>',
            'steps' => [
                'Open Scenario Profiles and choose the month at the top of the list.',

                'Adjust the weights and shocks on Macro Statistics, Scenario Assumptions.',
                'Propose the set on Scenario Sets; a second person approves it.',

            'images' => ['scenario-profiles' => 'Scenario Profiles with Start a set'],

Below it you enter or import <b>external series</b>, such as the Reserve Bank\'s industry NPL ratio, which give the model a longer history than MAIIC\'s own books. Leave the portfolio empty for an industry series, and give the date it was published: the model does not read it for any month before that date. <b>Add record</b>, <b>Import CSV</b> and <b>Measure</b> (a new kind of measure) are at the top right; the pencil and the bin edit and delete a record.</p>',

        'Adjusted forecast' => [
            'body' => '<p><b>Adjusted Forecast</b> shows what the model in force forecasts under each scenario, year by year: the credit-loss measure and the adjustment to the PD (year 1 is the one booked), and each portfolio\'s PD term structure: the conditional PD of each year, the probability of surviving to it, the marginal PD and the cumulative PD. After the governed forecast horizon the adjustment returns to nil in equal steps. <b>Project the scenarios</b> at the top right runs it for the month; the Overview runs it as step 8. A reviewer <b>proposes</b> a fit and a second person <b>approves</b> it. Approval publishes it as a <b>model version</b> in force from that month until it is replaced. <b>Model Versions</b> lists every version, which one is in force, the months each governed, and lets a version be retired (the months after it go back to the version before). The set itself is changed on Scenario Assumptions and approved on Scenario Sets.</p><p><b>Manual Overlays</b> are management judgements added on top of the model: a percentage on the PD of the book, a product group or a contract, with a reason, evidence, an owner and an expiry month, approved by a second person.         'External calculations and calculation history' => [

A step that needs a person (an import, an approval) says what to do and links to its screen; the others have a Run button and run in the background with their output on the right. <b>Run the remaining steps</b> at the top right runs every automated step that is not done and stops at the first that needs a person.</p><p><b>Waiting for a second person</b> lists the fits, scenario sets, overlays and external models proposed for the month, with an approve button; you cannot approve your own. <b>The month\'s record</b> shows the ECL before FLI, the forward-looking effect, the ECL booked, the ECL under each scenario and whether the weighted figure ties. const puppeteer = require('C:/xampp/htdocs/MAICC-IFRS9/node_modules/puppeteer');
const c = require(process.argv[2]);
const OUT = 'C:/xampp/htdocs/MAICC-IFRS9/public/manual/screenshots/';
const SHOTS = {
  'macro-elements': 'macro-statistics?tab=variables',
  'scenario-profiles': 'scenario-profiles',

};
(async () => {
  const b = await puppeteer.launch({ headless: 'new' });
  const p = await b.newPage();
  await p.setViewport({ width: 1600, height: 1000 });
  await p.setCookie({ name: c.name, value: c.value, domain: '127.0.0.1', path: '/' });
  for (const [key, path] of Object.entries(SHOTS)) {
    let ok = false;
    for (let i = 0; i < 3 && !ok; i++) {
      const errs = [];
      p.removeAllListeners('console');
      p.on('console', m => { if (m.type() === 'error') errs.push(m.text()); });
      await p.goto('http://127.0.0.1:8070/' + path, { waitUntil: 'load', timeout: 120000 });
      await new Promise(r => setTimeout(r, 3000));
      ok = errs.length === 0;
      if (ok) await p.screenshot({ path: OUT + key + '.jpg', type: 'jpeg', quality: 85 });
    }
    console.log(key, ok ? 'saved' : 'FAILED');
  }
  await b.close();
})().catch(e => { console.error(e.message); process.exit(1); });

Status while the two audits and the test breakdown finish in the background.

**Done and working end to end, all from the screens:**
- **The old FLI screens are back** under one new sidebar entry, Forward-Looking Information, with no "legacy" label. Each is now a working step of the governed chain: Credit Loss Data, Adjusted Forecast, Weighted Forecast, Scenario Profiles, Economic Scenarios, External Calculations and Calculation History. Three screens are new: the month-end Overview, Impact Analysis and Model Versions.
- **Model registry.** Approving a fit publishes a model version that stays in force until it is recalibrated, so a month-end no longer needs a new fit.
- **Month record.** Each month records the ECL under every scenario, a check that the weighted figure ties to the booked one, and a second-person sign-off.
- **Proof on demo.** I ran the full month-end for August from the Maintenance console. The booked ECL came back unchanged at MWK 11,314,579,806.97, with the scenario-weighted figure tying to it within MWK 0.60.
- **Macro Statistics now has real add, edit and delete** on Variables (via Add variable) and on Data Entry (via Add value). Import sits in a top-right window and also takes your own CSV. Source codes read "WB:" and "IMF:".
- **Scenario Assumptions answers "where do we add the percentages".** The Scenario weights row at the top holds every scenario's percentage, the total and a Save weights button. An approved set is locked, so its button is "New version to change it". Each scenario has its own tab, with Add a shock and Save at the top right.
- **Maintenance is down from fifteen commands to seven jobs**, including one "Run the month-end calculations" job.

**Why August showed two sets.** The second one is a draft, version 2, opened on 9 October with the reason typed as "yes". I didn't delete someone else's record. The new "Discard this draft" button removes it in one click. My own test sets for September are gone.

**Bug found and fixed.** Re-running the PD step clears the forward-looking PDs, and the Overview had still been treating the route as done. It now checks this properly.

**Tests.** All 41 forward-looking and navigation tests pass, including new ones for the registry, external models and the overlay double-count check. The full suite reports 89 failures. The few I've checked come from the inherited medical-module tests, for example a missing Vitals class. I'm confirming the rest before pushing, so nothing is pushed yet.

        $listed = LoanProductCategory::pluck('name')->map(fn ($n) => mb_strtolower(trim($n)))->all();

        return Inertia::render('LoanProductGroups/Index', [
            'filters' => \request()->all('search'),
            'groups' => $groups,
            'loansByGroup' => $inBook,
            'latestPeriod' => $latest,
            'unlisted' => $inBook->keys()->filter(fn ($g) => ! in_array(mb_strtolower(trim($g)), $listed, true))->values(),
        ]);
    }

    /** Add every product group the loan book uses that is not listed yet. */
    public function sync()
    {
        $listed = LoanProductCategory::pluck('name')->map(fn ($n) => mb_strtolower(trim($n)))->all();
        $added = 0;
        foreach (DB::table('loan_books')->whereNotNull('product_group')->distinct()->orderBy('product_group')->pluck('product_group') as $g) {
            if (trim((string) $g) === '' || in_array(mb_strtolower(trim($g)), $listed, true)) {
                continue;
            }
            LoanProductCategory::create(['name' => trim($g), 'description' => 'From the loan book (E-Banker product group)']);
            $listed[] = mb_strtolower(trim($g));
            $added++;
        }
        activity()->log("Product groups taken from the loan book: {$added}");

        return redirect()->route('groups.index')->with('success', $added ? "{$added} product group(s) added from the loan book." : 'Every product group in the loan book is already listed.');
    }"""),

    public function index(Request $request, EirCoverageService $coverage)
    {
        $periods = $coverage->availablePeriods();
        $period = (string) $request->input('period', '');
        if (! in_array($period, $periods, true)) {
            $period = $periods[0] ?? null;
        }

        $portfolio = trim((string) $request->input('portfolio', ''));
        $issue = trim((string) $request->input('issue', ''));

        $profile = $coverage->profile($period, $portfolio !== '' ? $portfolio : null);

        // Largest exposures first, optionally narrowed to one blocker: the
        // question a data request needs answered is which facilities are worth
        // chasing, not which happen to sort first by identifier.
        $contracts = $profile['contracts'];
        if ($issue !== '') {
            $contracts = array_filter($contracts, fn ($c) => in_array($issue, $c['issues'], true));
        }
        usort($contracts, fn ($a, $b) => $b['exposure'] <=> $a['exposure']);

        // The view comes from the section tab row (?tab=); a blocker filter
        // always opens the facilities behind it.
        $tab = (string) $request->input('tab', '');
        if (! in_array($tab, ['blockers', 'portfolios', 'facilities'], true)) {
            $tab = $issue !== '' ? 'facilities' : 'blockers';
        }

        return Inertia::render('Eir/Coverage', [
            'period' => $profile['period'],
            'periods' => $periods,
            'portfolios' => ContractEir::query()->whereNotNull('portfolio')->where('portfolio', '<>', '')
                ->distinct()->orderBy('portfolio')->pluck('portfolio'),

            'tabCounts' => [
                'blockers' => count($profile['issues']),

                'facilities' => count($contracts),

        ]);
    }

import { ref, onMounted } from 'vue'
import axios from 'axios'
import { usePage } from '@inertiajs/vue3'
import '@fortawesome/fontawesome-free/css/all.css';

const showHelp = ref(false)
const manual = ref(null)

// Automatically detect current route or menu path
const page = usePage()
const currentRoute = page.props.route_name // Gets example 'expected-credit-loss.index'

// Fetch manual for current route
const fetchManual = async () => {
  try {
    const res = await axios.get(`/api/manuals/route/${encodeURIComponent(currentRoute)}`)
    manual.value = res.data
  } catch (error) {
    console.error('Help manual fetch error:', error)
    manual.value = null
  }
}


onMounted(fetchManual)
</script>

function openChapter(id) {

function jump(c, slug) {
    search.value = ''
    chapter.value = c.id
    setTimeout(() => {
        const el = document.getElementById('article-' + slug)
        if (el) el.scrollIntoView({ behavior: 'smooth', block: 'start' })
    }, 50)
}

function step(delta) {
    const i = chapterIndex.value + delta
    if (i < 0) openChapter(props.front ? 'cover' : props.categories[0]?.id)
    else if (i < props.categories.length) openChapter(props.categories[i].id)
}

  <!-- The help button on a screen: opens the User Manual at the article written for this screen
       (help_article_routes), or the manual's contents when no article names the screen. -->
  <button type="button" @click="open"

<script setup>
import { usePage, router } from '@inertiajs/vue3'

const page = usePage()

async function open() {
  const name = page.props.route_name
  let slug = null
  if (name) {
    try {
      const res = await fetch(route('help.for-route', name), { credentials: 'same-origin', headers: { Accept: 'application/json' } })
      if (res.ok) slug = (await res.json()).slug
    } catch (e) { slug = null }
  }
  router.get(route('help.index'), slug ? { article: slug } : {})
}
</script>

    private static function count(string $route): ?int
    {
        if (! isset(self::TABLES[$route])) {
            return null;
        }

        return Cache::remember('section_tab_count.' . $route, 60, function () use ($route) {
            $total = 0;
            foreach ((array) self::TABLES[$route] as $table) {
                if (! Schema::hasTable($table)) {
                    return null;
                }
                $q = DB::table($table);
                if (Schema::hasColumn($table, 'deleted_at')) {
                    $q->whereNull('deleted_at');
                }
                $total += $q->count();
            }

            return $total;
        });
    }
}

--- content ---
// System codes in plain words for the screen. The codes stay what the engines
// store and read; only what a person sees changes. A code with no entry here is
// turned into a sentence ("SCHEDULE_NOT_APPROVED" reads "Schedule not approved").
const LABELS = {
    LIVE_AT_DRAWDOWN: 'The rate live at drawdown',
    AS_CAPTURED: 'As captured in E-Banker',
    SUPPLIED: 'Supplied by MAIIC',
    TAKEON_BALANCE: 'Take-on balance',
    MAIIC_EXTRACT_A: 'MAIIC extract A',
    MAIIC_EXTRACT_B: 'MAIIC extract B',
    MAIIC_EXTRACT_C: 'MAIIC extract C',
    ROUTE_1_MANUAL: 'Uploaded by hand',
    ROUTE_2_FEED: 'From the feed folder',
    ROUTE_2_FOLDER: 'From the feed folder',
    SCHEDULE_NOT_APPROVED: 'Schedule not approved',
    ORIGINAL_SCHEDULE_MISSING: 'Original schedule missing',
}

export function plainCode(value) {
    if (value === null || value === undefined || value === '') return '-'
    const v = String(value)
    if (LABELS[v]) return LABELS[v]
    if (/^[A-Z0-9]+(_[A-Z0-9]+)+$/.test(v)) {
        const s = v.toLowerCase().replace(/_/g, ' ')
        return s.charAt(0).toUpperCase() + s.slice(1)
    }
    return v
}

// The Governance Centre seeds its defaults as in force from 1 January 1900:
// on screen that is "the seeded default", not a date.
export function plainSince(date) {
    if (!date) return '-'
    return String(date).startsWith('1900') ? 'the seeded default' : String(date).slice(0, 10)
}

## CLAUDE  (2026-10-13 10:52:14 UTC)

I've fixed and pushed almost everything the first audit found. The second audit is still running; I'll work through its findings when it reports.

**Fixed (on demo, pushed to `eir_revenue_recognition`):**
- **Deleting a loan portfolio** gave a server error. It now works, and a portfolio that still holds loans is refused with a reason. The audit's leftover test portfolio is deleted.
- **The detailed disbursement export** failed. It now downloads, and exports covering every portfolio are labelled "All portfolios".
- **Loan book import** was ignoring your column mapping, and failed rows could not be downloaded. The mapping and the import type now reach the import. Rows that fail to save go to a failed-rows file, and asking for a missing file no longer errors.
- **Collateral Types** called the field "Haircut %", but the allocation uses it as the share of value kept. It is now "Value recognised", entered between 0 and 1 and shown as a percentage. The 18 types with no value are flagged "Not set". A realisation period of 0 can now be saved.
- **Collateral allocation** ignored the register date chosen on screen and opened on October, which has no loan book. It now uses that date and opens on August.
- **Clients** can be deleted from the list, the customer number must be unique, and the header no longer claims the loan book import creates them.
- **Product Groups** was empty while the loan book uses 12 groups. The screen now shows the loans per group and has a button to add the groups from the book. I pressed it on demo, so all 12 are listed.
- **Dashboard month-end status** showed PD and LGD as not applied. It now reads the loans themselves and includes a forward-looking step.
- **EIR screens:**
  - **Calculations:** the 113 contracts are "Pending" on Calculations but "Blocked" on Blockers, because one screen counts workflow state and the other missing data. The cards now explain this.
  - **GL Reconciliation:** no longer says "accounts for the variance in full" when no EIR interest has been calculated, and pages its facilities at 15.
  - **EIR as at a Date:** its tables stack instead of being cut off, and the contract list pages at 15.
  - **Plain words:** setting values and codes now read in words (for example "The rate live at drawdown"), and seeded settings show "the seeded default" instead of 1900-01-01.
- **Layout:** the "?" help button opens the User Manual at that screen's own article. Tab rows wrap instead of hiding tabs, and card labels no longer cut off. Import times show local time, and tab counts update immediately after an add or delete.

**Not changed, and why:**
- **EIR as-at figures may be wrong.** The revenue shift is minus MWK 1.76 billion, one contract (AB MWALE) has a negative gross carrying amount, and another shows contractual interest of 0 against EIR interest of 1.99 million. These are EIR engine results and need a calculation review, not a screen fix.
- **Clients aren't linked to the loan book.** No loan carries a client record, so linking them is a data decision.
- **Import history isn't filtered by type.** It lists every kind of import on each import page, because the imports table doesn't record which kind each file was.

184	    /**
185	     * Cash collected in the period, with its provenance.
186	     *
187	     * Delivered actuals are authoritative wherever the feed covers the period:
188	     * inside that window an absent row means the customer paid nothing, which
189	     * the contractual schedule cannot distinguish from a month it never
190	     * reached. Outside the window the schedule is the only evidence there is,
191	     * and the row is labelled DERIVED so a reader can tell a promise from a
192	     * receipt. A disbursement is cash advanced, not collected, and is never
193	     * netted off. Any other delivered type is excluded and reported rather
194	     * than absorbed, because its direction and component split are unknown.
195	     *
196	     * @return array{amount:float,source:string,unclassified:float}
197	     */
198	    private function cashReceived(string $contractId, string $period): array
199	    {
200	        $start = CarbonImmutable::createFromFormat('Y-m-d', $period . '-01')->startOfMonth();
201	        $end = $start->endOfMonth();
202	
203	        // The ledger covers a month when the feed's postings run past its
204	        // start and the contract existed by its end; a covered month with no
205	        // receipt is zero cash, not the schedule. System audit of 9 October
206	        // 2026, finding C5: the window was the contract's own first and last
207	        // posting, so every month after a borrower's last receipt fell back to
208	        // the schedule and the roll-forward retired a loan nobody was paying.
209	        $feedLast = (string) (DB::table('eir_actual_transactions')->max('transaction_date') ?? '');
210	        $window = DB::table('eir_actual_transactions')->where('contract_id', $contractId)
211	            ->selectRaw('MIN(transaction_date) as first_txn')->first();
212	        $contractStart = $window && $window->first_txn ? substr((string) $window->first_txn, 0, 10) : null;
213	        $covered = $feedLast !== '' && $contractStart !== null
214	            && $start->toDateString() <= substr((string) $feedLast, 0, 10)
215	            && $end->toDateString() >= $contractStart;
216	
217	        if (! $covered) {
218	            return ['amount' => $this->scheduledCash($contractId, $start, $end), 'source' => 'DERIVED', 'unclassified' => 0.0, 'derecognised' => 0.0];
219	        }
220	
221	        $collected = 0.0;
222	        $unclassified = 0.0;
223	        $derecognised = 0.0;
224	        $rows = DB::table('eir_actual_transactions')->where('contract_id', $contractId)
225	            ->whereBetween('transaction_date', [$start->toDateString(), $end->toDateString()])
226	            ->selectRaw('transaction_type, SUM(total_amount) as amount')->groupBy('transaction_type')->get();
227	
228	        foreach ($rows as $row) {
229	            if (in_array($row->transaction_type, self::COLLECTION_TYPES, true)) {
230	                $collected += (float) $row->amount;
231	            } elseif (in_array($row->transaction_type, self::DERECOGNITION_TYPES, true)) {
232	                $derecognised += (float) $row->amount;
233	            } elseif (! in_array($row->transaction_type, self::ADVANCE_TYPES, true)) {
234	                $unclassified += (float) $row->amount;
235	            }
236	        }
237	
238	        return ['amount' => $collected, 'source' => 'IMPORTED', 'unclassified' => $unclassified, 'derecognised' => $derecognised];
239	    }

<?php
namespace App\Services\Eir;
use App\Support\ContractId;
use Illuminate\Support\Facades\DB;
/**
 * Imports the contract transactions file (Extract B) without confusing actual
 * cash movements with contractual promises. The delivered Extract B has no
 * usable fee component, so absent/blank fees are deliberately routed as zero;
 * they do not manufacture a fee row or block the contractual schedule.
 */
class ContractTransactionImportService
{
    /**
     * Persisted lineage, not a display label: rows already in the database
     * carry this value and it names the vendor file an auditor will ask for.
     * The class was renamed for the operator; the stored provenance was not.
     */
    public const SOURCE = 'MAIIC_EXTRACT_B';
    public function __construct(
        private readonly RemainingScheduleImportService $remainingSchedules,
        private readonly FeeImportService $fees,
    ) {}
    public function import(array $rows): array
    {
        $scheduleRows = [];
        $feeRows = [];
        $actualRows = [];
        $held = [];
        $conflicts = [];
        $seen = [];
        $duplicates = 0;
        foreach ($rows as $index => $row) {
            $account = ContractId::normalise($row['contract_id'] ?? null) ?? '';
            $customer = trim((string) ($row['customer_id'] ?? ''));
            $subAccount = trim((string) ($row['sub_account_no'] ?? ''));
            $reference = trim((string) ($row['gl_posting_ref'] ?? ''));
            $externalId = $reference !== '' ? $reference : implode('|', [
                trim((string) ($row['run_id'] ?? '')), $account, $subAccount,
                (string) ($row['transaction_date'] ?? ''), (string) ($index + 1),
            ]);
            if (isset($seen[$externalId])) { $duplicates++; continue; }
            $seen[$externalId] = true;
            $loan = DB::table('loan_books')->where('contract_id', $account)
                ->orderByDesc('reporting_period')->first(['contract_id', 'customer_id']);
            if (! $loan) {
                $held[$account ?: 'row ' . ($index + 2)] = 'loan account is not present in the imported loan book';
                continue;
            }
            if ($customer !== '' && trim((string) $loan->customer_id) !== '' && $customer !== trim((string) $loan->customer_id)) {
                $conflicts[$account] = "customer {$customer} does not match loan-book customer {$loan->customer_id}";
                continue;
            }
            $base = ['contract_id' => $account, 'source_system' => self::SOURCE,
                'source_reference' => $reference ?: null, 'external_transaction_id' => $externalId];
            $flag = strtoupper(trim((string) ($row['scheduled_actual_flag'] ?? '')));
            if ($flag === 'SCHEDULED') {
                $scheduleRows[] = $base + ['due_date' => $row['transaction_date'] ?? null,
                    'principal_due' => (float) ($row['principal_component'] ?? 0),
                    'interest_due' => (float) ($row['interest_component'] ?? 0),
                    'fee_due' => (float) ($row['fee_component'] ?? 0),
                    'closing_balance' => $row['balance_after_transaction'] ?? null];
                continue;
            }
            if ($flag !== 'ACTUAL') {
                $conflicts[$account] = "unknown SCHEDULED_ACTUAL_FLAG '{$flag}'";
                continue;
            }
            $actualRows[] = $base + ['customer_id' => $customer ?: null, 'sub_account_no' => $subAccount ?: null,
                'transaction_date' => $row['transaction_date'] ?? null,
                'transaction_type' => trim((string) ($row['transaction_type'] ?? 'Other')) ?: 'Other',
                'principal_component' => (float) ($row['principal_component'] ?? 0),
                'interest_component' => (float) ($row['interest_component'] ?? 0),
                'fee_component' => (float) ($row['fee_component'] ?? 0), 'total_amount' => (float) ($row['total_amount'] ?? 0),
                'balance_after_transaction' => ($row['balance_after_transaction'] ?? '') === '' ? null : (float) $row['balance_after_transaction'],
                'row_note' => trim((string) ($row['row_note'] ?? '')) ?: null];
            if ((float) ($row['fee_component'] ?? 0) !== 0.0) {
                $feeRows[] = $base + ['fee_type' => 'other',
                    'description' => trim((string) ($row['transaction_type'] ?? 'Fee from Extract B')),
                    'amount' => (float) $row['fee_component'], 'transaction_date' => $row['transaction_date'] ?? null,
                    'gl_account_ref' => $reference ?: null];
            }
        }
        $actualLoaded = $this->insertActuals($actualRows);
        $scheduleResult = $this->remainingSchedules->import($scheduleRows);
        $feeResult = $this->fees->import($feeRows);
        return ['source_rows' => count($rows), 'scheduled_rows_routed' => count($scheduleRows),
            'actual_rows_loaded' => $actualLoaded, 'fee_rows_routed' => count($feeRows),
            'duplicate_source_rows' => $duplicates, 'held' => $held + $scheduleResult['held'],
            'skipped' => $conflicts + $scheduleResult['skipped'], 'loaded_contracts' => $scheduleResult['loaded_contracts'],
            'loaded_rows' => $scheduleResult['loaded_rows'], 'remaining_schedule_result' => $scheduleResult,
            'fee_result' => $feeResult, 'coverage' => $scheduleResult['coverage']];
    }
    private function insertActuals(array $rows): int
    {
        $loaded = 0;
        foreach ($rows as $row) {
            if (DB::table('eir_actual_transactions')->where('source_system', self::SOURCE)
                ->where('external_transaction_id', $row['external_transaction_id'])->exists()) continue;
            DB::table('eir_actual_transactions')->insert($row + ['created_at' => now(), 'updated_at' => now()]);
            $loaded++;
        }
        return $loaded;
    }
}

<?php

namespace App\Services\Eir;

use App\Services\AuditLoggerService;
use App\Services\Ebanker\LandingZoneReader;
use App\Services\Ebanker\LoanBookBuildService;
use Illuminate\Support\Facades\DB;

/**
 * The actual cash of every loan, from the E-Banker ledger already landed
 * (the P1 posting extract), for the EIR revenue engine.
 *
 * The engine takes a month's cash from eir_actual_transactions and falls back
 * to the contractual schedule only for a month no actual feed covers, labelled
 * DERIVED. MAIIC's transactions file (Extract B) was never delivered, so every
 * month fell back to the schedule: a loan repaid early kept "receiving" its
 * scheduled instalments and kept accruing EIR interest on a balance the
 * ledger shows repaid (system audit of 13 October 2026). The ledger holds the
 * same receipts, posting by posting; this service copies the cash movements
 * into the engine's table under their own source, so an imported Extract B
 * and the ledger never mix:
 *
 *   receipts (305, 306, 343, 900, 901)  Principal+Interest, the amount received
 *   write-off (300)                     Write-off
 *   settlement in kind (401)            Settlement in kind
 *   disbursement (301, 400)             Disbursement (cash advanced, never netted)
 *   interest charged (303, 120)         not cash: not copied
 *   any other type                      Other, which the engine reports as unclassified
 *
 * Each posting is copied once (its voucher id); re-running adds only new ones.
 */
class EirLedgerCashService
{
    public const SOURCE = 'EBANKER_LEDGER';

    public function __construct(private LandingZoneReader $zone)
    {
    }

    /** @return array{postings:int,loaded:int,accounts:int,by_type:array<string,int>,last_date:?string} */
    public function load(?string $toDate = null, ?int $userId = null): array
    {
        $toDate ??= $this->zone->lastLedgerDate();
        $existing = array_flip(DB::table('eir_actual_transactions')->where('source_system', self::SOURCE)->pluck('external_transaction_id')->all());
        $customers = DB::table('loan_books')->whereNotNull('customer_id')->orderByDesc('reporting_period')->pluck('customer_id', 'contract_id')->all();
        $batch = [];
        $byType = [];
        $postings = 0;
        $accounts = 0;
        foreach ($this->zone->ledgerByAccount($toDate) as $account => $rows) {
            $accounts++;
            $contract = ltrim((string) $account, '0');
            foreach ($rows as $r) {
                $p = $r['payload'];
                $type = (string) ($p['TRANTYPE'] ?? '');
                if (in_array($type, LoanBookBuildService::TYPE_INTEREST, true)) {
                    continue;
                }
                $postings++;
                $id = (string) ($p['CUMVOUCH_DET_ID'] ?? $r['source_key']);
                if (isset($existing[$id])) {
                    continue;
                }
                $amount = (float) str_replace(',', '', (string) ($p['TRANSAMT'] ?? 0));
                $kind = match (true) {
                    in_array($type, LoanBookBuildService::TYPE_RECEIPT, true) => 'Principal+Interest',
                    in_array($type, LoanBookBuildService::TYPE_WRITEOFF, true) => 'Write-off',
                    in_array($type, LoanBookBuildService::TYPE_SETTLEMENT_IN_KIND, true) => 'Settlement in kind',
                    in_array($type, LoanBookBuildService::TYPE_DISBURSEMENT, true) => 'Disbursement',
                    default => 'Other',
                };
                // a credit to the loan account is positive in the ledger: cash in, or the balance written down;
                // a receipt reversal (a debit on a receipt type) comes through negative and reduces the month's cash
                $total = in_array($kind, ['Write-off', 'Settlement in kind', 'Disbursement'], true) ? abs($amount) : $amount;
                $byType[$kind] = ($byType[$kind] ?? 0) + 1;
                $batch[] = ['contract_id' => $contract, 'customer_id' => $customers[$contract] ?? null, 'sub_account_no' => (string) ($p['SUB_ACCOUNT_NO'] ?? '') ?: null,
                    'transaction_date' => $r['row_date'], 'transaction_type' => $kind,
                    'principal_component' => 0, 'interest_component' => 0, 'fee_component' => 0, 'total_amount' => round($total, 2),
                    'balance_after_transaction' => null, 'source_system' => self::SOURCE, 'source_reference' => 'TRANTYPE ' . $type . ' ' . mb_substr((string) ($p['PARTICULARS'] ?? ''), 0, 120),
                    'external_transaction_id' => $id, 'row_note' => null, 'created_at' => now(), 'updated_at' => now()];
                $existing[$id] = true;
            }
        }
        foreach (array_chunk($batch, 500) as $chunk) {
            DB::table('eir_actual_transactions')->insert($chunk);
        }
        $result = ['postings' => $postings, 'loaded' => count($batch), 'accounts' => $accounts, 'by_type' => $byType, 'last_date' => $toDate];
        AuditLoggerService::log('EIR Ledger Cash Loaded', 'eir_actual_transactions', null, ['rows_affected' => count($batch), 'new_values' => $result, 'meta' => ['user' => $userId]]);

        return $result;
    }
}

<?php

namespace App\Console\Commands;

use App\Services\Eir\EirLedgerCashService;
use Illuminate\Console\Command;

/**
 * Copies the actual cash of every loan from the landed E-Banker ledger into
 * the EIR revenue engine's actual-cash table (see EirLedgerCashService).
 *
 *   php artisan eir:load-ledger-cash
 *   php artisan eir:load-ledger-cash --to=2026-08-31 --user=1
 */
class EirLoadLedgerCash extends Command
{
    protected $signature = 'eir:load-ledger-cash {--to= : Last posting date to read (default: the last loaded)} {--user=}';

    protected $description = 'Load the actual cash of every loan from the landed E-Banker ledger for the EIR revenue engine';

    public function handle(EirLedgerCashService $service): int
    {
        $r = $service->load($this->option('to') ?: null, $this->option('user') !== null ? (int) $this->option('user') : null);
        $this->info("Ledger to {$r['last_date']}: {$r['accounts']} loan accounts, {$r['postings']} cash postings read, {$r['loaded']} new rows loaded.");
        foreach ($r['by_type'] as $type => $n) {
            $this->line("  {$type}: {$n}");
        }

        return self::SUCCESS;
    }
}

                $opening = $previous ? (float) $previous->closing_gross : $this->initialOpening($contract, $period);
                $loan = $this->loanSnapshot($contractId, $period);
                if (! $loan) throw new RuntimeException("No loan-book snapshot exists for {$period}.");

                $stage = $this->stage($loan);
                if (! in_array($stage, [1, 2, 3], true)) throw new RuntimeException("The IFRS 9 stage for {$period} is missing or invalid.");
                $allowance = $this->openingAllowance($contractId, $period, $loan);
                $monthlyRate = pow(1 + (float) $contract->eir_effective_annual, 1 / 12) - 1;
                // Stage 3 accrues on the basis governed for this period
                // (stage3_interest_basis, IFRS 9 5.4.1(b) by default); a
                // performing loan always accrues on gross.
                $basis = $stage === 3 ? $this->governance->stage3InterestBasis($this->periodEnd($period)) : 'GROSS';
                $netOpening = max(0.0, $opening - $allowance);
                $interest = $monthlyRate * ($basis === 'NET' ? $netOpening : $opening);
                $unwind = $basis === 'NET' ? $monthlyRate * min($allowance, $opening) : 0.0;
                $cash = $this->cashReceived($contractId, $period);
                // a write-off or a settlement in kind leaves the gross without being cash
                $closing = max(0.0, $opening + $interest + $unwind - $cash['amount'] - $cash['derecognised']);

                $row = EirAmortisation::create([
                    'contract_id' => $contractId,
                    'reporting_period' => $period,
                    'opening_gross' => round($opening, 2),
                    'interest_accrued' => round($interest, 2),
                    'interest_basis' => $basis,
                    'unwind_amount' => round($unwind, 2),
                    'cash_received' => round($cash['amount'], 2),
                    'cash_source' => $cash['source'],
                    'modification_gain_loss' => round(-$cash['derecognised'], 2), // derecognition without cash, disclosed on the row
                    'closing_gross' => round($closing, 2),
                    'ecl_allowance' => round($allowance, 2),
                ]);

P = 'C:/xampp/htdocs/MAICC-IFRS9/app/Services/Eir/EirRevenueService.php'
s = open(P, encoding='utf-8').read()

def rep(a, b):
    global s
    assert a in s, a[:70]
    s = s.replace(a, b, 1)

rep(r"""        if ($pv <= 0) throw new RuntimeException("No remaining contractual cash flows exist after {$period}.");
        return $pv;
    }""", r"""        if ($pv <= 0) throw new RuntimeException("No remaining contractual cash flows exist after {$period}.");

        return $this->prepaidOpening($contract, $period, $pv);
    }

    /**
     * The first month's opening for a loan the borrower has prepaid (system
     * audit of 13 October 2026). The opening is the present value of the
     * remaining scheduled cash flows at the original EIR, which assumes every
     * instalment is still to come. When the borrower has repaid ahead of the
     * schedule, the schedule overstates what is owed: Barnet Agriculture
     * Resource Centre repaid MWK 55.6 million in November 2025 and the ledger
     * shows 0.4 million left, while the schedule's present value at December
     * was 38.8 million and the roll-forward accrued EIR interest on it. When
     * the ledger balance at the month before is less than half that present
     * value, the opening is the ledger balance (never below nil), and the
     * substitution is written to the audit log with both figures.
     */
    private function prepaidOpening(ContractEir $contract, string $period, float $pv): float
    {
        $priorEnd = CarbonImmutable::createFromFormat('Y-m-d', $period . '-01')->subDay()->toDateString();
        $account = DB::table('loan_books')->where('contract_id', $contract->contract_id)->whereNotNull('external_identity_id')
            ->where('external_identity_id', '!=', 'TBA')->value('external_identity_id') ?? str_pad((string) $contract->contract_id, 15, '0', STR_PAD_LEFT);
        try {
            $ledger = app(\App\Services\Ebanker\LandingZoneReader::class)->ledgerByAccount($priorEnd)[$account] ?? [];
        } catch (\Throwable) {
            return $pv;
        }
        if ($ledger === []) {
            return $pv;
        }
        $gross = -array_sum(array_map(fn ($p) => (float) str_replace(',', '', (string) ($p['payload']['TRANSAMT'] ?? 0)), $ledger));
        if ($gross >= 0.5 * $pv) {
            return $pv;
        }
        $opening = max(0.0, round($gross, 2));
        \App\Services\AuditLoggerService::log('EIR Opening From Ledger', 'eir_amortisation', null, ['reporting_period' => $period,
            'new_values' => ['contract_id' => $contract->contract_id, 'schedule_present_value' => round($pv, 2), 'ledger_balance' => round($gross, 2), 'opening' => $opening,
                'reason' => 'prepaid ahead of the schedule: the ledger balance at ' . $priorEnd . ' is below half the present value of the remaining schedule']]);

        return $opening;
    }""")
open(P, 'w', encoding='utf-8').write(s)
print('ok')

--- content ---
<?php

namespace App\Services;

use Illuminate\Support\Facades\DB;

/**
 * Links every loan in the loan book to its client (audit of 13 October 2026).
 *
 * The loan book carries the borrower's E-Banker customer number and name on
 * every loan, but no client record: the Clients screen held 82 borrowers
 * typed or imported by hand, and no loan pointed at any of them. This makes
 * one client per E-Banker customer number, by that number:
 *
 *  - a client that already has the number is kept as it is (its details are
 *    never overwritten by the loan book);
 *  - a customer with no client gets one, named as on its latest loan, typed
 *    corporate when the name says so (limited, SACCO, cooperative, trust,
 *    association, company, enterprises...), individual otherwise;
 *  - every loan then carries the client of its customer number.
 *
 * Idempotent: running it again adds only new customers and links only new
 * loans. A loan with no customer number is left unlinked and counted.
 */
class ClientLinkService
{
    private const CORPORATE = '/\b(limited|ltd|plc|sacco|co-?operative|coop|trust|association|company|enterprises?|group|holdings|farms?|investments?|industries|centre|center|school|church|clinic|hotel|lodge|ministry|council|club|union|foundation|services|trading|processors|resources)\b/i';

    /** @return array{customers:int,created:int,existing:int,loans_linked:int,loans_without_customer:int} */
    public function link(?int $userId = null): array
    {
        $customers = DB::table('loan_books')->whereNotNull('customer_id')->where('customer_id', '!=', '')
            ->selectRaw('customer_id, MAX(reporting_period) latest')->groupBy('customer_id')->get();
        $names = DB::table('loan_books as l')
            ->joinSub(DB::table('loan_books')->whereNotNull('customer_id')->selectRaw('customer_id, MAX(reporting_period) p')->groupBy('customer_id'), 'x', fn ($j) => $j->on('x.customer_id', '=', 'l.customer_id')->on('x.p', '=', 'l.reporting_period'))
            ->select('l.customer_id', 'l.customer_name', 'l.industry_type', 'l.industry_code')->get()->keyBy('customer_id');
        $known = DB::table('clients')->whereNotNull('customer_id')->whereNull('deleted_at')->pluck('id', 'customer_id')->all();

        $created = 0;
        $batch = [];
        foreach ($customers as $c) {
            $id = trim((string) $c->customer_id);
            if (isset($known[$id])) {
                continue;
            }
            $row = $names[$c->customer_id] ?? null;
            $name = trim((string) ($row->customer_name ?? '')) ?: 'Customer ' . $id;
            $batch[] = ['customer_id' => $id, 'name' => mb_substr($name, 0, 199), 'type' => preg_match(self::CORPORATE, $name) ? 'corporate' : 'individual',
                'industry_type' => $row->industry_type ?? null, 'industry_code' => $row->industry_code ?? null, 'is_active' => 1, 'status' => 'active',
                'description' => 'Created from the loan book (E-Banker customer ' . $id . ')', 'created_by_id' => $userId, 'created_at' => now(), 'updated_at' => now()];
            $created++;
        }
        foreach (array_chunk($batch, 500) as $chunk) {
            DB::table('clients')->insert($chunk);
        }

        // every loan carries the client of its customer number
        $linked = DB::update('UPDATE loan_books l JOIN clients c ON c.customer_id = l.customer_id AND c.deleted_at IS NULL SET l.client_id = c.id WHERE l.client_id IS NULL OR l.client_id <> c.id');
        $without = DB::table('loan_books')->where(fn ($q) => $q->whereNull('customer_id')->orWhere('customer_id', ''))->count();
        $result = ['customers' => $customers->count(), 'created' => $created, 'existing' => $customers->count() - $created, 'loans_linked' => $linked, 'loans_without_customer' => $without];
        AuditLoggerService::log('Clients Linked To Loan Book', 'clients', null, ['rows_affected' => $created + $linked, 'new_values' => $result, 'meta' => ['user' => $userId]]);

        return $result;
    }
}

````

<?php

namespace App\Console\Commands;

use App\Services\ClientLinkService;
use Illuminate\Console\Command;

/**
 * One client per E-Banker customer number, and every loan linked to it
 * (see ClientLinkService).
 *
 *   php artisan clients:link-loan-book --user=1
 */
class ClientsLinkLoanBook extends Command
{
    protected $signature = 'clients:link-loan-book {--user=}';

    protected $description = 'Create a client for every loan-book customer and link every loan to its client';

    public function handle(ClientLinkService $service): int
    {
        $r = $service->link($this->option('user') !== null ? (int) $this->option('user') : null);
        $this->info("{$r['customers']} customers in the loan book: {$r['created']} new clients, {$r['existing']} already held; {$r['loans_linked']} loans linked; {$r['loans_without_customer']} loans have no customer number.");

        return self::SUCCESS;
    }
}

import re

def kind_all(p, kind):
    s = open(P + p, encoding='utf-8').read()
    n = 0
    # add the kind to every Import::create([ ... 'status' => 'pending', of this file
    def add(m):
        nonlocal n
        n += 1
        return m.group(0) + "\n" + m.group(1) + "'kind' => '" + kind + "',"
    s2 = re.sub(r"Import::create\(\[\n(\s+)", lambda m: "Import::create([\n" + m.group(1) + "'kind' => '" + kind + "',\n" + m.group(1), s)
    n = s2.count("'kind' => '" + kind + "'") - s.count("'kind' => '" + kind + "'")
    open(P + p, 'w', encoding='utf-8').write(s2)
    print(p, n)

    public function exportECL(Request $request)
        {
            $exportable = [
                'contract_id',
                'carrying_amount',
                'pd_value',
                'lgd_value',
                'ecl_value',
                'ifrs9stage_pre_qualitative',

                'reporting_period',
                'customer_name',

                'remaining_tenor',
                'industry_code',

                'allocated_discounted_value',
                'commitments',
                'collection_lgd',
                'customer_lgd',
                'pd_prefli',
                'pd_post_fli',
                'fli_adj',

            ];

            // Validate request
            $validated = $request->validate([
                'portfolios' => 'required|exists:loan_portfolios,id',
                'reporting_period' => 'required|date',
                'mode' => 'required|in:summary,totalLoanBook',
                'columns' => 'nullable|array',
                'columns.*' => 'string|in:' . implode(',', $exportable),
            ]);

            $portfolioId = $validated['portfolios'];
            $period = Carbon::parse($validated['reporting_period'])->format('Y-m');
            $mode = $validated['mode'];
            $columns = $validated['columns'] ?? [];

            $filename = 'ecl_report_' . $period . '_' . $mode . '.csv';

            if ($mode === 'summary') {
                $data = DB::table('loan_books')
                    ->selectRaw('

                        AVG(lgd_value_used) as avg_lgd,

                    ')
                    ->where('loan_portfolio_id', $portfolioId)
                    ->where('reporting_period', $period)
                    ->groupByRaw('COALESCE(ifrs9stage_post_qualitative, calculated_ifrs9_stage, ifrs9stage_pre_qualitative)')
                    ->get();

                fputcsv($handle, ['Stage', 'Total EAD', 'PD', 'LGD', 'Total ECL']);

                $totalEAD = 0;
                $totalPD = 0;
                $totalLGD = 0;
                $totalECL = 0;
                $count = 0;

                foreach ($data as $row) {
                    fputcsv($handle, [
                        $row->stage,
                        $row->total_ead,
                        $row->avg_pd,
                        $row->avg_lgd,
                        $row->total_ecl,
                    ]);

                    $totalEAD += $row->total_ead;
                    $totalPD += $row->avg_pd;
                    $totalLGD += $row->avg_lgd;
    }

    public function macroScenarioPart(Request $request)
    {
        $period = $this->period($request);

        $macro = [];
        foreach (['macro_economic_variables', 'macro_economic_data', 'macroeconomic_variables', 'macro_variables'] as $tbl) {
            if (Schema::hasTable($tbl)) {
                try {
                    $macro = DB::table($tbl)->orderByDesc('id')->limit(40)->get()
                        ->map(fn ($r) => [$r->name ?? $r->variable ?? '-',
                            $r->period ?? $r->reporting_period ?? '-',
                            isset($r->value) ? $this->num($r->value, 4) : '-'])->all();
                } catch (\Throwable $e) {
                    $macro = [];
                }
                break;
            }
        }
        if (empty($macro)) {
            $macro = [['No macro-economic variables table found for this install', '-', '-']];
        }

        $scenarios = [];
        if (Schema::hasTable('scenario_sets')) {
            $scenarios = DB::table('scenario_sets')
                ->leftJoin('scenario_probabilities as sp', 'sp.scenario_set_id', '=', 'scenario_sets.id')
                ->selectRaw('scenario_sets.name set_name, sp.scenario_name, sp.probability')
                ->orderBy('scenario_sets.id')->get()
                ->map(fn ($r) => [$r->set_name, $r->scenario_name ?? '-',
                    $this->pct(($r->probability ?? 0) / 100)])->all();
        }

        return $this->respond(['key' => 'macro-scenario', 'period' => $period,
            'subtitle' => 'Forward-looking macro assumptions and economic scenarios',
            'kpis' => $this->totalsKpis($period),
            'sections' => [
                ['heading' => 'Macro-Economic Assumptions',
                 'columns' => ['Variable', 'Period', 'Value'], 'align' => ['l', 'l', 'r'], 'rows' => $macro],
                ['heading' => 'Economic Scenarios & Weights',
                 'columns' => ['Scenario Set', 'Scenario', 'Probability'], 'align' => ['l', 'l', 'r'],
                 'rows' => $scenarios ?: [['No scenario sets defined', '-', '-']]],
            ]]);
    }

    public function scenarioEcl(Request $request)
    {
        $period = $this->period($request);
        $sets = [];
        if (Schema::hasTable('scenario_sets')) {
            $sets = DB::table('scenario_sets')
                ->leftJoin('scenario_probabilities as sp', 'sp.scenario_set_id', '=', 'scenario_sets.id')
                ->selectRaw('scenario_sets.name, sp.scenario_name, sp.probability')
                ->orderBy('scenario_sets.id')->get()
                ->map(fn ($r) => [$r->name, $r->scenario_name ?? '-', $this->pct(($r->probability ?? 0) / 100)])->all();
        }

        $fli = DB::table('loan_books')->where('reporting_period', $period)
            ->selectRaw("SUM(COALESCE(ecl_value,0)) ecl, AVG(COALESCE(fli_adj,0)) fli")->first();

        return $this->respond(['key' => 'scenario-ecl', 'period' => $period,
            'subtitle' => 'Probability-weighted forward-looking scenarios',
            'kpis' => [
                ['label' => 'Probability-Weighted ECL', 'value' => $this->money($fli->ecl ?? 0), 'tone' => 'rose'],
                ['label' => 'Avg FLI Adjustment', 'value' => $this->num($fli->fli ?? 0, 6), 'tone' => 'amber'],
            ],
            'sections' => [[
                'heading' => 'Scenario Sets & Weights',
                'columns' => ['Scenario Set', 'Scenario', 'Probability'],
                'align' => ['l', 'l', 'r'],
                'rows' => $sets ?: [['No scenario sets defined', '-', '-']],
            ]]]);
    }

    private function period(Request $request): ?string

    /** The FLI month-end close of the month that stands (recorded or signed off), or null. */
    private function fliSnapshot(?string $period): ?object
    {
        if (! $period || ! Schema::hasTable('fli_run_snapshots')) {
            return null;
        }

        return DB::table('fli_run_snapshots')->where('reporting_period', $period)->whereIn('status', ['RECORDED', 'SIGNED_OFF'])->orderByDesc('id')->first();
    }

    /** The scenario set the close used, else the approved set of the month. */
    private function fliSet(?string $period, ?object $snap): ?object
    {
        if (! $period || ! Schema::hasTable('governed_scenario_sets')) {
            return null;
        }
        if ($snap && $snap->set_id) {
            return DB::table('governed_scenario_sets')->where('id', $snap->set_id)->first();
        }

        return DB::table('governed_scenario_sets')->where('reporting_period', $period)->whereIn('status', ['APPROVED', 'LOCKED'])->orderByDesc('version')->first();
    }

    public function eclPart(Request $request)
    {
        $period = $this->period($request);

        $rows = DB::table('expected_credit_loss')
            ->where('reporting_period', $period)
            ->orderBy('ecl_calculation_level')->orderBy('ifrs9_stage')
            ->get()
            ->map(fn ($r) => [
                ucfirst($r->ecl_calculation_level ?? '-'),
                'Stage ' . $r->ifrs9_stage,
                number_format($r->total_loans),
                $this->money($r->total_ead),
                $this->num($r->pd_value_used, 6),
                $this->num($r->lgd_value_used, 6),
                $this->money($r->total_ecl),
                $this->pct((float) $r->total_ead != 0.0 ? $r->total_ecl / $r->total_ead : 0),
            ])->all();

        return $this->respond(['key' => 'ecl', 'period' => $period,
            'kpis' => $this->totalsKpis($period),
            'sections' => [[
                'heading' => 'Expected Credit Loss by Stage',
                'columns' => ['Level', 'Stage', 'Loans', 'EAD', 'Avg PD', 'Avg LGD', 'ECL', 'Coverage %'],
                'align' => ['l', 'l', 'r', 'r', 'r', 'r', 'r', 'r'],
                'rows' => $rows,
            ]]]);
    }

    public function accountEcl(Request $request)
    {
        $period = $this->period($request);
        $rows = DB::table('loan_books')
            ->selectRaw("contract_id, customer_name, ifrs9stage_post_qualitative stage,
                " . self::EAD_SQL . " ead, COALESCE(pd_post_fli,pd_prefli) pd,
                COALESCE(lgd_value,0) lgd, COALESCE(ecl_value,0) ecl")
            ->where('reporting_period', $period)
            ->orderByDesc(DB::raw(self::EAD_SQL))->limit(200)->get()
            ->map(fn ($r) => [$r->contract_id, $r->customer_name ?: '(Unnamed)', 'Stage ' . $r->stage,
                $this->money($r->ead), $this->num($r->pd, 6), $this->num($r->lgd, 6),
                $this->money($r->ead * $r->pd * $r->lgd), $this->money($r->ecl)])->all();

        return $this->respond(['key' => 'account-ecl', 'period' => $period,
            'subtitle' => 'Loan-by-loan ECL = EAD x PD x LGD (top 200 by exposure)',
            'kpis' => $this->totalsKpis($period),
            'sections' => [[
                'heading' => 'Account-Level ECL Calculation Trail',
                'columns' => ['Contract', 'Client', 'Stage', 'EAD', 'PD', 'LGD', 'EAD x PD x LGD', 'Booked ECL'],
                'align' => ['l', 'l', 'l', 'r', 'r', 'r', 'r', 'r'],
                'rows' => $rows,
            ]]]);
    }

**Result of Bash**

````
    private function rbmBuild(string $period): array
    {
        $raw = DB::table('loan_books')->where('reporting_period', $period)
            ->selectRaw($this->rbmClassCase() . " rbm, COUNT(*) n, SUM(" . self::EAD_SQL . ") ead,
                SUM(COALESCE(ecl_value,0)) ecl")
            ->groupBy('rbm')->get()->keyBy('rbm');

        $rows = [];
        $totProv = 0;
        $totEcl  = 0;
        $nplEad  = 0;
        $totEad  = 0;
        foreach (self::RBM as $class => $def) {
            $r    = $raw->get($class);
            $n    = (int) ($r->n ?? 0);
            $ead  = (float) ($r->ead ?? 0);
            $ecl  = (float) ($r->ecl ?? 0);
            $prov = $ead * $def['rate'];
            $totProv += $prov;
            $totEcl  += $ecl;
            $totEad  += $ead;
            if (in_array($class, ['Substandard', 'Doubtful', 'Loss'], true)) {
                $nplEad += $ead;
            }
            $rows[] = [$class, number_format($n), $this->money($ead),
                $this->pct($def['rate']), $this->money($prov), $this->money($ecl),
                $this->money($ecl - $prov)];
        }

        return [
            'subtitle' => 'Prudential classification by days past due under the directive\'s bands by term: 30/90/180/365 days for a facility of 12 months or less, 90/180/365/746 otherwise (RBM Credit Risk Management for DFIs Directive, 2018, section 10 and the Schedule); the same bands and rates as the RBM Return',
            'kpis' => [
                ['label' => 'NPL Ratio (substandard and below)', 'value' => $this->pct($totEad ? $nplEad / $totEad : 0), 'tone' => 'rose'],
                ['label' => 'RBM Provision', 'value' => $this->money($totProv), 'tone' => 'amber'],
                ['label' => 'IFRS 9 ECL', 'value' => $this->money($totEcl), 'tone' => 'rose'],
                ['label' => 'ECL − RBM', 'value' => $this->money($totEcl - $totProv), 'tone' => ($totEcl - $totProv) >= 0 ? 'emerald' : 'rose'],
            ],
            'sections' => [[
                'heading' => 'RBM Asset Classification (by days past due and term of facility)',
                'columns' => ['RBM Class', 'Loans', 'Exposure (EAD)', 'Minimum Rate', 'RBM Provision', 'IFRS 9 ECL', 'ECL − RBM'],
                'align' => ['l', 'r', 'r', 'r', 'r', 'r', 'r'],
                'rows' => $rows,
            ]],
        ];
    }

    private function previousPeriod(?string $period): ?string
    {
        $periods = $this->periods();
        $i = array_search($period, $periods, true);
        return ($i !== false && isset($periods[$i + 1])) ? $periods[$i + 1] : null;
    }

    private function periodTotals(?string $period)
    {
        return DB::table('loan_books')
            ->selectRaw("COUNT(*) loans, SUM(" . self::EAD_SQL . ") ead, SUM(COALESCE(ecl_value,0)) ecl")
            ->where('reporting_period', $period)
            ->first();
    }

// Fetch available tables when component is mounted
const fetchTables = async () => {
  try {
    const response = await axios.get('/api/transition-profiles/tables');
    tables.value = response.data.tables;
  } catch (error) {
    console.error('Error fetching tables:', error);
  }
};

// Fetch columns for start and end tables
const fetchStartTableColumns = async () => {
  if (!form.start_table) return;
  try {
    const response = await axios.get(`/api/transition-profiles/columns/${form.start_table}`);
    startTableColumns.value = response.data;
  } catch (error) {
    console.error('Error fetching start table columns:', error);
  }
};

const fetchEndTableColumns = async () => {
  if (!form.end_table) return;
  try {
    const response = await axios.get(`/api/transition-profiles/columns/${form.end_table}`);
    endTableColumns.value = response.data;
  } catch (error) {
    console.error('Error fetching end table columns:', error);
  }
};
