<?php

namespace App\Http\Controllers;
use App\Models\InternalGradeProfile;
use App\Models\InternalGradeMapping;
use App\Models\LoanBook;
use App\Models\LoanPortfolio;
use App\Models\IndustryType;
use App\Models\ReportingPeriods;
use Carbon\Carbon;
use App\Models\GradeTenorPd;
use App\Services\AuditLoggerService;
use Illuminate\Validation\Rule;
use Illuminate\Support\Facades\DB;
use Illuminate\Support\Facades\Log;
use Inertia\Inertia;
use Illuminate\Http\Request;

class InternalGradingController extends Controller
{
    /**
     * List grades for a profile
     */
   public function profiles()
    {
        return Inertia::render('InternalGrading/Index', [
            'profiles' => InternalGradeProfile::withCount('mappings')
                ->orderBy('name')
                ->get(),
            'portfolios' => LoanPortfolio::select('id', 'name')->orderBy('name')->get(),
            'sectors' => IndustryType::select('code', 'name')->orderBy('name')->get(),
        ]);
    }

    /**
     * List grades for a profile
     */
    public function index(InternalGradeProfile $profile)
    {
        return Inertia::render('InternalGrading/Grades', [
            'profile' => $profile,
            'grades' => $profile->mappings()
                ->with('tenorPds')
                ->orderBy('grade_code')
                ->get(),

        ]);
    }
    /**
     * Create a new grading profile
     */
    public function storeProfile(Request $request)
    {
        $validated = $request->validate([
            'name'         => 'required|string|max:255',
            'description'  => 'nullable|string',
            'max_tenor_years' => 'required|integer|min:1',
        ]);

        InternalGradeProfile::create($validated);

        return back()->with('success', 'Profile created successfully');
    }

    /**
     * Store a grade + PD curve
     */
    public function storeGrade(Request $request, InternalGradeProfile $profile)
    {
        $request->validate([
            'grade_code' => [
                'required',
                'string',
                Rule::unique('internal_grade_mappings')
                    ->where('profile_id', $profile->id),
            ],
            'grade_name'  => 'required|string|max:255',
            'sp_rating'   => 'nullable|string|max:50',
            'rbm_class'   => 'nullable|string|max:50',
            'lower_bound' => 'nullable|numeric',
            'upper_bound' => 'nullable|numeric',

            'tenor_pds' => 'required|array',
            'tenor_pds.*.tenor_years'     => 'required|integer',
            'tenor_pds.*.pd_probability'  => 'required|numeric|min:0',
        ]);

        DB::transaction(function () use ($request, $profile) {

            $mapping = $profile->mappings()->create(
                $request->only([
                    'grade_name',
                    'grade_code',
                    'sp_rating',
                    'rbm_class',
                    'lower_bound',
                    'upper_bound',
                ])
            );

            $mapping->tenorPds()->createMany(
                collect($request->tenor_pds)->map(fn ($pd) => [
                    'tenor_years'    => $pd['tenor_years'],
                    'pd_probability' => $pd['pd_probability'],
                ])->toArray()
            );
        });

        return redirect()
            ->route('internal-grading.grades', $profile)
            ->with('success', 'Grade and PD curve saved successfully');
    }



    public function updateGrade( Request $request, InternalGradeProfile $profile, InternalGradeMapping $grade)
     {
        // Safety: grade must belong to profile
        abort_unless($grade->profile_id === $profile->id, 403);

        $validated = $request->validate([
            'grade_code' => [
                'required',
                'string',
                Rule::unique('internal_grade_mappings')
                    ->where('profile_id', $profile->id)
                    ->ignore($grade->id),
            ],
            'grade_name'  => 'required|string|max:255',
            'sp_rating'   => 'nullable|string|max:50',
            'rbm_class'   => 'nullable|string|max:50',
            'lower_bound' => 'nullable|numeric',
            'upper_bound' => 'nullable|numeric',

            'tenor_pds' => 'required|array|min:1',
            'tenor_pds.*.tenor_years'    => 'required|integer|min:1',
            'tenor_pds.*.pd_probability' => 'required|numeric|min:0|max:1',
        ]);

        DB::transaction(function () use ($validated, $grade) {

            // 1️⃣ Update grade metadata
            $grade->update(collect($validated)->except('tenor_pds')->toArray());

            // 2️⃣ Sync PD term structure
            $existing = $grade->tenorPds()->get()->keyBy('tenor_years');

            foreach ($validated['tenor_pds'] as $pd) {
                $existingPd = $existing->get($pd['tenor_years']);

                if ($existingPd) {
                    $existingPd->update([
                        'pd_probability' => $pd['pd_probability'],
                    ]);
                } else {
                    $grade->tenorPds()->create($pd);
                }
            }

            // 3️⃣ Remove PDs beyond profile max tenor (optional safety)
            $grade->tenorPds()
                ->where('tenor_years', '>', $grade->profile->max_tenor_years)
                ->delete();
        });

        return back()->with('success', 'Grade updated successfully');
    }

        public function toggle(InternalGradeProfile $profile)
        {
            DB::transaction(function () use ($profile) {

                if (! $profile->is_active) {
                    InternalGradeProfile::where('is_active', true)
                        ->update(['is_active' => false]);
                }

                $profile->update([
                    'is_active' => ! $profile->is_active
                ]);
            });

            return back();
        }


});


    Route::middleware(['auth', 'verified'])->group(function () {

        // Profiles
        Route::get('/internal-grading', [InternalGradingController::class, 'profiles'])
            ->name('internal-grading.profiles');

        Route::post('/internal-grading/profile', [InternalGradingController::class, 'storeProfile'])
            ->name('internal-grading.profile.store');

        // Grades + PD Curves per profile
        Route::get('/internal-grading/{profile}', [InternalGradingController::class, 'index'])

        Route::post('/internal-grading/{profile}/grade', [InternalGradingController::class, 'storeGrade'])
            ->name('internal-grading.grade.store');
        
        Route::put('/internal-grading/{profile}/grade/{grade}', [InternalGradingController::class, 'updateGrade'])
            ->name('internal-grading.grade.update');

        
        Route::get( '/internal-grading/{profile}/matrix', [InternalGradingController::class, 'matrix'])
            ->name('internal-grading.matrix.view');

        Route::post( '/internal-grading/loanbook/update-with-pd', [InternalGradingController::class, 'updateLoanBookWithPD'])
            ->name('internal-grading.loanbook.updateWithPD');
        });

````
<?php
namespace App\Http\Controllers;

use Illuminate\Http\Request;
use Illuminate\Support\Facades\DB;
use Inertia\Inertia;

class EclProjectionController extends Controller
{
    public function __construct(){ $this->middleware('auth'); }
    public function index(Request $request)
    {
        $runId=$request->input('run_id') ?: DB::table('ecl_projection_runs')->where('status','COMPLETED')->latest('id')->value('run_id');
        $search=trim((string)$request->input('search'));$scenario=trim((string)$request->input('scenario'));
        $run=$runId?DB::table('ecl_projection_runs')->where('run_id',$runId)->first():null;
        $rows=DB::table('ecl_cashflow_projections')->when($runId,fn($q)=>$q->where('run_id',$runId))
            ->when($search!=='',fn($q)=>$q->where('contract_id','like',"%{$search}%"))
            ->when($scenario!=='',fn($q)=>$q->where('scenario_code',$scenario))
            ->orderBy('contract_id')->orderBy('scenario_code')->orderBy('period_index')->paginate(15)->withQueryString();
        $contracts=$runId?DB::table('ecl_cashflow_projections')->where('run_id',$runId)->select('contract_id','ifrs9_stage')
            ->selectRaw('SUM(weighted_discounted_shortfall) weighted_ecl, SUM(undiscounted_shortfall * scenario_weight) undiscounted_ecl, MAX(discount_exponent) horizon')
            ->groupBy('contract_id','ifrs9_stage')->orderBy('contract_id')->get():collect();
        return Inertia::render('ExpectedCreditLoss/Projections',['run'=>$run,'rows'=>$rows,'contracts'=>$contracts,
            'runs'=>DB::table('ecl_projection_runs')->where('status','COMPLETED')->latest('id')->limit(20)->get(),
            'scenarios'=>DB::table('ecl_scenario_assumptions')->where('status','APPROVED')->orderByDesc('weight')->get(),
            'filters'=>['run_id'=>$runId,'search'=>$search,'scenario'=>$scenario]]);
    }
}

````
    public function store(Request $request)
    {
        $request->validate([
            'start_date' => ['required'],
        ]);
        $financialPeriod = new FinancialPeriod();
        $financialPeriod->created_by_id = Auth::id();
        $financialPeriod->name = $request->name;
        $financialPeriod->start_date = $request->start_date;
        $financialPeriod->end_date = $request->end_date;
        $financialPeriod->description = $request->description;
        $financialPeriod->save();
        FinancialPeriod::where('id', '!=', $financialPeriod->id)
            ->where('closed', 0)
            ->update([
                'closed_by_id' => Auth::id(),
                'closed' => 1,
            ]);
        activity()
            ->performedOn($financialPeriod)
            ->log('Create  Financial Period');
        return redirect()->route('accounting.financial_periods.index')->with('success', 'Financial Period successfully.');

    }

    public function show(FinancialPeriod $financialPeriod)
    {

    public function show(TransitionMatrix $matrix)
    {
        // Load the profile (which is actually a loan product) with its scoring attributes

        // Get states from loan product's configured category names

            ->map(function ($attribute) {

                    'id' => $attribute->id,

                ];

        // Get all portfolio groups from ScoringAttributeGroup
        $portfolioGroups = \App\Models\ScoringAttributeGroup::select('id', 'name', 'system_name', 'name', 'description')
            ->orderBy('name')
            ->get();

        return Inertia::render('TransitionMatrix/Show', [
            'matrix' => $matrix->load('transitionProfile', 'entries'),
            'portfolioGroups' => $portfolioGroups,
            'states' => $states
        ]);
    }

        if (!$matrix->external_file_path || !Storage::disk('public')->exists($matrix->external_file_path)) {

        return Storage::disk('public')->download($matrix->external_file_path);
    }

 * Header rows only: no example figures, so nothing in a sample can be

<script>
import AppLayout from '@/Layouts/AppLayout.vue'
import pickBy from 'lodash/pickBy'

export default {
    components: { AppLayout },
    props: {
        entries: Array,
        filters: Object,
        pagination: Object,
        users: Array,
        counts: Object,
    },
    data() {
        return {
            form: {
                search: this.filters.search,
                source: this.filters.source,
                user_id: this.filters.user_id,
                from: this.filters.from,
                to: this.filters.to,
            },
            expanded: null,
        }
    },
    watch: {
        form: {
            handler: _.debounce(function () {
                this.go(1)
            }, 450),
            deep: true,
        },
    },
    computed: {
        hasFilters() {
            return Object.values(this.form).some(v => v !== null && v !== '' && v !== undefined)
        },
        // Page numbers around the current page, with the first and last.
        pageWindow() {
            const cur = this.pagination.current_page, last = this.pagination.last_page
            const pages = []
            for (let n = 1; n <= last; n++) {
                if (n === 1 || n === last || Math.abs(n - cur) <= 2) pages.push(n)
                else if (pages[pages.length - 1] !== '...') pages.push('...')
            }
            return pages
        },
    },
    methods: {
        go(page) {
            this.expanded = null
            const query = pickBy({ ...this.form, page: page > 1 ? page : null },
                (v) => v !== null && v !== '' && v !== undefined)
            this.$inertia.get(this.route('audit-trail.index'), query, { preserveState: true, replace: true })
        },
        clear() {
            this.form = { search: null, source: null, user_id: null, from: null, to: null }
        },
        humanise(v) {
            if (!v) return ''
            const t = String(v).replace(/_/g, ' ')
            return t.charAt(0).toUpperCase() + t.slice(1)
        },
        formatDateTime(value) {
            if (!value) return ''
            return new Date(value).toLocaleString('en-GB', { year: 'numeric', month: 'short', day: 'numeric', hour: '2-digit', minute: '2-digit' })
        },
        cleanDetails(details) {
            if (!details || typeof details !== 'object') return {}
            // Drop empty members so only substance is shown.
            return Object.fromEntries(Object.entries(details).filter(([, v]) => v !== null && v !== undefined))
        },
    },
}
</script>

<script setup>
import { reactive, computed } from 'vue';
import { router } from '@inertiajs/vue3';
import AppLayout from '@/Layouts/AppLayout.vue';
import BackToReports from './Partials/BackToReports.vue';
import DownloadButton from './Partials/DownloadButton.vue';
import KpiRow from './Partials/KpiRow.vue';
import ReportIcon from './Partials/ReportIcon.vue';

const props = defineProps({
    report: { type: Object, default: null },
    error: { type: String, default: null },
    portfolios: { type: Array, default: () => [] },
    periods: { type: Array, default: () => [] },
    selectedPortfolio: { default: '' },
    selectedStartPeriod: { default: '' },
    selectedEndPeriod: { default: '' },
});

const form = reactive({
    portfolio_id: props.selectedPortfolio || (props.portfolios.length === 1 ? props.portfolios[0].value : ''),
    start_period: props.selectedStartPeriod || '',
    end_period: props.selectedEndPeriod || '',
});

const canRun = computed(() => form.portfolio_id && form.start_period && form.end_period && form.start_period < form.end_period);

const reload = (extra = {}) => router.get(route('reports.loan-book-reconciliation'), { ...form, ...extra }, { preserveScroll: true });
const onPortfolioChange = () => { form.start_period = ''; form.end_period = ''; reload(); };

const downloadUrl = (kind) => props.report
    ? route('reports.loan-book-reconciliation', { portfolio_id: props.selectedPortfolio, start_period: props.selectedStartPeriod, end_period: props.selectedEndPeriod, download: kind })
    : '';

const money = (v) => {
    const n = Number(v || 0);
    const t = Math.abs(n).toLocaleString('en-GB', { minimumFractionDigits: 2, maximumFractionDigits: 2 });
    return n < 0 ? '(' + t + ')' : t;
};
const line = (key) => (props.report?.lines || []).find(l => l.key === key) || { amount: 0, loans: 0 };
const figures = computed(() => props.report ? [
    { label: 'Opening loan book', value: money(line('opening').amount), sub: line('opening').loans + ' loans' },
    { label: 'New loans', value: money(line('new').amount), sub: line('new').loans + ' loans' },
    { label: 'Closing loan book', value: money(line('closing').amount), sub: line('closing').loans + ' loans' },
    { label: 'Difference', value: money(line('variance').amount), tone: props.report.ties ? 'maiic' : 'rose' },
] : []);
</script>

<script setup>
// In-page tabs in the system's tab style (as on EIR Data): green text and
// underline on the active tab, a count chip on each tab (green when active,
// grey otherwise). Sits at the top of a white panel, below the page header.
defineProps({
    tabs: { type: Array, default: () => [] }, // [{ key, label, count? }]
    modelValue: { type: String, default: '' },
})
const emit = defineEmits(['update:modelValue'])
const fmt = (n) => Number(n || 0).toLocaleString()
</script>

<template>
    <div class="border-b border-gray-200 px-5 pt-4">
        <nav class="flex gap-6 overflow-x-auto" role="tablist">
            <button v-for="tab in tabs" :key="tab.key" type="button" role="tab"
                    :aria-selected="modelValue === tab.key"
                    class="whitespace-nowrap border-b-2 px-1 pb-3 text-sm font-semibold"
                    :class="modelValue === tab.key ? 'border-maiic-600 text-maiic-700' : 'border-transparent text-gray-500 hover:text-gray-800'"
                    @click="emit('update:modelValue', tab.key)">
                {{ tab.label }}
                <span v-if="tab.count !== undefined && tab.count !== null"
                      class="ml-1 rounded-full px-2 py-0.5 text-xs"
                      :class="modelValue === tab.key ? 'bg-maiic-100 text-maiic-700' : 'bg-gray-100 text-gray-600'">{{ fmt(tab.count) }}</span>
            </button>
        </nav>
    </div>
</template>

**Result of Bash**

````
    public function portfolioTrend(Request $request)
    {
        $period = $this->period($request);

        // Last 12 periods up to the selected one, per portfolio, from the ECL store.
        $periods = collect($this->periods())->filter(fn ($p) => $p <= $period)
            ->take(12)->values()->reverse()->values();

        $rowsRaw = DB::table('expected_credit_loss as e')
            ->leftJoin('loan_portfolios as p', 'p.id', 'e.ecl_calculation_id')
            ->where('e.ecl_calculation_level', 'portfolio')
            ->whereIn('e.reporting_period', $periods)
            ->groupBy('e.reporting_period', 'p.name')
            ->selectRaw("e.reporting_period rp, COALESCE(p.name,'Unmapped') name, SUM(e.total_ecl) ecl")
            ->get();

        $portNames = $rowsRaw->pluck('name')->unique()->sort()->values();
        $pivot = [];
        foreach ($rowsRaw as $r) {
            $pivot[$r->rp][$r->name] = (float) $r->ecl;
        }

        $rows = [];
        foreach ($periods as $p) {
            $line = [$p];
            $tot = 0;
            foreach ($portNames as $n) {
                $val = $pivot[$p][$n] ?? 0;
                $tot += $val;
                $line[] = $this->money($val);
            }
            $line[] = $this->money($tot);
            $rows[] = $line;
        }

        return $this->respond(['key' => 'portfolio-trend', 'period' => $period,
            'subtitle' => 'Total ECL by portfolio over the last ' . count($periods) . ' periods',
            'kpis' => $this->totalsKpis($period),
            'sections' => [[
                'heading' => 'ECL by Portfolio over Time',
                'columns' => array_merge(['Period'], $portNames->all(), ['Total']),
                'align' => array_merge(['l'], array_fill(0, $portNames->count() + 1, 'r')),
                'rows' => $rows,
            ]]]);
    }

Each is a two-person control.</li><li><b>Evidence.</b> The audit trail, the support ticket record and the documentation, which together are what an auditor examines when they ask how a figure was controlled.</li></ul><h4>What you are not accountable for</h4><p>The platform is a calculation and reporting tool. Reports, model setup and administration: fixes from the second UI audit

Reports
- Forward-looking report reads what the ECL used: the macro data the bridge held for the month, the governed scenario set with its weights and shocks, and the FLI close (ECL per scenario, weighted against booked, sign-off status). Each month now shows its own figures.

- Financial periods validate name, dates and end after start; the success message is complete; the blank show page leads to edit.

## CLAUDE  (2026-10-13 11:53:33 UTC)

I've fixed the second audit's findings on reports, model setup and administration. They're committed as `8c8af93` and pushed to `eir_revenue_recognition`. The EIR, FLI, navigation and report download tests all pass (319). I clicked through the changed screens at 1440 px, and all writes went to `maiic_ifrs9_demo` only.

**Reports**
- **Forward-looking report:** it now shows what the August ECL actually used: the macro data held for the month, the approved scenario set with its weights and shocks, and the per-scenario ECL. Booked is 11,314,579,806.97 against weighted 11,314,579,806.37 (difference -0.60). A month with no FLI close says so instead of showing old figures.
- **ECL by stage:** each row now names its portfolio, and PD and LGD show as percentages in every report. Average LGDs used to count missing values as zero, which understated them. They now average only the loans that have an LGD and show "-" when none do.
- **RBM:** the classification screen now uses the gross balance, like the RBM Return, so both show NPL 31.98% and minimum provision 3,246,015,569.35.
- **Portfolio trend:** the empty 2023-12 row is gone. It came from three old sector-level test rows with no loans behind them.
- **Wide pages:** tables and report tabs now fit the panel.
- **Loan book reconciliation:** it opens already filled in (MAIIC Term, July to August, ties to 0.00).
- **Exports:** the disbursement export labels are fixed, and the loan book export is now served as CSV.

**Model setup**
- Transition profile Create works now. Its dropdowns were failing with "not logged in" (401) errors.
- Internal Grades now has edit and delete for draft profiles and delete for grades. I tested create, edit, add grade and both deletes.
- The ECL Projection Audit no longer contradicts itself. The FLI's portfolio projection was being treated as a contract-level run.
- The blank matrix and financial-period pages now lead to working pages.

**Administration**
- A role still held by someone can't be deleted, and you can't delete yourself or the last admin. I tested both.
- The Audit Trail labels each entry as a record change, a module action or an export, and has an **Export CSV** button.
- Financial periods now check the name and dates, and the success message is complete.
- The floating help button no longer covers Save buttons.

I updated the User and Administrator manual passages for these and reloaded them into the demo database.

**Not changed:**
- **SICR sample CSVs:** these stay header-only. That was a deliberate choice, so nothing in a sample can be mistaken for real data.
- **Compliance Audits (0 workbooks):** fixing it means running "Reload from the workbooks", which writes to the register. Tell me if you want me to run it.
- **Manual PDFs arriving cut short:** this is probably the test web server. Please check them under Apache.
- **Still open from the audit:** long unpaged EIR tables, styling on the old create pages, duplicate runs in the PD and LGD lists, RBM return CSV branding, and smaller items. The date pickers follow the browser's own date format, which the app can't change.
- **Tranched facilities:** the EIR engine still doesn't add later drawdowns. For example, Mphunzitsi 104430000085 shows amortised cost of 350m against a gross balance of 134m. It needs a drawdown plan first.

class ComplianceAuditService
{
    public const STATUSES = ['Done', 'Partially done', 'Outstanding', 'Not applicable, documented', 'Evidence needed from MAIIC'];

    /** Load (or refresh) the register from the builder's JSON files; a signed row keeps its signed state. */
    public function load(?string $dir = null): array
    {
        $dir ??= base_path('docs/compliance');
        $out = [];
        foreach (glob($dir . '/*.json') ?: [] as $file) {
            if (str_ends_with($file, '.signed.json')) {
                continue;
            }
            $data = json_decode(file_get_contents($file), true);
            if (! is_array($data) || ! isset($data['key'], $data['meta'], $data['rows'])) {
                continue;
            }
            $m = $data['meta'];
            $auditId = (int) (DB::table('compliance_audits')->where('key', $data['key'])->value('id') ?? 0);
            $values = ['file_stem' => $m['file_stem'], 'short' => $m['short'], 'title' => $m['title'], 'basis' => $m['basis'] ?? null, 'source' => $m['source'] ?? null, 'reviewer' => $m['reviewer'] ?? null, 'loaded_at' => now(), 'updated_at' => now()];
            if ($auditId) {
                DB::table('compliance_audits')->where('id', $auditId)->update($values);
            } else {
                $auditId = (int) DB::table('compliance_audits')->insertGetId($values + ['key' => $data['key'], 'created_at' => now()]);
            }
            $n = 0;
            foreach ($data['rows'] as $i => $r) {
                $existing = DB::table('compliance_audit_rows')->where('audit_id', $auditId)->where('reference', $r['reference'])->first();
                $row = array_intersect_key($r, array_flip(['part', 'section_name', 'requirement', 'engine_comment', 'general_comment', 'compliance_comment', 'where_to_see', 'governance_setting', 'test'])) + ['ordering' => $i, 'updated_at' => now()];
                if ($existing) {
                    // the module's status is taken only where no one has signed the row
                    if ($existing->signed_at === null) {
                        $row['status'] = $r['status'];
                    }
                    DB::table('compliance_audit_rows')->where('id', $existing->id)->update($row);
                } else {
                    DB::table('compliance_audit_rows')->insert($row + ['audit_id' => $auditId, 'reference' => $r['reference'], 'status' => $r['status'], 'created_at' => now()]);
                }
                $n++;
            }
            foreach ($data['findings'] ?? [] as $f) {
                DB::table('compliance_findings')->updateOrInsert(['audit_id' => $auditId, 'number' => $f['number']], array_intersect_key($f, array_flip(['reference', 'finding', 'what_was_found', 'impact', 'recommended_action', 'owner', 'status'])) + ['updated_at' => now(), 'created_at' => now()]);
            }
            $out[$data['key']] = $n;
        }

import re
R = 'C:/xampp/htdocs/MAICC-IFRS9/resources/js/Pages/'

def legacy_table(s):
    s = s.replace('<table class="min-w-full divide-y divide-gray-200">', '<table class="maiic-table">')
    s = re.sub(r'<thead class="bg-gray-(?:50|100|200)">', '<thead>', s)
    def th(m):
        cls = m.group(1)
        if 'text-right' in cls:
            return '<th class="num">'
        if 'text-center' in cls:
            return '<th class="text-center">'
        return '<th>'
    s = re.sub(r'<th class="([^"]*uppercase[^"]*)">', th, s)
    s = s.replace('<tbody class="bg-white divide-y divide-gray-200">', '<tbody>')
    return s

def header(s, title, desc, actions=''):
    m = re.search(r'<app-layout>\s*<template #header>.*?</template>', s, re.S)
    assert m
    new = f'<app-layout title="{title}" description="{desc}">'
    if actions:
        new += '\n        <template #actions>\n' + actions + '\n        </template>'
    return s[:m.start()] + new + s[m.end():]

# Payment tracking (LGD calculations)
p = R + 'RepaymentReports/Index.vue'
s = open(p, encoding='utf-8').read()
s = header(s, 'LGD payment tracking', 'Runs that follow Stage 3 loans and their payments month by month: the cures and recoveries the loss given default is built from', """            <button type="button" class="secondary-btn" @click="refreshData"><i class="fas fa-sync-alt"></i> Refresh</button>
            <button type="button" class="secondary-btn" @click="showFilters = !showFilters"><i class="fas fa-filter"></i> Filters</button>

--- content ---
<template>
    <!-- The segment a PD or LGD run was calculated for: its name on one line, the level under it.
         Shared by the monthly and cumulative PD and LGD lists. -->
    <div class="flex items-center gap-2.5">
        <span class="flex h-8 w-8 flex-none items-center justify-center rounded-lg" :class="look.chip">
            <font-awesome-icon :icon="look.icon" class="text-sm"/>
        </span>
        <span class="min-w-0">
            <span class="block font-semibold leading-tight text-gray-900 dark:text-slate-100">{{ label }}</span>
            <span class="block text-xs leading-tight text-gray-500 dark:text-slate-400">{{ caption }}</span>
        </span>
    </div>
</template>

<script setup>
import { computed } from 'vue'

const props = defineProps({
    level: { type: String, default: '' },      // book | portfolio | sector
    name: { type: String, default: '' },       // the portfolio or sector name, when known
    code: { type: [String, Number], default: '' },
})

const lvl = computed(() => String(props.level || '').toLowerCase())

const look = computed(() => ({
    book: { icon: 'database', chip: 'bg-maiic-50 text-maiic-700 dark:bg-maiic-900/40 dark:text-maiic-300' },
    portfolio: { icon: 'folder', chip: 'bg-amber-50 text-amber-700 dark:bg-amber-900/30 dark:text-amber-300' },
    sector: { icon: 'building', chip: 'bg-sky-50 text-sky-700 dark:bg-sky-900/30 dark:text-sky-300' },
}[lvl.value] || { icon: 'folder', chip: 'bg-gray-100 text-gray-600 dark:bg-slate-700 dark:text-slate-300' }))

const label = computed(() => {
    if (lvl.value === 'book') return 'Whole loan book'
    if (props.name) return props.name
    if (lvl.value === 'portfolio') return 'Portfolio ' + (props.code || '')
    if (lvl.value === 'sector') return 'Sector ' + (props.code || '')
    return props.code ? String(props.code) : '-'
})

const caption = computed(() => {
    if (lvl.value === 'book') return 'All portfolios pooled'
    if (lvl.value === 'portfolio') return 'Portfolio'
    if (lvl.value === 'sector') return props.code ? 'Sector · ' + props.code : 'Sector'
    return lvl.value ? lvl.value.charAt(0).toUpperCase() + lvl.value.slice(1) : ''
})
</script>

import re
R = 'C:/xampp/htdocs/MAICC-IFRS9/resources/js/Pages/'

def register(s):
    # add the import and the component registration
    m = re.search(r"import AppLayout from '@/Layouts/AppLayout.vue';?\n", s)
    assert m, 'AppLayout import'
    s = s[:m.end()] + "import SegmentCell from '@/Components/Maiic/SegmentCell.vue';\n" + s[m.end():]
    m = re.search(r'components\s*:\s*\{', s)
    assert m, 'components'
    s = s[:m.end()] + '\n        SegmentCell,' + s[m.end():]
    return s

for f, v, lvl, idf, codef, rel in [
    ('TransitionMatrix/Index.vue', 'matrix', 'pd_calculation_level', 'pd_calculation_id', 'pd_calculation_code', 'portfolio'),
    ('TransitionMatrix/Cummulative.vue', 'matrix', 'pd_calculation_level', 'pd_calculation_id', 'pd_calculation_code', 'portfolio'),
    ('LossGivenDefault/Cummulative.vue', 'lgdC', 'lgd_calculation_level', 'lgd_calculation_id', 'lgd_calculation_code', 'portfolio_group'),
]:
    p = R + f
    s = open(p, encoding='utf-8').read()
    pat = re.compile(r'<td>\s*<span class="maiic-badge maiic-badge-grey">\{\{ ' + v + r'\.' + lvl + r' \?.*?</div>\s*</td>', re.S)
    m = pat.search(s)
    assert m, f
    cell = (f'<td class="min-w-[11rem]"><SegmentCell :level="{v}.{lvl}" '
            f':name="{v}.{lvl} === \'portfolio\' ? ({v}.{rel}?.name || \'\') : ({v}.{lvl} === \'sector\' ? ({v}.sector?.name || \'\') : \'\')" '
            f':code="{v}.{lvl} === \'sector\' ? ({v}.sector?.code || {v}.{codef}) : {v}.{idf}"/></td>')
    s = s[:m.start()] + cell + s[m.end():]
    s = register(s)
    open(p, 'w', encoding='utf-8').write(s)
    print('ok', f)

p = R + 'LossGivenDefault/Index.vue'
s = open(p, encoding='utf-8').read()
a = "<td>{{ lgd.portfolio_group?.name || '-' }}</td>"
assert a in s
s = s.replace(a, """<td class="min-w-[11rem]"><SegmentCell :level="lgd.portfolio_group ? 'portfolio' : 'book'" :name="lgd.portfolio_group?.name || ''"/></td>""")
s = s.replace('                <th>Portfolio</th>', '                <th>Segment</th>', 1)
s = register(s)
open(p, 'w', encoding='utf-8').write(s)
print('ok lgd')

b="""    /**
     * The copy of a screenshot the PDF embeds: at most 1400 pixels wide (about 200 dpi across the
     * printed page), JPEG at quality 75, cached by path and modification time. The screen manual
     * keeps the full-size file. Without GD, or for anything but a PNG or JPEG, the original is used.
     */
    private static function pdfImage(string $file): string
    {
        if (! is_file($file) || ! function_exists('imagecreatefromjpeg') || ! preg_match('/\\.(jpe?g|png)$/i', $file)) {
            return $file;
        }
        [$w, $h] = @getimagesize($file) ?: [0, 0];
        if ($w <= 1400) {
            return $file;
        }
        $dir = storage_path('app/manual-pdf-images');
        $out = $dir . '/' . md5($file . '|' . filemtime($file)) . '.jpg';
        if (is_file($out)) {
            return $out;
        }
        if (! is_dir($dir)) {
            @mkdir($dir, 0775, true);
        }
        $src = preg_match('/\\.png$/i', $file) ? @imagecreatefrompng($file) : @imagecreatefromjpeg($file);
        if (! $src) {
            return $file;
        }
        $nw = 1400;
        $nh = (int) round($h * $nw / $w);
        $dst = imagecreatetruecolor($nw, $nh);
        imagefill($dst, 0, 0, imagecolorallocate($dst, 255, 255, 255));
        imagecopyresampled($dst, $src, 0, 0, 0, 0, $nw, $nh, $w, $h);
        $ok = imagejpeg($dst, $out, 75);
        imagedestroy($src);
        imagedestroy($dst);

        return $ok ? $out : $file;
    }

    private function company(): string"""
assert a in s; s=s.replace(a,b,1)

    /**
     * Stage 3 discloses the interest not recognised because accrual runs on
     * the net carrying amount instead of gross.
     */
    public function suspendedInterest(): float
    {
        if ($this->interest_basis !== 'NET') {
            return 0.0;
        }

        $gross = (float) $this->opening_gross;
        $net   = $gross - (float) $this->ecl_allowance;

        if ($net <= 0 || $gross <= 0) {
            return 0.0;
        }

        // interest_accrued was computed on net; scale up to the gross basis.
        return (float) $this->interest_accrued * ($gross / $net) - (float) $this->interest_accrued;
    }
}

/**
 * Facilities drawn in tranches (system audit of 13 October 2026). The roll-forward
 * records the advances drawn in the month and the basis its first month opened on:
 * SCHEDULE (the present value of the remaining scheduled cash flows, which already
 * counts every tranche) or LEDGER (the drawn balance in the ledger, to which each
 * later advance is added in the month it is drawn). The row then ties as
 * opening + advances + interest + unwind - cash - derecognised = closing.
 */
return new class extends Migration
{
    public function up(): void
    {
        foreach (['eir_amortisation', 'eir_amortisation_history'] as $table) {
            if (! Schema::hasTable($table)) {
                continue;
            }
            Schema::table($table, function (Blueprint $t) use ($table) {
                if (! Schema::hasColumn($table, 'advances')) {
                    $t->decimal('advances', 20, 2)->default(0)->after('opening_gross');
                }
                if (! Schema::hasColumn($table, 'opening_basis')) {
                    $t->string('opening_basis', 12)->nullable()->after('advances')
                        ->comment('SCHEDULE or LEDGER: what the first month of the roll-forward opened on');
                }
            });
        }
    }

                });

    }
};

("""                $opening = $previous ? (float) $previous->closing_gross : $this->initialOpening($contract, $period);""",
 """                // The first month opens on the schedule's present value or on the ledger's drawn balance;
                // every later month carries that basis forward with the closing balance.
                if ($previous) {
                    $opening = (float) $previous->closing_gross;
                    $openingBasis = $previous->opening_basis ?: 'SCHEDULE';
                } else {
                    [$opening, $openingBasis] = $this->initialOpening($contract, $period);
                }"""),
("""                $cash = $this->cashReceived($contractId, $period);
                // a write-off or a settlement in kind leaves the gross without being cash
                $closing = max(0.0, $opening + $interest + $unwind - $cash['amount'] - $cash['derecognised']);""",
 """                $cash = $this->cashReceived($contractId, $period);
                // A tranche drawn in the month raises the gross, and earns interest from the day it is
                // drawn, but only on a ledger basis: a schedule's present value already counts every
                // tranche, so adding the advance there would count it twice.
                $advances = 0.0;
                if ($openingBasis === 'LEDGER') {
                    $rate = $basis === 'NET' ? 0.0 : $monthlyRate; // Stage 3 on net: the advance is not accrued
                    foreach ($cash['advances'] as $adv) {
                        $advances += $adv['amount'];
                        $interest += $rate * $adv['amount'] * $adv['share_of_month'];
                    }
                }
                // a write-off or a settlement in kind leaves the gross without being cash
                $closing = max(0.0, $opening + $advances + $interest + $unwind - $cash['amount'] - $cash['derecognised']);"""),

        if ($gross >= 0.5 * $pv) {
            return $pv;
        }
        // a facility still drawing down is not prepaid: its schedule carries the tranches to come,
        // and the roll-forward does not add a later advance, so the schedule's value stands
        $laterAdvance = DB::table('eir_actual_transactions')->where('contract_id', $contract->contract_id)->where('transaction_type', 'Disbursement')
            ->where('transaction_date', '>', $priorEnd)->exists();

        return $opening;

        // A facility still drawing down: the schedule assumes every tranche was advanced at the

docs/MAIIC_EIR_Engine_Specification_v4_2026-10-07.md:514:- **What "as at a date" means.** The engine takes every posting in the landing zone dated on or before the date, the rate in force on the date, the governance values in force on the date, the schedule version in force on the date, and the take-on basis of 6.9, and produces for that date: the EIR in force and when it was last re-solved, the amortised cost, the gross carrying amount, the interest recognised to the date in the period and the year, the cumulative difference between the EIR interest and the contractual interest posted, the remaining expected cash flows, and the modification history. Each figure is shown with the inputs that produced it.
docs/manuals/technical/06-eir-engine.md:35:Extract B carries remaining cash flows, not the original promise, so the original schedule is either imported or generated from Extract A terms by `app/Services/Eir/ScheduleGeneratorService.php` (level annuity, moratorium interest capitalising monthly, any of 1, 2, 4, 6 or 12 payments a year, final instalment closing rounding drift). `app/Services/Eir/ScheduleWorkflowService.php` writes generated rows as version 1 with source GENERATED and status DRAFT, compares them with the remaining schedule from the earliest remaining due date (principal and interest variance within one percent gives WITHIN_TOLERANCE, otherwise PRINCIPAL_VARIANCE or INTEREST_VARIANCE, or NO_REMAINING_DATA), and approves only a DRAFT with a review note when the comparison is outside tolerance. An APPROVED schedule cannot be regenerated. Only version 1 is written by any code today; restructures as version 2 and modification gains and losses are not yet implemented and `modification_gain_loss` is stored as zero.

        $rows = DB::table('eir_amortisation')->where('contract_id', 'PV')->orderBy('reporting_period')->get();

        // January opens on the value at 31 December, so the loan is repaid in full in March;
        // opened on the value at 31 January, a month's interest would be left over
        $this->assertSame('SCHEDULE', $rows[0]->opening_basis);
        $this->assertEqualsWithDelta(0, $rows[2]->closing_gross, 1.0);
    }

    public function test_a_facility_lent_within_the_month_opens_at_nil_and_adds_each_tranche_from_its_day(): void
    {
        DB::table('contract_eir')->insert(['contract_id' => 'TR', 'eir_effective_annual' => 0.126825, 'origination_date' => '2025-01-10',
            'source_day_count_basis' => 'ACT/365', 'input_snapshot' => json_encode(['initial_net_investment' => 1000, 'cash_flows' => [
                ['due_date' => '2025-12-31', 'amount' => 1150],
            ]]), 'locked_at' => '2025-01-10', 'created_at' => now(), 'updated_at' => now()]);
        $this->loan('TR', '2025-01', 1);
        $this->loan('TR', '2025-02', 1);
        $this->actual('TR', '2025-01-11', 'Disbursement', 600);
        $this->actual('TR', '2025-02-15', 'Disbursement', 400);

        $service = new EirRevenueService();
        $service->run('TR', '2025-01');
        $service->run('TR', '2025-02');
        [$jan, $feb] = DB::table('eir_amortisation')->where('contract_id', 'TR')->orderBy('reporting_period')->get()->all();
        $r = pow(1.126825, 1 / 12) - 1;

        $this->assertSame('LEDGER', $jan->opening_basis);
        $this->assertEqualsWithDelta(0, $jan->opening_gross, 0.01);
        $this->assertEqualsWithDelta(600, $jan->advances, 0.01);
        $this->assertEqualsWithDelta($r * 600 * 21 / 31, $jan->interest_accrued, 0.01);
        // February carries the basis, and the second tranche earns interest from 15 February
        $this->assertSame('LEDGER', $feb->opening_basis);
        $this->assertEqualsWithDelta(400, $feb->advances, 0.01);
        $this->assertEqualsWithDelta($r * $jan->closing_gross + $r * 400 * 14 / 28, $feb->interest_accrued, 0.01);
        $this->assertEqualsWithDelta($jan->closing_gross + 400 + $feb->interest_accrued, $feb->closing_gross, 0.01);
    }

    public function test_an_advance_is_not_added_to_a_schedule_basis_roll_forward(): void
    {
        $this->seedLocked(); // no schedule dates: the initial net investment, which counts every tranche
        $this->loan('C-1', '2025-01', 1);
        $this->actual('C-1', '2025-01-05', 'Disbursement', 5_000);

        (new EirRevenueService())->run('C-1', '2025-01');
        $row = DB::table('eir_amortisation')->first();

        $this->assertSame('SCHEDULE', $row->opening_basis);
        $this->assertEqualsWithDelta(0, $row->advances, 0.01);
        $this->assertEqualsWithDelta(1010, $row->closing_gross, 0.01);
    }
}

1:## 6. EIR and Revenue Recognition Engine
3:### 6.1 The three doors
9:| 1 Measurement | Constructs amortised cost as a roll-forward: closing = opening + interest + unwind minus cash, replacing the tape-imported carrying amount | `app/Services/Eir/EirRevenueService.php` |
15:### 6.2 Pipeline
23:The EIR screens are gated in their controller constructors: the rules, fee classification, schedule and calculation screens by `permission:settings` (fee classification and intake also admit `eir.fees.import`); EIR Data, the coverage tabs (Blockers, Coverage by Portfolio, Largest Facilities), EIR as at a Date and the GL Reconciliation view by `eir.view`; the reconciliation export by `eir.export`; the Governance Centre by `eir.govern`. The menu hides each tab from a user without its permission (chapter 2.3). `hasRole('admin')` remains the finer control used for the review override, the lock override and reopening.
25:### 6.3 Fee rulebook
29:### 6.4 Fee classification
33:### 6.5 Schedule governance
37:### 6.6 Readiness gate
41:### 6.7 Solver
43:`app/Services/Eir/CalculateEirService.php` is a pure periodic internal rate of return solver with no database access. Newton-Raphson runs up to 100 iterations with a bisection fallback of up to 250 iterations; the result is accepted only if the residual net present value is within one part in a billion of the initial investment. Outputs are always labelled: `eir_period`, `eir_nominal_annual` (period rate times payments per year) and `eir_effective_annual` ((1 + period rate) to the power of payments per year, minus one). The date-sensitive entry point discounts on the actual contractual dates under the contract's day-count basis (ACT/365, ACT/360, 30/360, 30E/360) and solves the effective annual rate directly, so an irregular first period or a moratorium does not distort the rate; `EirCalculationService` chooses it whenever every cash flow carries a due date. Validation refuses a non-positive initial investment, an unsupported frequency, duplicate periods and negative receipts.
47:### 6.8 Calculation, lock and reopening
49:`app/Services/Eir/EirCalculationService.php` writes the result to `contract_eir` with status CALCULATED, the solver method, iterations and residual, and the input snapshot; a failure sets BLOCKED with the error. `app/Jobs/CalculateEirJob.php` processes a batch and a blocked contract does not stop the batch. Locking requires a CALCULATED result and a reviewer different from the calculator (admin override allowed); it sets LOCKED and is final. Reopening is administrator-only, demands a reason of at least ten characters, archives the locked result to `eir_calculation_history`, moves every amortisation row to `eir_amortisation_history`, marks the contract's ECL discounting as `STALE_EIR_REOPENED` and returns the contract to REOPENED for recalculation and fresh approval. Recalculating an unlocked contract archives the previous result with the reason "Recalculated before final approval".
51:### 6.9 Revenue run
58:interest    = monthlyRate x (basis NET ? max(0, opening - allowance) : opening)
59:unwind      = basis NET ? monthlyRate x min(allowance, opening) : 0
60:closing     = max(0, opening + interest + unwind - cash)
63:Opening is the prior month's closing, or for a late first run the present value of the remaining contractual flows at the locked rate. The stage and ECL allowance are read from the loan book row for the month. Cash received comes from imported actuals when the actuals window covers the month (collection types Interest, Principal+Interest and Fee; disbursements are never netted; unknown types are reported), otherwise from the version 1 schedule and marked DERIVED. Rerunning a period archives that period and every later one for the contract, because each opening is the prior closing; recalculation without a reason is refused.
65:### 6.10 GL reconciliation
71:base effect       = contractual monthly x (amortised opening - implied base)
72:rate effect       = (effective monthly - contractual monthly) x opening
73:impairment effect = accrued - effective monthly x opening

````
### 6.9 Revenue run

`php artisan eir:run-revenue {period}` (queued with `--queue`) runs `app/Jobs/RunEirRevenueJob.php` over locked contracts. Per contract and month, `EirRevenueService` computes:

```
monthlyRate = (1 + eir_effective_annual)^(1/12) - 1
basis       = stage 3 ? NET : GROSS
interest    = monthlyRate x (basis NET ? max(0, opening - allowance) : opening)
unwind      = basis NET ? monthlyRate x min(allowance, opening) : 0
closing     = max(0, opening + interest + unwind - cash)
```

Opening is the prior month's closing, or for a late first run the present value of the remaining contractual flows at the locked rate. The stage and ECL allowance are read from the loan book row for the month. Cash received comes from imported actuals when the actuals window covers the month (collection types Interest, Principal+Interest and Fee; disbursements are never netted; unknown types are reported), otherwise from the version 1 schedule and marked DERIVED. Rerunning a period archives that period and every later one for the contract, because each opening is the prior closing; recalculation without a reason is refused.
### 6.12 Not yet implemented

Proposed adjusting journal entries, the auditor-format Excel export of the reconciliation, schedule versions beyond one, modification accounting, rate-reset regeneration, an actuals import with `cash_source = IMPORTED` end to end, a CCF model, and scheduling of the monthly run. `app/Console/Kernel.php` does not schedule the monthly revenue run; it is run by hand or as a step of the Maintenance month-end job (`maiic:task month-end`, chapter 9.5).

Opening is the prior month's closing, or for a late first run the present value of the remaining contractual flows at the locked rate."""
b="""unwind      = basis NET ? monthlyRate x min(allowance, opening) : 0
advances    = basis LEDGER ? tranches drawn in the month : 0
interest   += monthlyRate x each advance x (days outstanding in the month / days in the month)
closing     = max(0, opening + advances + interest + unwind - cash - derecognised)
```

Opening is the prior month's closing. The first month opens on one of two bases, recorded on every row as `opening_basis` and carried forward with the closing balance:

- **SCHEDULE**: the present value, at the locked rate, of the contractual flows due after the end of the month before. (Until 13 October 2026 the value was taken at the end of the month itself, which counted that month's interest twice.)
- **LEDGER**: the drawn balance in the E-Banker ledger at the end of the month before, used when the facility is still drawing down (an advance falls after that date), when it was lent within the month (the opening is then nil), or when the borrower has prepaid (the ledger is below half the present value). Each later tranche is added in the month it is drawn and earns interest from that day; the row's `advances` column holds it. A schedule-basis row never adds an advance, because the schedule's present value already counts every tranche. Each ledger opening is written to the audit log as `EIR Opening From Ledger` with both figures and the reason."""

EIR openings and tranched facilities; segment column; remaining audit items; Technical Manual brought up to date

EIR revenue engine
- The first month opens on the amortised cost at the end of the month before (the present value at that date of the flows still to come). It was taken at the end of the month itself, which counted that month's interest twice.
- A facility still drawing down, or lent within the month, opens on the ledger's drawn balance (nil when lent in the month) and adds each later tranche in the month it is drawn, with interest from that day. A schedule-basis roll-forward never adds a tranche, because the schedule's value already counts every one. Each row records advances and opening_basis (migration 2026_10_13_150000), and the history keeps both.
- Mphunzitsi SACCO (104430000085) now tracks its ledger (August 127.2m against 133.6m, was 349.9m); Malawi Police SACCO is within 10.9m of 3,054m (was 135m over).
- Tests: the prior-month-end opening, a facility lent within the month with two tranches, and no advance on a schedule basis.

Screens
- PD and LGD lists, monthly and cumulative: one segment cell (name, level caption, icon) replaces the badge over the name; run time shown under each run; LGD amounts with comma separators; cumulative tables fit the panel.
- Legacy create pages (PD matrix, cumulative PD, LGD, cumulative LGD, transition profile) and the payment tracking, page help, licence and currency pages use the standard header, description, Back button and tables; buttons in sentence case throughout (Jetstream button restyled).
- Role editor: "Staging and SICR Rules" (label only; permission names unchanged, migration 2026_10_13_140000) and the banks, branches and legal types modules listed last as legacy screens.
- EIR GL reconciliation facilities table fits the panel; Audit Trail and LGD lists use the standard pager; the SICR Raise dialog has its width; hub format labels are text, not button-like badges.

Reports and documents
- RBM return CSV is the branded report with the per-facility section; on-screen totals rows line up.
- Report PDFs keep a short section, with its part banner, on one page, so no heading or table header is left at the foot of a page.
- User and Administrator manual PDFs embed screenshots at 1400 pixels (user manual 26 MB to 10 MB) and are served from a file, so they arrive whole.
- Technical Manual chapters updated for the 9 October menu and the 13 October FLI module; the EIR chapter documents the opening bases and tranches and lists floating-rate re-estimation and opening arrears as not yet implemented. Installation Guide scheduler paragraph corrected.

## 0. How to read this document

Version 3 was written before MAIIC's database could be read directly. It described the engine around three extracts (A, B and C) that MAIIC's ICT team produced with their own scripts, and it listed twenty-three choices that were still open. Between 5 and 7 October 2026 Barry Makumba ran twenty-seven data-dictionary queries and eighteen follow-up extracts for us, then five more on request. Those ex

This document records that. It is written, as before, for three readers at once: the CFO, who has to be confident that the numbers will stand up to Deloitte; the ICT manager, who supplies the data and hosts the system; and the developers, who build it. Every section starts in plain language. The same three words are used in the same way as in version 3:

- **Agreed** means a decision that has been taken, by whom and when.
- **Decided and seeded** is new. It means a choice that has been settled by Dupleix on the evidence, written into the Governance Centre as the default in force, and is waiting only for Dr Thom to confirm or change it. Section 4 lists every one, with its default.
- **Proven** means a fact tested against MAIIC's own data and reproduced, with the file and the count given so that anyone can repeat the test.

Where a file is named, it is one of the extracts committed under `docs/bootstrap/` in the repository (section 6.10), with a copy in `2. ### 4.2 Decided and seeded: every setting, its default, and where it stands

### 6.11 The EIR as at any date

A requirement in its own right: **the system shows the EIR computation for any loan as at any date the user names**, not only at month-ends and not only for the latest run.

- **What "as at a date" means.** The engine takes every posting in the landing zone dated on or before the date, the rate in force on the date, the governance values in force on the date, the schedule version in force on the date, and the take-on basis of 6.9, and produces for that date: the EIR in 
- **Any date, not only a period end.** A date inside a month uses the actual-day convention of section 3 (prior month-end balance, rate, days over 365) for the part-month. A date in a locked period reproduces the locked figures exactly, because a locked period keeps the settings and the schedule it 
- **For the whole book.** The same view at portfolio level: the EIR interest, the contractual interest and the difference for the year to the date, by product, by GL and in total, which is the revenue shift Dr Thom asked for, at any date.

rep("## 4. Decisions, and the Governance Centre", """### 3.10 Where the revenue roll-forward starts, and facilities drawn in tranches (added 13 October 2026)

**In plain language.** The engine builds each loan's amortised cost month by month: the opening balance, plus the interest at the EIR, less the cash. Everything after the first month follows from the month before, so the first month has to be right. Two faults were found in it on 13 October 2026 and both are corrected.

**The first month was dated a month late.** The opening was the present value of the remaining instalments taken at the end of the first month, and the month's interest was then added on top, so that month's interest was counted twice. A loan with one repayment of 1,030 due at the end of March, run from January at 1 percent a month, was left with about 10 outstanding after it was repaid in full. The opening is now the present value at the end of the month before (decision D32).

**A facility drawn in tranches was treated as if it had been lent in full on day one.** The schedule assumes every tranche is advanced at the start, so its present value counts money not yet lent, and the roll-forward never added a later tranche. Proven on Mphunzitsi SACCO (104430000085): approved 1,047.7 million, drawn 397.7 million in August 2025, 350 million in November 2025 and 300 million in February 2026; the engine opened December 2025 at 887.5 million against a ledger of 421.2 million and closed August 2026 at 349.9 million against 133.6 million. Malawi Police SACCO (3,139.3 million drawn on 19 January 2026) and KWACHA Boutique Hotel (800 million on 20 May and 700 million on 2 June 2026) were lent within their first engine month and were opened at the full present value with a full month's interest.

**The rule now (decision D33).** The first month opens on one of two bases, recorded on every row as `opening_basis` and carried forward with the closing balance:

| Basis | When | Opening | Later advances |
|---|---|---|---|
| SCHEDULE | The usual case | Present value, at the locked EIR, of the contractual flows due after the end of the month before | Never added: the schedule's value already counts every tranche |
| LEDGER | The facility is still drawing down (an advance falls after the end of the month before), or was lent within the month (opening nil), or the borrower has prepaid (the ledger is below half the present value, decision D34) | The drawn balance in the E-Banker ledger at the end of the month before | Each tranche added in the month it is drawn, earning interest from that day; held on the row as `advances` |

Every ledger opening is written to the audit log (`EIR Opening From Ledger`) with the present value, the ledger balance and the reason. The row now ties as opening + advances + interest + unwind - cash - derecognised = closing.

**What it did to the figures (demo database, August 2026).** The ten loans on the ledger basis tie to the loan book within 2.8 million on 6,675.7 million: Mphunzitsi 127.2 million against 133.6 million, Malawi Police SACCO 3,065.1 million against 3,054.2 million. EIR interest for January to August 2026 is 1,812.3 million against contractual interest of 2,031.4 million, a shift of -219.1 million (it read -51.6 million before the correction, because the double-counted first months raised the EIR side).

**What is still open, with the evidence.** The 21 loans on the schedule basis opened December 2025 within 62 million of the ledger in total but are 479.5 million below it by August 2026, and the gap grows every month. The largest are Chipala Investment (-117.6 million), Saile Financial Services (-70.1 million) and Chikomanyama Farms (-41.2 million). Two causes, both already in the build plan: the contractual rate has moved with the prime lending rate while the locked EIR has not been re-estimated (IFRS 9 B5.4.5, phase P5); and instalments unpaid before the first month are not added to the opening (Chipala had paid 152.2 million of 219.5 million due by 30 November 2025; phase P6, arrears). Until P5 and P6 are built the shift for these loans is overstated and is reported as such.

## 4. Decisions, and the Governance Centre""")

# decisions D32 to D37 after the D23 row

| D33 | **A facility still drawing down, or lent within the month, runs on the ledger's drawn balance** (section 3.10): the opening is the drawn balance (nil when lent in the month) and each later tranche is added in the month it is drawn, with interest from that day; a schedule-basis loan never adds a tranche. The basis is recorded on every row. | Dupleix, 13 Oct 2026 | The schedule assumes every tranche on day one; Mphunzitsi SACCO was overstated by 216 million at August 2026. |
| D34 | **A prepaid loan opens on the ledger balance** when the ledger at the end of the month before is below half the present value of the remaining schedule; the substitution is audit-logged with both figures. | Dupleix, 13 Oct 2026 | Barnet Agriculture repaid 55.6 million in November 2025; the schedule's value was 38.8 million against 0.4 million owed. |
| D35 | **The actual cash of every loan is loaded from the E-Banker ledger** (`eir:load-ledger-cash`, source `EBANKER_LEDGER` in `eir_actual_transactions`) and is part of the month-end job, so the roll-forward uses receipts, not the schedule, wherever the ledger covers the month. | D36 | **Every client is linked to its loans** (`clients:link-loan-book`, by external identity and then by name, recorded on the client) and **each import screen shows only its own import history** (`imports.kind`). | Edward, 13 Oct 2026 | Clients were not linked to the loan book; every import screen listed every import. |
| D37 | **Maintenance is seven jobs, as in the Stress Testing suite** (`maiic:task`): month-end (link clients, stage, PD by segment, forward-looking month-end, ledger cash, revenue run, Mega Farm ECL where present), refresh data, health check, update and bootstrap behind a typed confirmation, with a run history. | Edward, 13 Oct 2026 | The tabs were overwhelming; the month-end order is now one button. |

## 4. The screens

The forward-looking module moves out of IFRS 9 Model Setup into its own menu entry, **Forward-Looking Information**, with one tab row (the section-tab pattern used across the system):

| Tab | What it holds | Built from |
|---|---|---|
| Overview | The period's FLI readiness: model version in force, scenario set in force, vintage, overlays, the effect on the ECL, what is missing | New |
| Economic Indicators | The series, actuals and forecasts kept apart, source and release date per value, revisions compared, imports with how-to and samples | Macro Statistics |
| Scenario Workbench | Draft, compare and approve scenario sets: paths per series per year, weights, narrative, calibration note, trajectories charted against history | Scenario Sets |
| Model Calibration | The annual workbench: data selection, the Correlation Finder, the fits under the guardrail, out-of-time back-test, stability, the model version and its lifecycle | Correlation Finder and Regression |
| Overlays | The overlay register with the double-counting check | Manual Overlays |
| Impact Analysis | Proposed against approved: ECL per scenario, weighted ECL, by portfolio, stage, driver and overlay; drill to the loan | New, from the per-scenario results |
| Approval and History | Every model version, scenario set and overlay, who proposed, who approved, when, and what each month-end ran under | New, from the existing approval records |

Every figure on the Overview and Impact Analysis tabs comes from the same stored results as the ECL and the dashboard build-up panel, so a headline can never disagree with the detail.

## 5. The data model
## 8. Reports and workbooks

The Report Hub gains, under Annual report and audit and under Risk and analytics:

- The FLI scenario workbook: the paths, weights, narrative and approvals of the set in force.
- The model calibration workbook: the data, the coefficients, the diagnostics, the back-test and the validation sign-off of the model version in force.
- The FLI impact workbook: ECL per scenario and weighted, by portfolio and stage, with the driver attribution and the overlays.
- The FLI line in the IFRS 9 note's movement reconciliation.

Each carries the reporting date and the run identifier, so it can be reproduced from the run snapshot.

| 4. Screens | Section 4: the Forward-Looking Information menu, Overview, Impact Analysis, Approval and History | Every headline figure equals the stored results; one tab row; the Legacy FLI tools stay under Administration |

| 6. Workbooks | Section 8 | Each workbook reproduces from the run snapshot |

Each phase lands with its tests, its screens, the user and administrator manuals updated, and the Installation Guide month-end run (section 9.9) amended where a step changes.

## 10. Asked of MAIIC and Dr Thom

| # | Question | Why it matters |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Do you agree the three cadences of D-F1 (model yearly, scenarios quarterly, application monthly), and who owns each? | Today the fit is re-approved every month, which is neither necessary nor what auditors expect |
| 2 | Can the Reserve Bank's industry NPL series (or the DFI peer series) be obtained, monthly or quarterly, as far back as possible? | It is the series the credit-cycle method needs while MAIIC's own history is short |
| 3 | Who proposes and who approves the scenario set: Finance, Risk, ALCO? Are the current weights (50 / 15 / 25 / 10, with a severe scenario) the starting point? | Governance of the weights is the first question an auditor asks |
| 4 | Should the LGD of agricultural loans respond to the scenarios through crop prices and warehouse-receipt values? | Decides whether phase 5 includes a scenario-sensitive LGD |
| 5 | For PLR-linked floating loans, is the current effective rate (original spread over the PLR in force) the accepted discount basis? | D-F6; it changes the discounted ECL of 36 floating contracts |
| 6 | What month-on-month ECL movement should require commentary before sign-off? | Sets the tolerance in section 7 |
| 7 | Is a three-year reasonable forecast horizon, with reversion to the long-run average after it, acceptable? | Sets the horizon of D-F4 |

## Conventions agreed in the UI audits of 13 October 2026

Two audits walked every screen from the imports, through the calculations, to
the reports. What they settled is the standard for every screen from now on;
the code that implements each point is named so it can be reused, not
re-invented.

### Screens

- **Page header.** `app-layout` with `title` and a one-line `description`;
  the actions sit at the top right (`#actions`). Back is a white secondary
  button (`secondary-btn`) in the header actions, never a second green
  button, and there is no blank gap above the first panel.
- **Buttons.** Sentence case everywhere (the Jetstream button is now
  `primary-btn`). Green primary, white secondary, red `danger-btn` for a
  delete, which always asks for confirmation naming what is deleted.
- **Every list can be worked from the screen.** Create, edit, delete and
  refresh are on the screen itself. A delete that would leave the system
  wrong is refused with the reason: a role still held by a user, your own
  account, the last administrator, an active grading profile.
- **Tables fit the panel at 1440 px.** A table of more than six columns uses
  `maiic-table-compact`; long text columns are capped in width; a short
  first column (a period, a code) never wraps. Tab rows wrap onto a second
  line rather than scroll sideways. Footer totals line up with the body
  (`tfoot th` has the body's padding).
- **Paging.** 15 rows a page, with the standard pager (`Pagination.vue` for
  server pages, `ClientPager.vue` for lists the page holds in full).
- **Segments.** The segment a PD or LGD run was calculated for is shown with
  `Components/Maiic/SegmentCell.vue`: an icon chip, the name on one line and
  the level under it (Whole loan book / All portfolios pooled, Portfolio,
  Sector and code).
- **Numbers and dates.** Comma thousands and two decimals; PD and LGD as
  percentages; dates as `13 Oct 2026` and run times as `13 Oct, 11:59`, so
  two runs of the same window can be told apart.
- **Imports.** An Import button at the top right opens a modal with the
  instructions, the layout and a sample file; the file is previewed before it
  is committed; each import screen lists only its own history
  (`imports.kind`).
- **Source codes** of macro series read `WB: code` and `IMF: code`.
- **Help.** The floating help button opens the manual article for the screen;
  page content keeps clear of it (bottom padding), so it never covers a Save
  button.
- **Dialogs** take a width from `sm` to `6xl` (`Jetstream/Modal.vue`).
- **Light and dark mode** for every change.

### Reports

- **Hub tiles** list their formats as text ("Downloads as PDF, Excel, CSV"),
  not as badges that look like buttons.
- **PDF.** A section of up to 20 rows stays on one page together with its
  part banner, so no heading or table header is left at the foot of a page;
  `thead` repeats on each page of a long table.
- **Same basis on every screen.** The RBM classification and the RBM Return
  both apply the directive's minimum rates to the gross balance, so the NPL
  ratio and the minimum provision agree.
- **The forward-looking reports** read the month record (`fli_run_snapshots`)
  and the approved scenario set of the chosen month; a month with no record
  says so.
- **CSV** downloads are the branded report (the RBM Return included) and are
  served as `text/csv`.
- **Large PDFs** (the manuals) embed screenshots at 1400 pixels wide and are
  served from a file, so they arrive whole (the user manual went from 26 MB to
  10 MB).

### Maintenance

Seven jobs, as in the Stress Testing suite (`maiic:task`): month-end, refresh
data, health check, update and bootstrap (behind a typed confirmation), with a
run history.

Local clone at `c:\xampp\htdocs\MAICC-IFRS9`. Data at `OneDrive\2026\Projects\MAIIC\`. Mirrors the IFRS 9 teaching workbook at `Documents\IFRS9_Floating_Rate_EIR_Illustration.xlsx`.

## OPEN QUESTIONS FOR MAIIC (raise at the meeting on/around 24-25 Sep 2026)

1. **The reference-rate refresh button in the loan origination system.** The field arrives pre-populated with a refresh button beside it, which implies it holds a *stamped snapshot*, not a live link to the PLR file. Evidence: offer letter L01 (Ebenezer Midian) was approved 8 Aug 2025 carrying a typed rate of 25.10%, but PLR was 25.30% on both the approval and accrual dates - 25.10% had not been in force since early July 2025. **Ask: is the reference rate stamped at record creation, when is it refreshed, who clicks it, and is refresh mandatory before the offer letter prints?** This decides the `Margin Derivation Basis` governance default (AS_CAPTURED vs LIVE_AT_DRAWDOWN).
2. **Does file B (actual cash flow transactions) exist and can it be supplied?** Not a blocker any more (the loan book substitutes), but needed to resolve the ~24% of accounts with counter resets.
3. **Can MAIIC export the original repayment schedules as issued, for the whole book?** Would turn "reproduce the offer letter" from a 10-loan test into a whole-book control.
4. **Why does `rate_type` in the contract master extract appear inverted?** See findings below. Something downstream may be reading it backwards.
5. **What causes a `Repayments` counter reset to zero?** Settlement, restructure, or re-booked facility? 23 zero-resets in 9 months.
6. **Integration vs CSV** - is direct integration to VGCBS/E-Banker in scope, or CSV import first?
7. **How was `Interest Rate Change History.xlsx` generated?** Root cause of its date bug is SOLVED (see findings) - it is an Excel locale artefact, not a system fault. But confirm: was it a direct database extract by Barry, or did the vendor supply it? **There is no PLR / interest-rate-change report in E-Banker's documented report catalogue**, so it is almost certainly a raw DB query. Ask for it re-supplied as **CSV with ISO `yyyy-mm-dd` dates**, and as a repeatable extract rather than a one-off.
8. **Ask for three E-Banker reports that are documented but never requested** (`Ebanker MANUAL.pdf` s.5, "MAIIC Report"): **5.2 Reschedule Report** (restructuring events - needed for modification accounting), **5.1 Audit Trail Report** (who changed a rate and when - would confirm which accounts are `Interest Policy = Manual`), **5.3 IFRS9 Detail Report** (what E-Banker already computes for IFRS 9). 5.4 Loan Book Report is the source of the loan books we already have.

## MEETING PACK - Barry Makumba (ICT) + Dr Thomson Kumwenda (CFO), ~25 Sep 2026

Builds on the **Consolidated Information Request of 11 Sep 2026** (15 numbered requests, in `Email requests6-09-11 ... UPDATED (to MAIIC).html`). Do NOT re-ask items already in it. Below is only what is new, changed, or now answerable.

**A. Request 14 (manuals) is CLOSED** - `Ebanker MANUAL.pdf` and `LOS MANUAL.pdf` arrived 21 Sep 2026 and answer several items still marked Open:
- The "three separate grace and moratorium fields" query in request 14: LOS has `Moratorium`, `Moratorium Type` and a SEPARATE `Grace Period (In Month)` (p.76-77). Still ask how Moratorium and Grace Period interact.
- Field #5 `Moratorium Type`: the LOS dropdown has **exactly two options, "Principle Only" and "Both"** - the system cannot express an interest-only moratorium.

**B. SIX NEW ASKS not in the 11 Sep request**
1. **`Interest Policy` per account** - the highest-value missing field. Field #2 of the 11 Sep request asks for "Rate Type", but the manuals show E-Banker has TWO fields: `Interest Policy` (No applied / Manual (M) / Link with Lien / **Link with PLR (P)** / Customer-wise / Fixed (F)) and `Floating Flag`. **`RATE_BASIS` in Extract A is the Floating Flag, not the PLR link.** That is why it looked inverted. Ask for `Interest Policy` AND `Floating Flag` per account.
2. **Three documented E-Banker reports never requested** (`Ebanker MANUAL.pdf` s.5 "MAIIC Report"): **5.2 Reschedule Report** (restructure events - supports request 12), **5.1 Audit Trail Report** (who changed a rate and when - would identify the `Manual (M)` accounts; may be the "per account audit report" already referenced in request 12), **5.3 IFRS9 Detail Report** (what E-Banker already computes for IFRS 9).
3. **ISO DATES ON EVERY EXTRACT - and re-supply the ones already affected.** Not just the rate file. A scan of all extracts on 2026-09-24 found the same Excel locale artefact throughout, with **1,134 business-critical dates silently wrong** (3,974 including `GENERATED_ON` metadata): Extract A `LOAN_START_DATE` 142, `FIRST_REPAYMENT_DATE` 74, `CONTRACTUAL_MATURITY_DATE` 108, `ACTUAL_CLOSURE_DATE` 52; **Extract B `TRANSACTION_DATE` 686 of 2,478 rows = 28%**; Interest Rate Change History 20; Dec-2025 EIR assessment 52. Extract C appears clean. Loan books are .xls and were not covered by that scan - still to do. A date is only genuinely wrong where day != month (e.g. 01/01/2025 survives transposition, 03/04/2023 does not). **Ask: every future extract as CSV with ISO `yyyy-mm-dd`, generated straight from the database, never opened or re-saved in Excel before sending. And re-supply Extract A and Extract B on that basis, since the versions we hold cannot be trusted on dates.** Consequence to state: a wrong LOAN_START_DATE shifts a whole schedule by months; a wrong TRANSACTION_DATE puts cash in the wrong period. Both flow straight into the EIR and neither looks wrong on the page.
4. **E-Banker `IFRS9 Detail Report` (Menu ID 3863)** - manual p.76 text is boilerplate, but the screenshot shows cols 25-36 of a 36+ column report: TENURE/TERMS, INTEREST RATE, **INTEREST COMPOUND (Monthly/semi-annual/annually)**, LOAN SERIES, INSTALLMENT DATE, INSTALLMENT AMOUNT, FIRST INSTALLMENT DATE, LAST INSTALLMENT DATE/MATURITY, ARREAR DAYS, ARREAR AMOUNT (P+I+PENALTIES), ARREAR AMOUNT-INTEREST, ARREAR AMOUNT-PRINCIPAL. **Every visible column is an INPUT to IFRS 9, not an output** - no EIR, no amortised cost, no carrying amount, no stage, no ECL. --- content ---
---
name: maiic-eir-opening-basis
description: MAIIC EIR roll-forward opening rules (D32-D34, 13 Oct 2026) and the open P5/P6 gap; don't re-add advances on a schedule basis
metadata:
  type: project
---

MAIIC EIR revenue engine (`EirRevenueService`), decided and built 13 Oct 2026 (spec v4 section 3.10, D32-D37; commit ac2abb7 on `eir_revenue_recognition`):

- First month opens at the present value at the END OF THE MONTH BEFORE (D32). It used to be the month's own end, which double-counted that month's interest.
- `opening_basis` on every `eir_amortisation` row, carried forward. LEDGER = drawn balance at prior month-end (nil if lent within the month), used for facilities still drawing down, lent in the month, or prepaid (<50% of PV); each later tranche goes in the `advances` column with pro-rata interest from its draw date. SCHEDULE never adds advances. (An earlier attempt added advances on schedule-basis rows too and double-counted KWACHA; that's why the basis is recorded.)
- Demo DB after re-run: 10 LEDGER loans tie to gross within 2.8m on 6.68bn; Jan-Aug 2026 EIR 1,812.3m vs contractual 2,031.4m (shift -219.1m, was -51.6m).

**Still open:** 21 SCHEDULE loans are 479.5m below gross at Aug 2026, and the gap grows monthly. Causes: no B5.4.5 re-estimation when the prime rate moves (phase P5), and opening arrears not added (phase P6; e.g. Chipala paid 152.2m of 219.5m due by 30 Nov 2025). Spec 6.9 says the arrears difference is "booked as arrears", but how arrears enter the opening is a methodology call to put to Edward, not one to make silently.

**How to apply:** when re-running revenue from the console, redirect stdin (`</dev/null`) in loops, because artisan swallows piped input. Contracts that start after the recalculated period need their own `--contract --recalculate` run from their first month. Related: [[maiic-eir-calculator]], [[feedback-correctness-over-golden]].
