<script setup lang="ts">
import { computed, ref } from 'vue'
import { Link } from '@inertiajs/vue3'
import AppLayout from '@/Layouts/AppLayout.vue'
import InfoPopover from '@/Components/InfoPopover.vue'
import { num } from '@/format'

interface Item {
  slug: string
  label: string
  blurb: string
  tier: number
  tables: number
  rows: number
  url: string
}
interface Group { domain: string; items: Item[] }

interface Interpretation {
  code: string
  engine: string
  subject: string
  authority: string
  ambiguity: string
  applied: string
  is_default: boolean
  alternatives: string[]
  rationale: string
  boz_status: string
}

interface PoolAllocation {
  id: number
  category: string
  code: string
  amount: number
  rationale: string
  author: string | null
  effective: string | null
}

interface DepositPool {
  code: string
  label: string
  as_of: string | null
  statement: number
  register: number
  amount: number
  allocated: number
  residual: number
  residual_category: string
  residual_pct: number
  gap_pct: number
  allocations: PoolAllocation[]
  basis: string | null
}

interface FcProjection { year: number; method: string; scenario: string; stage: string; hqla: number; net_outflows: number; lcr: number | null; lcr_min: number; lcr_surplus: number; asf: number; rsf: number; nsfr: number | null; legacy_warning: string | null; source_run_id: number | null }
interface FcAssumption { year: number; code: string; label: string; group: string | null; share: number; source: string; is_override: boolean; rationale: string | null; by: string | null; from_run_id: number | null }
interface FcAction { year: number; expiry_year: number | null; name: string; type: string; amount: number; feasibility: string; impact: string | null; rationale: string; by: string | null }
interface LiquidityForecast {
  available: boolean
  base_run?: { id: number; name: string | null; year: number | null; rulebook_date: string | null }
  calibration_source?: string
  worst_of_n?: number
  reporting_method?: string
  parked_return_reason?: string
  nsfr_label?: string
  projections?: FcProjection[]
  assumptions?: FcAssumption[]
  actions?: FcAction[]
}

const props = defineProps<{
  groups: Group[]
  interpretations: Interpretation[]
  depositPools: DepositPool[]
  liquidityForecast: LiquidityForecast
  totals: { items: number; rows: number }
}>()

const fmt = (n: number) => num(n)
type View = 'areas' | 'attention' | 'forecast'
const activeView = ref<View>('areas')
const search = ref('')
const selectedDomain = ref('all')
const forecastYears = computed(() => [...new Set((props.liquidityForecast.projections ?? []).map(p => p.year))].sort((a, b) => a - b))
const selectedYear = ref<number | null>(null)
const currentYear = computed(() => selectedYear.value ?? forecastYears.value[0] ?? null)
const visibleProjections = computed(() => (props.liquidityForecast.projections ?? []).filter(p => p.year === currentYear.value))
const visibleAssumptions = computed(() => (props.liquidityForecast.assumptions ?? []).filter(a => a.year === currentYear.value))
const visibleActions = computed(() => (props.liquidityForecast.actions ?? []).filter(a => a.year === currentYear.value))
const filteredGroups = computed(() => props.groups.map((group, index) => ({
  ...group,
  index,
  items: group.items.filter(item => {
    const matchesDomain = selectedDomain.value === 'all' || group.domain === selectedDomain.value
    const term = search.value.trim().toLowerCase()
    return matchesDomain && (!term || `${item.label} ${item.blurb} ${group.domain}`.toLowerCase().includes(term))
  }),
})).filter(group => group.items.length > 0))
const shownAreas = computed(() => filteredGroups.value.reduce((total, group) => total + group.items.length, 0))
const attentionCount = computed(() => props.depositPools.length + props.interpretations.length)
const domainPalettes = [
  { solid: '#047857', bright: '#6ee7b7', dark: '#0b2c25', light: '#ecfdf5', border: '#a7f3d0' },
  { solid: '#92400e', bright: '#fcd34d', dark: '#30230f', light: '#fffbeb', border: '#fcd34d' },
  { solid: '#0369a1', bright: '#7dd3fc', dark: '#102b3f', light: '#eff6ff', border: '#93c5fd' },
  { solid: '#6d28d9', bright: '#c4b5fd', dark: '#251a3b', light: '#f5f3ff', border: '#c4b5fd' },
  { solid: '#be123c', bright: '#fda4af', dark: '#361625', light: '#fff1f2', border: '#fda4af' },
]
const domainPalette = (domain: string) => {
  const index = props.groups.findIndex(group => group.domain === domain)
  const tone = domainPalettes[index < 0 ? 0 : (index + 1) % domainPalettes.length]
  return {
    '--gov-solid': tone.solid,
    '--gov-bright': tone.bright,
    '--gov-dark': tone.dark,
    '--gov-light': tone.light,
    '--gov-border': tone.border,
  }
}

// Per-domain accent so the section headers (Regulatory Configuration, Credit &
// Capital, Liquidity & Rates, Monitoring & Stress ...) read as distinct, coloured
// bands instead of dim grey text. Full literal class strings so Tailwind JIT keeps them.
const ACCENTS = [
  { bar: 'bg-amber-400',   text: 'text-amber-300',   pill: 'border-amber-400/40 bg-amber-400/10 text-amber-200',     card: 'hover:border-amber-400/50' },
  { bar: 'bg-emerald-400', text: 'text-emerald-300', pill: 'border-emerald-400/40 bg-emerald-400/10 text-emerald-200', card: 'hover:border-emerald-400/50' },
  { bar: 'bg-sky-400',     text: 'text-sky-300',     pill: 'border-sky-400/40 bg-sky-400/10 text-sky-200',           card: 'hover:border-sky-400/50' },
  { bar: 'bg-violet-400',  text: 'text-violet-300',  pill: 'border-violet-400/40 bg-violet-400/10 text-violet-200',  card: 'hover:border-violet-400/50' },
  { bar: 'bg-rose-400',    text: 'text-rose-300',    pill: 'border-rose-400/40 bg-rose-400/10 text-rose-200',        card: 'hover:border-rose-400/50' },
  { bar: 'bg-teal-400',    text: 'text-teal-300',    pill: 'border-teal-400/40 bg-teal-400/10 text-teal-200',        card: 'hover:border-teal-400/50' },
]
const accent = (i: number) => ACCENTS[i % ACCENTS.length]
</script>

    haystack(s) { return [s.label, s.key, this.plain(s.description), s.in_force ? s.in_force.value : ''].join(' ').toLowerCase() },
    sinceText(s) {

  },
  computed: {
    errorMessage() {
      return this.errors.governance || Object.values(this.errors)[0] || null
    },
    areas() {
      const list = AREAS.map(a => ({ ...a, settings: this.settings.filter(s => a.keys.includes(s.key)) }))
      const other = this.settings.filter(s => !KNOWN.includes(s.key))
      if (other.length) list.push({ key: 'other', label: 'Other', description: 'Settings not yet placed in an area.', settings: other })
      return list
    },
    shownAreas() {
      const term = this.search.trim().toLowerCase()
      return this.areas.map((a, index) => ({ ...a, index, shown: a.settings.filter(s => !term || this.haystack(s).includes(term)) }))
        .filter(a => (this.selected === 'all' || a.key === this.selected) && a.shown.length)
    },
    shownCount() {
      return this.shownAreas.reduce((n, a) => n + a.shown.length, 0)
    },
    attention() {
      const term = this.search.trim().toLowerCase()
      return this.settings.filter(s => (!s.in_force || this.pendingRows(s).length) && (!term || this.haystack(s).includes(term)))
    },
    pendingCount() {
      return this.settings.reduce((n, s) => n + s.rows.filter(r => r.state === 'PROPOSED').length, 0)
    },
    upcomingCount() {
      return this.settings.reduce((n, s) => n + s.rows.filter(r => r.state === 'UPCOMING').length, 0)
    },
    noValueCount() {
      return this.settings.filter(s => !s.in_force).length
    },
    views() {
      return [
        { id: 'areas', label: 'Settings by area', icon: 'cogs', count: this.settings.length },
        { id: 'attention', label: 'Needs attention', icon: 'exclamation-triangle', count: this.settings.filter(s => !s.in_force || this.pendingRows(s).length).length },
      ]
    },
  },
  watch: {
    // keep the open setting in step with the page after a proposal or an approval
    settings() {
      if (this.detail) this.detail = this.settings.find(s => s.key === this.detail.key) || null
    },
  },
  methods: {
    palette(i) { return PALETTES[i % PALETTES.length] },
    areaOf(s) { return (this.areas.find(a => a.settings.some(x => x.key === s.key)) || {}).label || '' },
    haystack(s) { return [s.label, s.key, this.plain(s.description), s.in_force ? s.in_force.value : ''].join(' ').toLowerCase() },
    sinceText(s) {
      const since = this.$filters.since(s.in_force.effective_from)
      return since === 'the seeded default' ? 'The seeded default' : 'From ' + since
    },
    // Specification references are for the build team, not the screen.
    plain(text) {
      return String(text || '')
        .replace(/\s*\((?:spec v\d+ section [\d.]+[^)]*|O\d+|decision D\d+)\)/g, '')
        .replace(/\s*Agreed as decision D\d+\./g, '')
        .replace(/\s*Open choice O\d+[^.]*\./g, '')
        .replace(/\s*Decided ([^(]*?) \(O\d+\):/g, ' Decided $1:')
        .trim()
    },
    cardFor(option) { return this.methodCards.find(c => c.key === option) || null },
    pendingRows(s) { return s.rows.filter(r => r.state === 'PROPOSED' || r.state === 'UPCOMING') },
    hasPending(s) { return s.rows.some(r => r.state === 'PROPOSED') },
    canApprove(r) { return this.adminOverride || (r.proposer_id !== null && r.proposer_id !== this.userId) },
    isInForce(option) { return Boolean(this.proposing?.in_force) && option === this.proposing.in_force.value },
    stateLabel(state) { return { IN_FORCE: 'In force', PAST: 'Past', UPCOMING: 'Upcoming', PROPOSED: 'Awaiting approval' }[state] || state },
    stateClass(state) { return state === 'IN_FORCE' ? 'maiic-badge maiic-badge-green' : state === 'PROPOSED' ? 'maiic-badge maiic-badge-gold' : 'maiic-badge maiic-badge-grey' },
    openDetail(s) { this.openCard = null; this.detail = s },
    openPropose(s) {
      this.proposing = s
      this.form = { ...blank(this.asOf), key: s.key }
      this.showModal = true
    },
    closeModal() {
      if (this.processing) return
      this.showModal = false
      this.proposing = null
      this.form = blank(this.asOf)
    },
    save() {
      this.processing = true
      this.$inertia.post(this.route('eir-governance.propose'), this.form, {
        preserveScroll: true,
        onFinish: () => { this.processing = false },
        onSuccess: () => { this.showModal = false; this.proposing = null; this.form = blank(this.asOf) },
      })
    },
    approve(r) {
      if (!this.canApprove(r)) return
      this.processing = true
      this.$inertia.post(this.route('eir-governance.approve', r.id), {}, { preserveScroll: true, onFinish: () => { this.processing = false } })
    },
  },
}
</script>

<?php

namespace App\Services\Ifrs9;

use App\Models\InternalGradeProfile;
use App\Services\AuditLoggerService;
use Illuminate\Support\Facades\DB;
use PhpOffice\PhpSpreadsheet\IOFactory;
use RuntimeException;

/**
 * The S&P internal grading of MAIIC's ECL model, loaded as an internal grading
 * profile (13 October 2026). The December 2025 model (MAIIC & FInES ECL Model -
 * 14th December 2025_Final.xlsx) carries it on two sheets, and any later model
 * built from the same template does too:
 *
 *  - "ASS1-Internal Grades": the group's ten credit grades, each with its
 *    description, its mapping to an S&P rating, its broad grade and its PD range;
 *  - "PDs-S&P": S&P's average cumulative default rates for the region (the
 *    December 2025 model uses Table 25, Emerging Markets 1981-2024), by S&P
 *    rating and time horizon 1 to 10 years, each row tied to an internal grade
 *    by the grade's combined label.
 *
 * A grade with no row of cumulative PDs on the second sheet (in the December 2025
 * model grades 7, CCC+, and 9, CC) is reported and left out rather than given a
 * curve the model does not have. The profile is created as a draft: it changes no
 * PD until someone activates it on Internal Grades.
 */
class SpGradesImportService
{
    public const GRADES_SHEET = 'ASS1-Internal Grades';
    public const PDS_SHEET = 'PDs-S&P';

    /** @return array{source:array,grades:list<array>,skipped:list<string>,max_tenor:int} */
    public function read(string $path): array
    {
        $reader = IOFactory::createReaderForFile($path);
        $reader->setReadDataOnly(true);
        $reader->setLoadSheetsOnly([self::GRADES_SHEET, self::PDS_SHEET]);
        $book = $reader->load($path);
        $grades = $book->getSheetByName(self::GRADES_SHEET);
        $pds = $book->getSheetByName(self::PDS_SHEET);
        if (! $grades || ! $pds) {
            throw new RuntimeException('The workbook needs the sheets "' . self::GRADES_SHEET . '" and "' . self::PDS_SHEET . '", as the ECL model has them.');
        }

        // the grades: number, description, S&P mapping, broad grade, combined label, PD range
        $out = [];
        $broad = null;
        foreach ($grades->toArray(null, true, false, false) as $r) {
            if (! is_numeric($r[0] ?? null) || trim((string) ($r[4] ?? '')) === '') {
                continue;
            }
            $broad = trim((string) ($r[3] ?? '')) ?: $broad;
            $out[trim((string) $r[4])] = ['grade_code' => (string) (int) $r[0], 'description' => trim((string) $r[1]), 'sp_rating' => trim((string) $r[2]),
                'broad' => $broad, 'label' => trim((string) $r[4]),
                'lower' => is_numeric($r[5] ?? null) ? (float) $r[5] : null, 'upper' => is_numeric($r[6] ?? null) ? (float) $r[6] : null, 'pds' => []];
        }
        if ($out === []) {
            throw new RuntimeException('No grade was found on "' . self::GRADES_SHEET . '": each row needs the grade number in column A and its combined label in column E.');
        }

        // the cumulative PDs: the header row names the horizons; each row names its internal grade
        $rows = $pds->toArray(null, true, false, false);
        $years = null;
        $source = ['provider' => null, 'link' => null, 'table' => null, 'title' => null, 'region' => null, 'note' => null];
        foreach ($rows as $i => $r) {
            $c1 = trim((string) ($r[1] ?? ''));
            $c2 = trim((string) ($r[2] ?? ''));
            if ($c2 === 'Data Source Provider:' || (string) ($r[2] ?? '') === 'Data Source Provider:') {
                $source['provider'] = trim((string) ($r[5] ?? ''));
            } elseif ($c2 === 'Report link:') {
                $source['link'] = trim((string) ($r[5] ?? ''));
            } elseif (stripos($c1, 'Table') === 0 && $source['table'] === null) {
                $source['table'] = $c1;
            } elseif (stripos($c1, 'Cumulative Default') !== false) {
                $source['title'] = $c1;
            } elseif ($c1 === 'S&P Rating' && $c2 === 'Internal Grade') {
                $years = [];
                foreach ($r as $col => $v) {
                    if ($col >= 3 && is_numeric($v)) {
                        $years[$col] = (int) $v;
                    }
                }
                $source['region'] = trim((string) ($rows[$i - 1][1] ?? '')) ?: null;
            } elseif ($years !== null && $c2 !== '' && isset($out[$c2])) {
                foreach ($years as $col => $year) {
                    if (is_numeric($r[$col] ?? null)) {
                        $out[$c2]['pds'][$year] = (float) $r[$col];
                    }
                }
                $out[$c2]['sp_row'] = $c1 !== '' ? $c1 : null;
            } elseif (stripos($c1, 'Report Extract') !== false) {
                $source['note'] = $c1;
            }
        }
        if ($years === null) {
            throw new RuntimeException('"' . self::PDS_SHEET . '" has no header row with "S&P Rating" and "Internal Grade" and the horizons 1, 2, 3 ...');
        }

        $grades = [];
        $skipped = [];
        foreach ($out as $g) {
            if ($g['pds'] === []) {
                $skipped[] = "Grade {$g['grade_code']} ({$g['sp_rating']}) has no row of cumulative PDs on \"" . self::PDS_SHEET . '"; it is left out.';
                continue;
            }
            ksort($g['pds']);
            $grades[] = $g;
        }
        usort($grades, fn ($a, $b) => (int) $a['grade_code'] <=> (int) $b['grade_code']);

        return ['source' => $source, 'grades' => $grades, 'skipped' => $skipped, 'max_tenor' => $years === [] ? 0 : max($years)];
    }

    /** A draft profile from the workbook; the name must be new. */
    public function import(string $path, string $fileName, string $name, ?int $userId = null): InternalGradeProfile
    {
        $r = $this->read($path);
        if ($r['grades'] === []) {
            throw new RuntimeException('The workbook carries no grade with cumulative PDs.');
        }
        if (InternalGradeProfile::where('name', $name)->exists()) {
            throw new RuntimeException("A grading profile named \"{$name}\" exists already; choose another name.");
        }
        $s = $r['source'];
        $description = trim(implode(' ', array_filter([
            ($s['provider'] ?: 'S&P') . ' ' . ($s['title'] ?: 'average cumulative default rates') . ($s['region'] ? ', ' . $s['region'] : '') . ($s['table'] ? ' (' . $s['table'] . ')' : '') . '.',
            $s['note'] ? $s['note'] . '.' : null,
            'Loaded from ' . $fileName . ' (sheets ' . self::GRADES_SHEET . ' and ' . self::PDS_SHEET . ').',
            $s['link'] ? 'Source: ' . $s['link'] : null,
            $r['skipped'] !== [] ? 'Left out: ' . implode(' ', $r['skipped']) : null,
        ])));

        return DB::transaction(function () use ($r, $name, $description, $fileName, $userId) {
            $profile = InternalGradeProfile::create(['name' => $name, 'description' => $description, 'max_tenor_years' => max(1, $r['max_tenor']), 'is_active' => false]);
            foreach ($r['grades'] as $g) {
                $m = $profile->mappings()->create([
                    'grade_code' => $g['grade_code'], 'grade_name' => $g['label'], 'sp_rating' => $g['sp_rating'],
                    'rbm_class' => $g['broad'], 'lower_bound' => $g['lower'], 'upper_bound' => $g['upper'],
                ]);
                $m->tenorPds()->createMany(array_map(fn ($year, $pd) => ['tenor_years' => $year, 'pd_probability' => $pd], array_keys($g['pds']), $g['pds']));
            }
            AuditLoggerService::log('Internal Grades Imported (S&P)', 'internal_grade_profiles', $profile->id, ['new_values' => [
                'file' => $fileName, 'profile' => $name, 'grades' => count($r['grades']), 'skipped' => $r['skipped'], 'source' => $r['source'], 'user' => $userId]]);

            return $profile;
        });
    }
}

    {
        return Inertia::render('InternalGrading/Index', [
            'profiles' => InternalGradeProfile::withCount('mappings')

                ->get(),
            'portfolios' => LoanPortfolio::select('id', 'name')->orderBy('name')->get(),

            'grades' => $profile->mappings()
                ->with('tenorPds')
                ->orderBy('grade_code')
                ->get(),

        ]);
    }

        ]);

<script setup>
import { ref } from 'vue'
import { router } from '@inertiajs/vue3'
import AppLayout from '@/Layouts/AppLayout.vue'
import GradesPdMatrix from './GradesPdMatrix.vue'
import axios from 'axios'
import '@fortawesome/fontawesome-free/css/all.css';

defineProps(
    { profiles: Array,
        portfolios: Array,
        sectors: Array
    }
     )

const showModal = ref(false)
const sp = ref({ open: false, file: null, name: '', preview: null, error: null, busy: false })
const openSp = () => { sp.value = { open: true, file: null, name: 'S&P Emerging Markets (ECL model, December 2025)', preview: null, error: null, busy: false } }
const spFile = (e) => { sp.value.file = e.target.files[0] || null; sp.value.preview = null; sp.value.error = null }
const pctTxt = (v) => (v === null || v === undefined) ? '-' : (Number(v) * 100).toFixed(2) + '%'
const previewSp = async () => {
    sp.value.busy = true; sp.value.error = null
    const fd = new FormData(); fd.append('file', sp.value.file)
    try {
        const { data } = await axios.post(route('internal-grading.import-sp.preview'), fd)
        sp.value.preview = data
    } catch (e) {
        sp.value.error = e.response?.data?.message || 'The workbook could not be read.'
    } finally { sp.value.busy = false }
}
const importSp = () => {
    sp.value.busy = true
    router.post(route('internal-grading.import-sp'), { file: sp.value.file, name: sp.value.name }, {
        forceFormData: true, preserveScroll: true,
        onSuccess: () => { sp.value.open = false },
        onFinish: () => { sp.value.busy = false },
    })
}
const showMatrix = ref(false)
const selectedProfile = ref(null)
const matrixGrades = ref([])
const matrixMaxTenor = ref(0)
const showLoanBookModal = ref(false)


const form = ref({
    name: '',
    description: '',
    max_tenor_years: 5,
})
const editingId = ref(null)
const formErrors = ref({})

const openCreateProfile = () => {
    editingId.value = null
    formErrors.value = {}
    form.value = { name: '', description: '', max_tenor_years: 5 }
    showModal.value = true
}

const openEditProfile = (profile) => {
    editingId.value = profile.id
    formErrors.value = {}
    form.value = { name: profile.name, description: profile.description || '', max_tenor_years: profile.max_tenor_years }
    showModal.value = true
}

const deleteProfile = (profile) => {
    if (!confirm(`Delete the profile ${profile.name} and its ${profile.mappings_count || 0} grade(s)? This cannot be undone.`)) return
    router.delete(route('internal-grading.profile.destroy', profile.id), { preserveScroll: true })
}

const goToGrades = (id) => {
    router.visit(route('internal-grading.grades', id))
}

const viewMatrix = (id) => {
    router.visit(route('internal-grading.matrix.view', id))
}

const toggleStatus = (profile) => {
    router.put(
        route('internal-grading.profile.toggle', profile.id),
        {},
        { preserveScroll: true }
    )
}

const submit = () => {
    const opts = {
        preserveScroll: true,
        onSuccess: () => {
            showModal.value = false
            editingId.value = null
            form.value = { name: '', description: '', max_tenor_years: 5 }
        },
        onError: (e) => { formErrors.value = e },
    }
    if (editingId.value) {
        router.put(route('internal-grading.profile.update', editingId.value), form.value, opts)
    } else {
        router.post(route('internal-grading.profile.store'), form.value, opts)
    }
}

const openMatrix = async (profile) => {
  const { data } = await axios.get(
    route('internal-grading.matrix.view', profile.id)
  )

  selectedProfile.value = data.profile
  matrixGrades.value = data.grades
  matrixMaxTenor.value = data.maxTenor
  showMatrix.value = true
}

const handleManage = (profile) => {
    if (profile.is_active) {
        return
    }

    goToGrades(profile.id)
}


const loanBookForm = ref({
    reporting_period: '',
    scope: '',
    portfolio_id: null,
    sector_code: null,
})

const openLoanBookModal = (profile) => {
    selectedProfile.value = profile
    showLoanBookModal.value = true

    // reset form
    loanBookForm.value = {
        reporting_period: '',
        scope: '',
        portfolio_id: null,
        sector_code: null,
    }
}


const updateLoanBookWithPD = () => {
    router.post(
        route('internal-grading.loanbook.updateWithPD'),
        {
            profile_id: selectedProfile.value.id,
            reporting_period: loanBookForm.value.reporting_period,
            scope: loanBookForm.value.scope,
            portfolio_id: loanBookForm.value.portfolio_id,
            sector_code: loanBookForm.value.sector_code,
        },
        {
            preserveScroll: true,
            onSuccess: () => {
                showLoanBookModal.value = false
            }
        }
    )
}

const activeClass = 'bg-maiic-100 text-maiic-700'
const draftClass = 'bg-amber-100 text-amber-700'
</script>
<template>
  <div
    v-if="show"
    class="fixed inset-0 z-50 flex items-center justify-center"
    @click.self="$emit('close')"

<script setup>
defineProps({
  show: Boolean,
  profile: Object,
  grades: Array,
  maxTenor: Number
})

function formatPd(value) {
  return (Number(value) * 100).toFixed(2) + '%'
}

// colour steps for a cumulative PD; light and dark variants
const bands = [
  { max: 0.005, label: 'under 0.5%', cls: 'bg-emerald-50 text-emerald-800 dark:bg-emerald-900/30 dark:text-emerald-200' },
  { max: 0.02, label: '0.5% to 2%', cls: 'bg-lime-50 text-lime-800 dark:bg-lime-900/30 dark:text-lime-200' },
  { max: 0.10, label: '2% to 10%', cls: 'bg-amber-50 text-amber-800 dark:bg-amber-900/30 dark:text-amber-200' },
  { max: 0.30, label: '10% to 30%', cls: 'bg-orange-100 text-orange-800 dark:bg-orange-900/40 dark:text-orange-200' },
  { max: 0.9999, label: '30% to under 100%', cls: 'bg-red-100 text-red-800 dark:bg-red-900/40 dark:text-red-200' },
  { max: Infinity, label: '100% (default)', cls: 'bg-red-200 font-semibold text-red-900 dark:bg-red-900/70 dark:text-red-100' },
]
function heat(pd) {
  const v = Number(pd)
  return (bands.find(b => v < b.max) || bands[bands.length - 1]).cls
}

// the broad grade's colour: investment grade green, monitoring amber, special monitoring orange, default red
function broadTone(broad) {
  const b = (broad || '').toLowerCase()
  if (b.includes('investment')) return { badge: 'bg-emerald-100 text-emerald-800 dark:bg-emerald-900/50 dark:text-emerald-200', pill: 'bg-emerald-50 text-emerald-700 dark:bg-emerald-900/30 dark:text-emerald-200' }
  if (b.includes('special')) return { badge: 'bg-orange-100 text-orange-800 dark:bg-orange-900/50 dark:text-orange-200', pill: 'bg-orange-50 text-orange-700 dark:bg-orange-900/30 dark:text-orange-200' }
  if (b.includes('monitoring')) return { badge: 'bg-amber-100 text-amber-800 dark:bg-amber-900/50 dark:text-amber-200', pill: 'bg-amber-50 text-amber-700 dark:bg-amber-900/30 dark:text-amber-200' }
  if (b.includes('default') || b.includes('impaired')) return { badge: 'bg-red-100 text-red-800 dark:bg-red-900/50 dark:text-red-200', pill: 'bg-red-50 text-red-700 dark:bg-red-900/30 dark:text-red-200' }
  return { badge: 'bg-gray-100 text-gray-700 dark:bg-slate-700 dark:text-slate-200', pill: 'bg-gray-100 text-gray-700 dark:bg-slate-700 dark:text-slate-200' }
}
</script>

import { ref } from 'vue';
import { router } from '@inertiajs/vue3';

/**
 * Light, dark, or follow the device (spec v4 section 11.5).
 *
 * Tailwind runs in class mode, so the whole system is dark when the `dark`
 * class is on <html> and light when it is not; nothing else decides the
 * theme. The first paint is set by the four-line script in app.blade.php,
 * which reads `maiic.theme` from the browser before the page renders; this
 * composable mirrors that state in one module-level ref, so the top-bar
 * switch, the profile page and any other consumer stay in step. The choice
 * is kept in the browser (so the first paint is right) and on the user's
 * record (so it follows the user to another machine).
 */
const STORAGE_KEY = 'maiic.theme';
export const THEMES = ['light', 'dark', 'system'];

function stored() {
    try {
        const v = localStorage.getItem(STORAGE_KEY);
        return THEMES.includes(v) ? v : 'system';
    } catch (e) {
        return 'system';
    }
}

function deviceDark() {
    return typeof window !== 'undefined' && window.matchMedia && window.matchMedia('(prefers-color-scheme: dark)').matches;
}

const preference = ref(stored());
const isDark = ref(typeof document !== 'undefined' && document.documentElement.classList.contains('dark'));

function apply(pref, tellServer) {
    preference.value = pref;
    const dark = pref === 'dark' || (pref === 'system' && deviceDark());
    isDark.value = dark;
    if (typeof document !== 'undefined') document.documentElement.classList.toggle('dark', dark);
    try {
        localStorage.setItem(STORAGE_KEY, pref);
    } catch (e) {
        /* storage unavailable: the theme still applies for the session */
    }
    if (tellServer) {
        try {
            router.post(route('profile.theme'), { theme: pref }, { preserveScroll: true, preserveState: true, only: [] });
        } catch (e) {
            /* no route on this page (login): the browser value stands */
        }

- **Grade 1 (AAA) is riskier than grades 2 and 3.** The workbook ties grade 1 to S&P's "Investment Grade" average row, so it starts at 0.08% and reaches 1.44% by year 10. S&P's own AAA row is zero.
- **Grades 2 and 3 look wrong.** Grade 2 (AA) is 0% in every year, and grade 3 (A) stays at 0.03% in every year.

The profile is a draft and nothing reads it yet, so no ECL has changed. I'd raise those three points with Finance or Dr Thom before activating it.

    public function test_method_b_derives_the_carrying_amount_from_the_ledger_and_keeps_the_stored_figure_beside_it(): void
    {
        $r = $this->service()->build('2024-07', '2024-08', 'B', 1, 2);
        $this->assertSame('BUILT', $r['status']);
        $this->assertSame(['2024-07' => 1, '2024-08' => 1], array_map(fn ($p) => $p['rows'], $r['periods']));
        $jul = DB::table('loan_books')->where('reporting_period', '2024-07')->first();
        $this->assertSame('104420000005', $jul->contract_id);
        $this->assertSame('000104420000005', $jul->external_identity_id);
        $this->assertEquals(10000000, $jul->carrying_amount);
        $this->assertEquals(10000000, $jul->disbursed);
        $this->assertNull($jul->stored_carrying_amount);
        $this->assertSame('B', $jul->build_method);
        $this->assertNull($jul->build_flag);
        $this->assertSame('MAIIC Agricultural Loans', $jul->product_group);
        $this->assertEquals(20.20, $jul->interest_rate); // no run, no set-up: the account master
        $aug = DB::table('loan_books')->where('reporting_period', '2024-08')->first();
        $this->assertEquals(8000000, $aug->carrying_amount);   // 10m + 1m interest - 3m receipt; the deleted row ignored
        $this->assertEquals(1000000, $aug->interest_to_date);
        $this->assertEquals(3000000, $aug->repayments);
        $this->assertEquals(8000001, $aug->stored_carrying_amount);
        $this->assertStringContainsString('differs from the stored run by -1.00', $aug->build_flag);
        $this->assertEquals(21.5, $aug->interest_rate);        // the rate charged, from the run
        $this->assertEquals(500000, $aug->arrears_30_to_90);
        $this->assertSame(61, (int) $aug->overdue_days);        // 1 Jul to 31 Aug under the directive basis
        $this->assertSame('2024-07-01', $aug->overdue_principal_date);
        $this->assertSame(24, (int) $aug->tenor);
        $this->assertEquals(2000000, $aug->commitments);
        $this->assertEquals(10000000, $aug->ead);
        $basis = json_decode($aug->build_basis, true);
        $this->assertSame('P2_08:5000', $basis['stored_run']);
        $this->assertSame(3, $basis['postings']); // the deleted row is not a posting
        $this->assertSame('BUILT', DB::table('loan_book_builds')->first()->status);
        $this->assertSame(1, DB::table('audit_logs')->where('action', 'Loan Book Built')->count());
    }

I'll make the link jump straight to the table. A link can't target a table inside someone else's page, but modern browsers support a text-fragment link (`#:~:text=...`). It opens the page already scrolled to, and highlighting, the table's title, "Average Cumulative Default Rates For Corporates By Region". Chrome and Edge both support it.

def rep(a,b):
    global s; assert s.count(a)==1, a[:60]; s=s.replace(a,b)
rep("""            <span class="font-semibold text-gray-600 dark:text-slate-300">Link given in the workbook:</span>
            <a :href="source.url" target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer" class="ml-1 inline-flex items-center gap-1 break-all text-maiic-700 underline decoration-dotted underline-offset-2 hover:text-maiic-800 dark:text-emerald-300 dark:hover:text-emerald-200">{{ source.label }} <i class="fas fa-external-link-alt text-[10px]"></i></a>""",
"""            <span class="font-semibold text-gray-600 dark:text-slate-300">S&amp;P table:</span>
            <a :href="source.tableUrl" target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer" class="ml-1 inline-flex items-center gap-1 break-all text-maiic-700 underline decoration-dotted underline-offset-2 hover:text-maiic-800 dark:text-emerald-300 dark:hover:text-emerald-200" :title="source.url">{{ source.tableLabel }} <i class="fas fa-external-link-alt text-[10px]"></i></a>
            <span class="block text-[11px] text-gray-400 dark:text-slate-500">Opens the S&amp;P page given in the workbook ({{ source.label }}) at the table's title; the page may ask for an S&amp;P login first.</span>""")
rep("""  return { text, url, label, leftOut }""","""  // a text-fragment link opens the page at the table's own title (Chrome, Edge); the title is the one the
  // workbook names, without its period, which differs between S&P's annual studies
  const t = (props.profile?.description || '').match(/(Average Cumulative Default Rates[^(.,]*)/)
  const tableTitle = t ? t[1].trim() : null
  const tableNo = ((props.profile?.description || '').match(/\\((Table \\d+)\\)/) || [])[1]
  const region = ((props.profile?.description || '').match(/\\),\\s*([A-Z][A-Za-z ]+?)\\s*\\(Table/) || [])[1]
  const tableUrl = url && tableTitle ? url.split('#')[0] + '#:~:text=' + encodeURIComponent(tableTitle) : url
  const tableLabel = tableTitle ? [tableNo, tableTitle, region].filter(Boolean).join(' - ') : label
  return { text, url, label, leftOut, tableUrl, tableLabel }""")
open(p,'w',encoding='utf-8').write(s)
EOF

````
--==============================================================================
-- MAIIC E-Banker: FOLLOW-UP EXTRACTS, PACK 8  |  Dupleix Institute  |  13 October 2026
--==============================================================================
-- Read-only queries, numbered in run order, each with the file name to save
-- it under. Nothing here writes to the database.
--
-- Pack 7 is complete (the review is in the Pack 4 folder, Pack 7\Export
-- Results\Results review). It showed that CUMVOUCH_BK240824 gives the full
-- history before the migration for 41 of the 78 term loans, and that Ifracon
-- and Tapempha were renumbered at the migration. Two things are left that the
-- database itself can answer:
--
--   RUN 1a, 1b  the older ledger copy (CUMVOUCH_BAK) keeps its loans on
--               accounts 000100750000001 to 000100750000084 plus
--               000101270000001 and 000101350000001, which are not in the
--               account extracts we hold; these two queries bring their
--               account and loan master rows, so they can be linked to
--               today's loans
--   RUN 2, 3    names only (no data): any table that may hold the migration
--               working (take-on, opening balances, conversion), and any
--               column that links an old account number to a new one
--
-- Four small grid exports. Please save the results in the Pack 4 folder on
-- OneDrive, in the subfolder Pack 8\Export Results.
--==============================================================================


--==============================================================================
-- RUN 0  |  session settings  |  run once, first, in THIS worksheet
-- The pack 4 to 7 files still came out with dates as m/d/yyyy. These two
-- lines must be run in the same worksheet (same connection tab) as the
-- queries; each tab is its own session.
ALTER SESSION SET NLS_DATE_FORMAT = 'YYYY-MM-DD HH24:MI:SS';
ALTER SESSION SET NLS_NUMERIC_CHARACTERS = '.,';

-- RUN 0 check  |  do not export, just look at the grid
-- It must show a date like 2026-10-13 09:15:00 and the number 1234567.89.
-- If it shows 13-OCT-26 or 10/13/2026, run the two lines above again here.
SELECT SYSDATE AS today_as_text, 1234567.89 AS a_number FROM dual;

-- If the grid is right but the CSV still shows 10/13/2026, the export is
-- re-formatting it: Tools > Preferences > Database > NLS > Date Format =
-- YYYY-MM-DD HH24:MI:SS (type NLS in the search box at the top left of the
-- Preferences window if Database is not visible). Set once, it sticks.


--==============================================================================
-- RUN 1  |  the accounts behind the older ledger copy

-- RUN 1a  |  save as CV_05a_old_accounts_master.csv
-- The account master rows for the 75 loan accounts in CUMVOUCH_BAK (and any
-- other account in the 00010075 block): scheme,
-- GL, customer, name, open date, status, and the old account number.
SELECT a.*
FROM   acmaster a
WHERE  a.new_ac_number LIKE '00010075%'
OR     a.new_ac_number IN ('000101270000001', '000101350000001')
ORDER  BY a.new_ac_number;
-- Expect 75 to 86 rows. If none come back, the block is not in ACMASTER:
-- please tell us, and where those accounts are kept.

-- RUN 1b  |  save as CV_05b_old_accounts_loan_master.csv
-- The loan master rows for the same accounts: sanctioned amount, dates,
-- tenor and rate, so each old loan can be matched to its loan today.
SELECT lm.*
FROM   acloanmaster lm
WHERE  lm.new_ac_number LIKE '00010075%'
OR     lm.new_ac_number IN ('000101270000001', '000101350000001')
ORDER  BY lm.new_ac_number;


--==============================================================================
-- RUN 2  |  save as CV_06_migration_tables_probe.csv
-- Names and row counts only, no data: tables that may hold the take-on
-- working of July 2024 (the three opening postings per loan: amount
-- disbursed, interest charged, amount recovered). The opening interest
-- differs from the old ledger on 74 of 78 loans; the working would explain it.
SELECT t.owner, t.table_name, t.num_rows, t.last_analyzed
FROM   all_tables t
WHERE  t.owner NOT IN ('SYS', 'SYSTEM', 'XDB', 'MDSYS', 'CTXSYS', 'ORDSYS', 'OLAPSYS', 'WMSYS', 'APEX_040200', 'DVSYS', 'LBACSYS', 'AUDSYS', 'GSMADMIN_INTERNAL', 'OJVMSYS', 'DBSNMP', 'OUTLN')
AND   (t.table_name LIKE '%TAKE%'
OR     t.table_name LIKE '%OPEN%'
OR     t.table_name LIKE '%CONV%'
OR     t.table_name LIKE '%LEGACY%'
OR     t.table_name LIKE '%MIGR%'
OR     t.table_name LIKE '%UPLOAD%'
OR     t.table_name LIKE '%IMPORT%'
OR     t.table_name LIKE '%OLD%')
ORDER  BY t.owner, t.table_name;


--==============================================================================
-- RUN 3  |  save as CV_07_account_mapping_columns_probe.csv
-- Names only, no data: any column in any table that may link an old account
-- number to a new one (Ifracon moved from 000104430000059 to
-- 000104430000062 and Tapempha from 000104460000058 to 000104430000061 at
-- the migration; there may be others).
SELECT c.owner, c.table_name, c.column_name, c.data_type
FROM   all_tab_columns c
WHERE  c.owner NOT IN ('SYS', 'SYSTEM', 'XDB', 'MDSYS', 'CTXSYS', 'ORDSYS', 'OLAPSYS', 'WMSYS', 'APEX_040200', 'DVSYS', 'LBACSYS', 'AUDSYS', 'GSMADMIN_INTERNAL', 'OJVMSYS', 'DBSNMP', 'OUTLN')
AND   (c.column_name LIKE '%OLD%AC%'

# MAIIC E-Banker extracts, pack 7: results review

Dupleix Institute. Review of the six files in this Export Results folder, received 13 October 2026 at 10:00.

## 1. Where we are

All six files are in and complete. Each row count matches the count by year from pack 6 exactly; every file has all 84 ledger columns; no file is a copy of another.

| Run | File | Rows | Expected | Dates |
|---|---|---:|---:|---|
| RUN 1a | CV_04a1_bk240824_2018_2022.csv | 3,530 | 3,530 | 2018-05-08 to 2022-12-31 |

RUN 0 (the date settings) still did not take: dates arrive as m/d/yyyy. The files load as they are.

## 2. What the two copies are

- **CUMVOUCH_BK240824** is a full ledger (bank, payables, income and loans) under today's chart and account numbers. Its loan postings run from 2020 on the MAIIC GLs 1050101 and 1050102, from 2021 on the FInES GLs 1050201 and 1050202, and in 2024 also on the Mega Farm GLs: 3,386 loan postings on 344 loan accounts. 154 of them are dated on or after 31 July 2024, the first two weeks after the migration.
- **CUMVOUCH_BAK** is an older ledger under an earlier chart (loan GLs 1050, 1052, 1053): 2,023 loan postings on 75 loan accounts, 73 of them in the account block 000100750000xxx, which does not appear in the account master extracts we hold.
- The two copies share 10,549 posting ids, but none of the shared ids carries the same account and amount, so the ids come from different sequences and the copies cannot be merged on id.

## 3. Does the old ledger lead into the balances taken on at the migration?

On 31 July 2024 each term loan was taken on in E-Banker with up to three postings: "Opening Account Balance Disbursement amount" (type 301), "Opening interest charge" (303) and "Opening Recover Amount" (305). For the 78 term loans in the July 2024 take-on, against CUMVOUCH_BK240824 up to 30 July 2024:

| | Take-on, 31 Jul 2024 | Old ledger to 30 Jul 2024 | Loans agreeing |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Principal (drawn less recovered) | 5,916,330,548.34 | 5,083,311,268.38 | 41 of 78 |
| Interest | 1,725,540,227.73 | 1,837,507,266.04 | 4 of 78 |

Where the principal differs:

- **41 loans agree exactly.** For these, the old ledger gives the full history before the migration.
- **Ifracon Limited (000104430000062), 627,746,500**: the loan was renumbered at the migration. Before it, it sat on 000104430000059 "INFRACON LIMITED" (opened 9 May 2024, now closed), drawn 362,090,000 on 9 May 2024 (TRF 7777) and 265,656,500 on 18 June 2024 (DISB 4), together exactly the 627,746,500 taken on. Tapempha Medical Care was renumbered the same way (000104460000058 to 000104430000061; principal within 3,400,000).
- **23 loans have the same drawdowns but different repayments** (net 51,576,096). Some offset between two loans of the same customer, for example Nature's Gift Limited, 000104420000010 and 000104420000012, by 31,512,451 each way, a repayment re-allocated at the migration.
- **7 loans have different drawdown totals** (net 63,226,321), for example MUSECO (000104420000005): 405,097,990 taken on against 375,550,000 in the old ledger.
- **6 more loans** (net 193,622,554) have drawdowns or repayments missing from the copy, most of them opened before it starts (for example Edge View Academy, opened March 2020).

Interest agrees on only 4 loans. On 35 more the take-on is higher by about one month's interest (58,687,253 in all): the old system's last interest postings are in June 2024, so the opening interest includes July 2024, accrued at the migration. On one loan it is about two months. On the other 38 the opening interest is 213,572,462 lower in total than the interest the old ledger charged, which suggests it was taken on net of interest already paid; the working behind it would settle that.

## 4. What we need from MAIIC ICT and Finance

1. **How the take-on figures were prepared**: the working (or the migration worksheet) behind the three opening postings per loan, in particular the opening interest on the 38 loans where it is lower than the old ledger's interest, and any other loans renumbered at the migration besides Ifracon and Tapempha.
2. **Renumbered loans**: confirm that 000104430000059 became 000104430000062 (Ifracon) and 000104460000058 became 000104430000061 (Tapempha).
3. **The 000100750000xxx accounts in CUMVOUCH_BAK**: the account master rows for that block (or the mapping to today's account numbers), so the older history can be attached to the right loans. We will send a short query.

# MAIIC E-Banker extracts, pack 8: results review

Dupleix Institute. Review of the files in this Export Results folder, received 13 October 2026 at 16:53.

## 1. Where we are

The four pack 8 files are in. Two of them answer the questions that were asked; the other two show where the answer is kept instead.

| Run | File | Rows | Expected | Result |
|---|---|---:|---:|---|
| RUN 1a | CV_05a_old_accounts_master.csv | 3 | 75 to 86 | Only one account of the 000100750000xxx block is in ACMASTER (see 2) |
| RUN 1b | CV_05b_old_accounts_loan_master.csv | 0 | 75 to 86 | None of the old loans is in ACLOANMASTER |
| RUN 2 | CV_06_migration_tables_probe.csv | 53 tables | names only | Opening-balance and old-ledger tables found (see 3) |
| RUN 3 | CV_07_account_mapping_columns_probe.csv | 47 columns | names only | Two account-mapping tables and a migration staging pair found (see 3) |

RUN 0 (the date settings) did not take again: dates still arrive as m/d/yyyy. The files load as they are.

**The six CV_04 files in this folder are not new.** Four are byte-for-byte the pack 7 files. Two are shorter copies: CV_04b1_bak_2000_2021.csv has 5,980 rows against 7,019 in pack 7, and CV_04b2_bak_2022.csv has 4,465 against 5,639. Every row they hold is in the pack 7 file with the same values; 1,039 and 1,174 rows are simply missing, so these two look like an export that stopped early. We use the pack 7 files and ignore these.

## 2. The old loan accounts are not in today's account master

The older ledger copy (CUMVOUCH_BAK) holds its term loans on 73 accounts from 000100750000001 to 000100750000084, under the earlier loan GL 1050. Of that block, ACMASTER holds one row: 000100750000001, named "Term Loans", customer 1, opened 1 January 2015. It is a control account, not a borrower's loan. The other two accounts asked for are also control accounts: 000101270000001 is GL 1053 Accounts Receivables and 000101350000001 is GL 1052 Prepaid Expenses. ACLOANMASTER has none of them.

So the 72 borrower accounts 000100750000002 to 000100750000084 were removed from E-Banker's masters when the loans were moved onto today's GLs (1050101, 1050102, 1050201, 1050202). The ledger postings survive in CUMVOUCH_BAK; the names and terms that would say which loan each was do not.

Two things that do not give the link, checked so that nobody tries them:

- **OLD_AC_NUMBER in today's account master** is the account's serial number within its GL (000104420000005 carries 5), not the number the loan had before; every value in the account extracts we hold is of that kind.
- **Transfers in CUMVOUCH_BAK** from the old loan accounts go to the bank and cash accounts (block 00010327, GL 1001), which are disbursements and receipts, not transfers to the new loan accounts.

Matching the old loans to today's loans by borrower name or by amount is not safe for a take-on: the link should come from E-Banker's own mapping, which section 3 shows exists.

## 3. Where the migration working and the mapping are kept

From the two probes, the tables worth reading are:

| Table (owner) | Rows | Why it matters |
|---|---:|---|
| VGCBS.ACCOUNT_NO_MAPP | not given | Columns OLD_AC_NUMBER and NEW_OLDACNO: an old-to-new account map |
| VGCBS.NEW_ACMAP | not given | Column EB_OLDACNO: the E-Banker map from old account numbers |
| VGCBS.T_ACCOUNT, VGCBS.T_ACCOUNTBALANCE | not given | Column OLDACCOUNTID: the account and balance tables of the conversion, as loaded from the old system |
| VGCBS.TEMP_MASTER | not given | Column OLD_AC_NUMBER: a staging master |
| VGCBS.OPENING_BAL | 95 | Opening balances; 95 is close to the 78 term loans plus the other balances taken on in July 2024 |
| VGCBS.GL_OPENING_BALANCE_BK240824 | 331 | GL opening balances as at the 24 August 2024 backup |
| VGCBS.GL_OPENING_BALANCE, \_02OCT24, \_120423 | 598, 357, 331 | GL opening balances now, at 2 October 2024 and at 12 April 2023 |
| VGCBS.CUMOVUCH_OLD | 13,359 | A third old ledger copy we have not seen (the name is spelt this way in the database) |
| MAIIC_ORA_LIVE.CRM_ACMASTER_05082024 | not given | The account master as at 5 August 2024, days after the migration |
| VGCBS.G_ACMASTER, ACMASTER_MW, ACMASTER_NF | not given | Other copies of the account master, which may still hold the removed accounts |

The row counts come from the database's statistics of 13 June 2026, so they are approximate; tables with no count have not been analysed.

## 4. What this means for the take-on loans

- The pack 7 result stands: for 41 of the 78 term loans, CUMVOUCH_BK240824 gives the full history before the migration under today's account numbers, and Ifracon and Tapempha were renumbered.
- For the rest, the history before 2024 sits in CUMVOUCH_BAK under accounts that today's masters no longer know. ACCOUNT_NO_MAPP, NEW_ACMAP or T_ACCOUNT should give the link, and OPENING_BAL should show how the three opening postings per loan of 31 July 2024 were prepared, including the opening interest that differs from the old ledger on 74 of the 78 loans.
- Until the link is in, the EIR of a take-on loan stays measured from the migration balance, as now.

## 5. What we will ask for next (pack 9)

1. ACCOUNT_NO_MAPP and NEW_ACMAP in full (they are maps, so small).
2. OPENING_BAL in full (95 rows).
3. T_ACCOUNT and T_ACCOUNTBALANCE: the row counts first, then the rows for loan accounts.
4. The account master rows of the block 000100750000xxx from G_ACMASTER, ACMASTER_MW, ACMASTER_NF, TEMP_MASTER and CRM_ACMASTER_05082024, whichever hold them.
5. CUMOVUCH_OLD: rows by year and by account block, before any full export.
6. GL_OPENING_BALANCE_BK240824 in full (331 rows), to tie the take-on to the GL at the migration.
7. RUN 0 again, and the Preferences setting, so the dates come out as YYYY-MM-DD.

"""Pack 9 run sheet, per-query files, PDF, zip and an unsent .eml draft (nothing is sent)."""
import os, io, zipfile
from email.message import EmailMessage
from email.utils import formatdate, make_msgid
from reportlab.lib.pagesizes import A4
from reportlab.pdfgen import canvas

BASE = r"C:\Users\DELL\OneDrive\2026\Projects\MAIIC\2. Documents from clients\Raw Query Scripts\Query Requests to MAIIC"
PACK4 = os.path.join(BASE, "Received 12 October 2026", "Pack 4")
PACK9 = os.path.join(PACK4, "Pack 9")
DATE = "13 Oct 2026"

SESSION = """ALTER SESSION SET NLS_DATE_FORMAT = 'YYYY-MM-DD HH24:MI:SS';
ALTER SESSION SET NLS_NUMERIC_CHARACTERS = '.,';"""

EXCL = "('SYS', 'SYSTEM', 'XDB', 'MDSYS', 'CTXSYS', 'ORDSYS', 'OLAPSYS', 'WMSYS', 'APEX_040200', 'DVSYS', 'LBACSYS', 'AUDSYS', 'GSMADMIN_INTERNAL', 'OJVMSYS', 'DBSNMP', 'OUTLN')"

# (run id, file name, title, reason, sql)
RUNS = [
    ("RUN 1", "CV_08_table_counts", "row counts of the tables in this pack",
     """Counts only, no data. Run this first: it tells us which of the later
-- runs can be exported in one grid. If a line errors because the table is
-- not there or not visible to you, delete that line and run the rest.""",
     """SELECT 'VGCBS.ACCOUNT_NO_MAPP' AS table_name, COUNT(*) AS row_count FROM vgcbs.account_no_mapp
UNION ALL SELECT 'VGCBS.NEW_ACMAP', COUNT(*) FROM vgcbs.new_acmap
UNION ALL SELECT 'VGCBS.OPENING_BAL', COUNT(*) FROM vgcbs.opening_bal
UNION ALL SELECT 'VGCBS.T_ACCOUNT', COUNT(*) FROM vgcbs.t_account
UNION ALL SELECT 'VGCBS.T_ACCOUNTBALANCE', COUNT(*) FROM vgcbs.t_accountbalance
UNION ALL SELECT 'VGCBS.TEMP_MASTER', COUNT(*) FROM vgcbs.temp_master
UNION ALL SELECT 'VGCBS.G_ACMASTER', COUNT(*) FROM vgcbs.g_acmaster
UNION ALL SELECT 'VGCBS.ACMASTER_MW', COUNT(*) FROM vgcbs.acmaster_mw
UNION ALL SELECT 'VGCBS.ACMASTER_NF', COUNT(*) FROM vgcbs.acmaster_nf
UNION ALL SELECT 'VGCBS.CUMOVUCH_OLD', COUNT(*) FROM vgcbs.cumovuch_old
UNION ALL SELECT 'VGCBS.GL_OPENING_BALANCE_BK240824', COUNT(*) FROM vgcbs.gl_opening_balance_bk240824
UNION ALL SELECT 'MAIIC_ORA_LIVE.CRM_ACMASTER_05082024', COUNT(*) FROM maiic_ora_live.crm_acmaster_05082024;"""),

    ("RUN 2a", "CV_09a_account_no_mapp", "the old-to-new account map",
     """ACCOUNT_NO_MAPP holds OLD_AC_NUMBER and NEW_OLDACNO: the link from an
-- account number before the migration to its number today. In full.""",
     "SELECT m.* FROM vgcbs.account_no_mapp m ORDER BY 1;"),

    ("RUN 2b", "CV_09b_new_acmap", "the E-Banker account map",
     """NEW_ACMAP holds EB_OLDACNO, the old account number against the new one. In full.""",
     "SELECT m.* FROM vgcbs.new_acmap m ORDER BY 1;"),

    ("RUN 3", "CV_10_opening_bal", "the opening balances taken on",
     """OPENING_BAL (about 95 rows): the balances taken on at the migration. We
-- expect the 78 term loans of 31 July 2024 among them; this should show how
-- the three opening postings per loan were prepared, in particular the
-- opening interest, which differs from the old ledger on 74 of the 78 loans.""",
     "SELECT o.* FROM vgcbs.opening_bal o ORDER BY 1;"),

    ("RUN 4a", "CV_11a_t_account", "the conversion's account table",
     """T_ACCOUNT holds OLDACCOUNTID: the accounts as loaded from the old system.
-- In full if RUN 1 shows 50,000 rows or fewer; if more, export only the
-- first 100 rows (add  FETCH FIRST 100 ROWS ONLY  before the semicolon) and tell us.""",
     "SELECT t.* FROM vgcbs.t_account t ORDER BY 1;"),

    ("RUN 4b", "CV_11b_t_accountbalance", "the conversion's balance table",
     """T_ACCOUNTBALANCE holds OLDACCOUNTID and the balances converted. Same rule
-- as RUN 4a for the size.""",
     "SELECT t.* FROM vgcbs.t_accountbalance t ORDER BY 1;"),

    ("RUN 5a", "CV_12a_old_block_g_acmaster", "the old loan accounts in G_ACMASTER",
     """The older ledger copy (CUMVOUCH_BAK) keeps its term loans on accounts
-- 000100750000002 to 000100750000084, which ACMASTER no longer holds (pack 8).
-- These three copies of the account master may still hold them.""",
     "SELECT a.* FROM vgcbs.g_acmaster a WHERE a.new_ac_number LIKE '00010075%' ORDER BY a.new_ac_number;"),

    ("RUN 5b", "CV_12b_old_block_acmaster_mw", "the old loan accounts in ACMASTER_MW", "As RUN 5a.",
     "SELECT a.* FROM vgcbs.acmaster_mw a WHERE a.new_ac_number LIKE '00010075%' ORDER BY a.new_ac_number;"),

    ("RUN 5c", "CV_12c_old_block_acmaster_nf", "the old loan accounts in ACMASTER_NF", "As RUN 5a.",
     "SELECT a.* FROM vgcbs.acmaster_nf a WHERE a.new_ac_number LIKE '00010075%' ORDER BY a.new_ac_number;"),

    ("RUN 5d", "CV_12d_acmaster_05082024_loans", "the account master as at 5 August 2024",
     """CRM_ACMASTER_05082024 is a copy of the account master taken days after the
-- migration: the loan accounts and the old block, as they stood then.""",
     """SELECT a.* FROM maiic_ora_live.crm_acmaster_05082024 a
WHERE  a.new_ac_number LIKE '00010075%'
OR     a.glcode IN ('1050', '1050101', '1050102', '1050103', '1050201', '1050202', '1050203', '1050401')
ORDER  BY a.new_ac_number;"""),

    ("RUN 5e", "CV_12e_temp_master", "the staging master",
     """TEMP_MASTER holds OLD_AC_NUMBER. In full if RUN 1 shows 20,000 rows or
-- fewer; if more, the first 100 rows only, as in RUN 4a.""",
     "SELECT t.* FROM vgcbs.temp_master t ORDER BY 1;"),

    ("RUN 6", "CV_13_cumovuch_old_profile", "a profile of the third old ledger copy",
     """CUMOVUCH_OLD (about 13,359 rows; the name is spelt this way in the
-- database) is a ledger copy we have not seen. Counts by year and account
-- block only, so we can see what it covers before asking for it.""",
     """SELECT EXTRACT(YEAR FROM c.transaction_date) AS yr,
       SUBSTR(c.new_ac_number, 1, 8)           AS account_block,
       COUNT(*)                                 AS row_count,
       MIN(c.transaction_date)                  AS first_date,
       MAX(c.transaction_date)                  AS last_date,
       SUM(c.transamt)                          AS net_amount
FROM   vgcbs.cumovuch_old c
GROUP  BY EXTRACT(YEAR FROM c.transaction_date), SUBSTR(c.new_ac_number, 1, 8)
ORDER  BY 1, 2;"""),

    ("RUN 7", "CV_14_gl_opening_balance_bk240824", "the GL opening balances at the August 2024 backup",
     """GL_OPENING_BALANCE_BK240824 (about 331 rows): the GL balances kept with the
-- 24 August 2024 backup, to tie the loans taken on to the GL at the migration.""",
     "SELECT g.* FROM vgcbs.gl_opening_balance_bk240824 g ORDER BY 1;"),
]

HEAD = f"""--==============================================================================
-- MAIIC E-Banker: FOLLOW-UP EXTRACTS, PACK 9  |  Dupleix Institute  |  {DATE.replace('Oct', 'October')}
--==============================================================================
-- Read-only queries, numbered in run order, each with the file name to save
-- it under. Nothing here writes to the database.
--
-- Pack 8 showed that the loan accounts behind the older ledger copy
-- (CUMVOUCH_BAK, accounts 000100750000002 to 000100750000084) are no longer in
-- ACMASTER or ACLOANMASTER, and that OLD_AC_NUMBER in today's account master
-- is a serial number within the GL, not the number a loan had before. It also
-- found the tables where the link and the migration working should be:
--
--   RUN 1       row counts of all the tables below (run first)
--   RUN 2a, 2b  the two account maps, ACCOUNT_NO_MAPP and NEW_ACMAP
--   RUN 3       OPENING_BAL, the balances taken on at the migration
--   RUN 4a, 4b  T_ACCOUNT and T_ACCOUNTBALANCE, the conversion tables
--   RUN 5a-5e   the old loan accounts in the other copies of the account master
--   RUN 6       a profile of CUMOVUCH_OLD, a third old ledger copy
--   RUN 7       GL_OPENING_BALANCE_BK240824, the GL at the migration
--
-- If a query errors because a table or column is not there, skip it and tell
-- us; the rest still help. Please save the results in the Pack 4 folder on
-- OneDrive, in the subfolder Pack 9\\Export Results.
--
-- Note on pack 8: the CV_04 files in Pack 8\\Export Results are copies of the
-- pack 7 files and were not needed. Two of them (CV_04b1 and CV_04b2) are
-- shorter than the pack 7 ones (5,980 and 4,465 rows against 7,019 and
-- 5,639), so they look like exports that stopped early; we use the pack 7
-- files, and nothing needs re-running.
--==============================================================================


--==============================================================================
-- RUN 0  |  session settings  |  run once, first, in THIS worksheet
-- The pack 8 files still came out with dates as m/d/yyyy. These two lines
-- must be run in the same worksheet (same connection tab) as the queries;
-- each tab is its own session.
{SESSION}

-- RUN 0 check  |  do not export, just look at the grid
-- It must show a date like 2026-10-14 09:15:00 and the number 1234567.89.
SELECT SYSDATE AS today_as_text, 1234567.89 AS a_number FROM dual;

-- If the grid is right but the CSV still shows 10/14/2026, the export is
-- re-formatting it: Tools > Preferences > Database > NLS > Date Format =
-- YYYY-MM-DD HH24:MI:SS (type NLS in the search box at the top left of the
-- Preferences window if Database is not visible). Set once, it sticks.
"""

def run_block(r):
    rid, name, title, why, sql = r
    return f"""

--==============================================================================
-- {rid}  |  {title}  |  save as {name}.csv
-- {why}
{sql}
"""

FULL = HEAD + "".join(run_block(r) for r in RUNS) + """
--==============================================================================
-- End of pack 9. Thank you, Barry.
--==============================================================================
"""

def per_query(r):
    rid, name, title, why, sql = r
    return f"""-- MAIIC E-Banker: pack 9 ({DATE.replace('Oct', 'October')}) | Dupleix Institute
-- Read-only. Run in one SQL Developer worksheet, export the grid as CSV
-- (header row, comma, strings in double quotes, UTF-8), named as below.
-- Session settings first (RUN 0), in the same worksheet:
{SESSION}

-- {rid}  |  {title}  |  save as {name}.csv
-- {why}
{sql}
"""

README = f"""PACK 9 QUERIES  |  Dupleix Institute  |  {DATE.replace('Oct', 'October')}

One file per query, in run order. Each opens with the RUN 0 session settings,
so it can be pasted into a fresh worksheet on its own. Export each grid as CSV
(header row, comma, strings in double quotes, UTF-8) under the name in the file,
and save it in the Export Results folder next to this file. Run RUN 1 first.
The full run sheet, with the reasons for each run, is the '(all runs)' file.

Files:
  RUN 0 - session settings and check.sql
""" + "".join(f"  {r[0]} - {r[1]}.sql\n" for r in RUNS)

RUN0 = f"""-- MAIIC E-Banker: pack 9 | RUN 0 session settings and check
{SESSION}
SELECT SYSDATE AS today_as_text, 1234567.89 AS a_number FROM dual;
-- It must show a date like 2026-10-14 09:15:00 and the number 1234567.89.
"""

def pdf_bytes(text, title):
    buf = io.BytesIO()
    c = canvas.Canvas(buf, pagesize=A4)
    c.setTitle(title); c.setAuthor('Dupleix Institute')
    w, h = A4
    y = h - 40
    c.setFont('Courier', 7.6)
    for line in text.splitlines():
        while len(line) > 110:
            c.drawString(36, y, line[:110]); line = '    ' + line[110:]; y -= 9.6
            if y < 40: c.showPage(); c.setFont('Courier', 7.6); y = h - 40
        c.drawString(36, y, line); y -= 9.6
        if y < 40: c.showPage(); c.setFont('Courier', 7.6); y = h - 40
    c.save()
    return buf.getvalue()

os.makedirs(os.path.join(PACK9, "Export Results"), exist_ok=True)
stem = f"FOLLOW-UP extracts for Barry - pack 9 - {DATE}"
for ext in ("txt", "sql"):
    open(os.path.join(BASE, f"{stem}.{ext}"), "w", encoding="utf-8", newline="\r\n").write(FULL)
pdf = pdf_bytes(FULL, f"{stem}")
open(os.path.join(BASE, f"{stem}.pdf"), "wb").write(pdf)

files = {"README.txt": README, "RUN 0 - session settings and check.sql": RUN0}
for r in RUNS:
    files[f"{r[0]} - {r[1]}.sql"] = per_query(r)
files[f"{stem} (all runs).sql"] = FULL
for n, t in files.items():
    open(os.path.join(PACK9, n), "w", encoding="utf-8", newline="\r\n").write(t)
open(os.path.join(PACK9, f"{stem} (all runs).pdf"), "wb").write(pdf)

zbuf = io.BytesIO()
with zipfile.ZipFile(zbuf, "w", zipfile.ZIP_DEFLATED) as z:
    for n, t in files.items():
        z.writestr(n, t.replace("\n", "\r\n"))
zip_name = f"Pack 9 - one file per query - {DATE}.zip"
open(os.path.join(BASE, zip_name), "wb").write(zbuf.getvalue())

BODY = """Dear Barry,

Thank you for pack 8, which came through complete.

It showed that the loan accounts behind the older ledger copy (CUMVOUCH_BAK, accounts 000100750000002 to 000100750000084) are no longer in ACMASTER or ACLOANMASTER: only 000100750000001, the "Term Loans" control account, is still there. The OLD_AC_NUMBER column in today's account master is a serial number within each GL, so it doesn't give the old number either. Your two probes found where the link and the migration working should be kept: ACCOUNT_NO_MAPP and NEW_ACMAP (the account maps), T_ACCOUNT and T_ACCOUNTBALANCE (the conversion tables), and OPENING_BAL (the balances taken on).

Pack 9 reads those tables, and a few related ones: twelve grid exports, most of them small. RUN 1 gives the row counts of all of them, so please run it first; the run sheet says what to do if a table turns out large or isn't visible to you.

Two small things:
1. The CV_04 files in Pack 8\\Export Results were not needed (they're the pack 7 files). Two of them, CV_04b1 and CV_04b2, are shorter than the pack 7 copies, as if the export stopped early. We use the pack 7 files, so nothing needs re-running.
2. The dates still come out as m/d/yyyy. They load fine, but the run sheet repeats the Preferences setting that fixes it for good.

Where to save the results: the Pack 4 folder on OneDrive, in the new subfolder Pack 9\\Export Results. The queries are in Pack 9 too, one file per query, and the pack 8 review is in Pack 8\\Export Results\\Results review.

With thanks,

Edward Mazibuko
Director, Data Analytics
Dupleix Institute
"""

## CLAUDE  (2026-10-13 15:58:04 UTC)

That's the final stage, and I'll run it in order, because each step changes what the next one checks. Four jobs are still finishing first:
- breadcrumbs and the folding admin entries
- sample files and validation on every import
- the three dashboard charts
- the fresh bootstrap re-test, which is at the trial balance step now

I'll review, commit and push each as it lands, then start.

**The plan**

1. **Results first.**
   - Calculate ECL for every period through September 2026, on a database built fresh by the bootstrap, not the demo copy.
   - Compare December 2025 with MAIIC's own December 2025 ECL model and audited figures, by stage, portfolio, PD, LGD and exposure.
   - Correct genuine method differences: wrong formulas, missing inputs, data mapped to the wrong field. I won't adjust anything just to land closer to their number. Where a gap comes from their workbook or missing data, the report says so plainly.
   - Compare the EIR with the cases done by hand (Tamanda's workbook and the take-on schedules), loan by loan, to find where we fall short and why.
   - Save the report to your Downloads folder in Word and PDF.
2. **Click-through test of the whole UI, at the same time.** An agent works as a client would on a separate copy of the fresh database, through every menu entry, tab and button, from loading data to the finished reports and month-end close. It fixes anything that fails.
3. **Bootstrap with checks.** Once the corrections from step 1 are settled:
   - make sure the bootstrap loads everything we hold;
   - add checks at the end, set from a fresh run, so a client who runs it gets exactly our results and can see each check pass;
   - remove anything hardcoded or made up: where there's no data, the system says "no data".
4. **Documentation audit.**
   - Every manual brought up to date with the current screens.
   - Screenshots retaken.
   - Every page, tab, button and icon explained.
   - PDFs rendered again.
5. **Last, the next period end to end.** Run October 2026 three ways and check each produces the right results:
   - from the UI (loading data, calculating and closing the month)
   - from the bootstrap
   - from the other data-loading routes

This is several hours of work. I'll keep you posted at each stage, and put every figure in the report for you to judge rather than asserting it's close.

#!/usr/bin/env bash

set -Eeuo pipefail

# This script is executed from the existing production Git checkout by
# .github/workflows/deploy.yml. The workflow pulls origin/master first so this
# script always matches the commit being deployed.

APP_DIR="$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/.." && pwd)"
PHP_BIN="${PHP_BIN:-php}"
COMPOSER_BIN="${COMPOSER_BIN:-composer}"
NPM_BIN="${NPM_BIN:-npm}"
HEALTHCHECK_URL="${HEALTHCHECK_URL:-}"
LOCK_FILE="${DEPLOY_LOCK_FILE:-/tmp/maiic-ifrs9-deploy.lock}"
MAINTENANCE_ENABLED=0

cd "$APP_DIR"

if command -v flock >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    exec 9>"$LOCK_FILE"
    if ! flock -n 9; then
        echo "Another MAIIC deployment is already running."
        exit 1
    fi
fi

restore_application() {
    exit_code=$?

    if [[ "$MAINTENANCE_ENABLED" -eq 1 ]]; then
        "$PHP_BIN" artisan up || true
    fi

    if [[ "$exit_code" -ne 0 ]]; then
        echo "Deployment failed. The application was taken out of maintenance mode."
    fi

    exit "$exit_code"
}

trap restore_application EXIT

echo "Deploying $(git rev-parse --short HEAD) in $APP_DIR"

"$COMPOSER_BIN" install \
    --no-dev \
    --prefer-dist \
    --optimize-autoloader \
    --no-interaction \
    --no-progress

# public/build is intentionally not committed, so production builds the Vite
# assets after each successful merge to master.
"$NPM_BIN" ci
"$NPM_BIN" run build

"$PHP_BIN" artisan down --retry=60
MAINTENANCE_ENABLED=1

"$PHP_BIN" artisan migrate --force

    }

    /**
     * Ledger postings dated on or before the date, grouped by account, each in date then key order;
     * one account's only when it is named (the EIR asks for one loan at a time). Only postings on
     * the in-scope loan GLs are kept, so the Mega Farm ledger (MF_03, on the programme's GLs 1050301
     * to 1050307) is left out unless asked for: the loan book's method B asks, because the Mega Farm
     * accounts are in E-Banker's Loan Book Report (MF_05) and their carrying amount is derived from
     * their own postings; the EIR and the other readers do not (the programme is outside the EIR,
     * decision D30).
     */
    public function ledgerByAccount(?string $toDate = null, ?string $account = null, bool $withMegaFarm = false): array
    {
        $gls = self::LOAN_GLS + ($withMegaFarm ? array_flip(\App\Services\MegaFarm\MegaFarmEclService::GLS) : []);
        $by = [];
        foreach ($this->family(self::LEDGER, $toDate, null, $account) as $row) {
            $p = $row['payload'];
            if (($p['DELETE_FLAG'] ?? 'N') === 'Y' || $row['account'] === null || $row['account'] === '') {
                continue;
            }
            // only loan accounts: the GL_03 extract also carries the contra legs on
            // the income GLs (4215, 4216) and the FInES suspense (3065), which are
            // not loans and have no account master row
            $gl = trim((string) ($p['AC_GLCODE'] ?? ($p['CB_GLCODE'] ?? '')));
            if ($gl !== '' && ! isset($gls[$gl])) {
                continue;
            }
            $by[$row['account']][] = $row;
        }
        foreach ($by as &$rows) {
            usort($rows, fn ($a, $b) => [$a['row_date'], (int) $a['source_key']] <=> [$b['row_date'], (int) $b['source_key']]);
        }

        return $by;
    }

    /** The last month-end of the build in progress, and the ledger read once to it. */
    private ?string $ledgerTo = null;

    private ?array $ledgerCache = null;

    /** The masters, read once per build: they do not depend on the month. */
    private array $masterCache = [];

    /**
     * The ledger dated on or before the month-end, with the Mega Farm postings. Within a build it is
     * a slice of the ledger read once to the build's last month-end: each account's postings are in
     * date order, so the slice is the same rows a read to this month-end returns.
     */
    private function ledgerOn(string $monthEnd): array
    {
        if ($this->ledgerTo === null || $monthEnd > $this->ledgerTo) {
            return $this->zone->ledgerByAccount($monthEnd, null, true);
        }
        $this->ledgerCache ??= $this->zone->ledgerByAccount($this->ledgerTo, null, true);
        if ($monthEnd === $this->ledgerTo) {
            return $this->ledgerCache;
        }
        $out = [];
        foreach ($this->ledgerCache as $account => $rows) {
            $kept = [];
            foreach ($rows as $row) {
                if ($row['row_date'] === null || $row['row_date'] > $monthEnd) {
                    break;
                }
                $kept[] = $row;
            }
            if ($kept !== []) {
                $out[$account] = $kept;
            }
        }

        return $out;
    }

## CLAUDE  (2026-10-14 06:33:24 UTC)

Pushed (9aa67da): the loan book build now reads the ledger once per build instead of once per month. Each month after the first takes about 4 seconds instead of 40, and the rows are identical.

Earlier pushes this morning:
- **d95317b, the UI click-through fixes:**
  - a period lock screen and an "Awaiting approval" tab;
  - fee-review screens for unassigned fee lines;
  - the booked (discounted) ECL labelled correctly;

  - whole-ledger screens skip the Mega Farm ledger, so they no longer stall;
  - Support Tickets no longer shows "access denied" on a fresh install;
  - a write-off can't be proposed in a locked month.

    public function lock(string $contractId, int $reviewerId, bool $allowMakerCheckerOverride = false): ContractEir
    {
        return DB::transaction(function () use ($contractId, $reviewerId, $allowMakerCheckerOverride) {
            $contract = ContractEir::where('contract_id', $contractId)->lockForUpdate()->firstOrFail();
            if ($contract->locked_at !== null) return $contract;
            if ($contract->calculation_status !== 'CALCULATED' || $contract->eir_period === null) {
                throw new LogicException('Only a successfully calculated EIR can be approved and locked.');
            }
            if (!$allowMakerCheckerOverride && $contract->calculated_by === null) {
                throw new LogicException('The calculation has no identifiable maker and cannot be approved.');
            }
            if (!$allowMakerCheckerOverride && (int) $contract->calculated_by === $reviewerId) {
                throw new LogicException('The calculator cannot approve and lock their own EIR.');
            }

            $contract->update([
                'calculation_status' => 'LOCKED',
                'locked_at' => now(),
                'locked_by' => $reviewerId,
            ]);

            return $contract->fresh();
        });
    }

    /**
     * Lock a reviewer-approved batch without allowing one ineligible contract

     * Reopen a locked original EIR for a controlled correction. The locked
     * measurement remains append-only history and every downstream live
     * result that depended on it is invalidated before recalculation.
     */
    public function reopen(string $contractId, int $userId, string $reason): ContractEir
    {
        $reason = trim($reason);
        if (mb_strlen($reason) < 10) {
            throw new LogicException('A specific reopening reason of at least 10 characters is required.');
        }

        return DB::transaction(function () use ($contractId, $userId, $reason) {
            $contract = ContractEir::where('contract_id', $contractId)->lockForUpdate()->firstOrFail();
            if ($contract->locked_at === null || $contract->calculation_status !== 'LOCKED') {
                throw new LogicException('Only a locked original EIR can be reopened.');
            }

            DB::table('eir_calculation_history')->insert([
                'contract_id' => $contract->contract_id,
                'eir_period' => $contract->eir_period,
                'eir_nominal_annual' => $contract->eir_nominal_annual,
                'eir_effective_annual' => $contract->eir_effective_annual,
                'rate_source' => $contract->rate_source,
                'solver_iterations' => $contract->solver_iterations,
                'solver_residual' => $contract->solver_residual,
                'solver_method' => $contract->solver_method,
                'input_snapshot' => json_encode($contract->input_snapshot),
                'calculation_status' => $contract->calculation_status,
                'calculation_error' => $contract->calculation_error,
                'calculated_at' => $contract->calculated_at,
                'calculated_by' => $contract->calculated_by,
                'locked_at' => $contract->locked_at,
                'locked_by' => $contract->locked_by,
                'archive_action' => 'REOPENED',
                'archive_reason' => $reason,
                'archived_by' => $userId,
                'archived_at' => now(),
                'created_at' => now(),
                'updated_at' => now(),
            ]);

            $amortisation = DB::table('eir_amortisation')->where('contract_id', $contractId)->get();
            foreach ($amortisation as $row) {
                DB::table('eir_amortisation_history')->insert([
                    'contract_id' => $row->contract_id,
                    'reporting_period' => $row->reporting_period,
                    'opening_gross' => $row->opening_gross,
                    'interest_accrued' => $row->interest_accrued,
                    'interest_basis' => $row->interest_basis,
                    'unwind_amount' => $row->unwind_amount,
                    'cash_received' => $row->cash_received,
                    'cash_source' => $row->cash_source,
                    'modification_gain_loss' => $row->modification_gain_loss,
                    'closing_gross' => $row->closing_gross,
                    'ecl_allowance' => $row->ecl_allowance,
                    'originally_created_at' => $row->created_at,
                    'superseded_at' => now(),
                    'superseded_by' => $userId,
                    'supersession_reason' => 'Original EIR reopened: '.$reason,
                    'created_at' => now(),
                    'updated_at' => now(),
                ]);
            }
            DB::table('eir_amortisation')->where('contract_id', $contractId)->delete();

            DB::table('loan_books')->where('contract_id', $contractId)->update([
                'ecl_value_discounted' => null,
                'ecl_discounting_effect' => null,
                'ecl_discount_rate' => null,
                'ecl_discount_rate_source' => null,
                'ecl_discount_status' => 'STALE_EIR_REOPENED',

    public function test_admin_override_can_lock_own_and_unattributed_calculations(): void
    {
        $this->seedContract('OWN');
        $this->seedContract('NO-MAKER');
        $service = $this->service();
        $service->calculate('OWN', 10);
        $service->calculate('NO-MAKER');

        $result = $service->lockMany(['OWN', 'NO-MAKER'], 10, true);

        $this->assertCount(2, $result['locked']);
        $this->assertSame([], $result['skipped']);
        $this->assertSame('LOCKED', DB::table('contract_eir')->where('contract_id', 'OWN')->value('calculation_status'));
        $this->assertSame('LOCKED', DB::table('contract_eir')->where('contract_id', 'NO-MAKER')->value('calculation_status'));
        $this->assertSame(10, DB::table('contract_eir')->where('contract_id', 'OWN')->value('locked_by'));
        $this->assertSame(10, DB::table('contract_eir')->where('contract_id', 'NO-MAKER')->value('locked_by'));
    }

# MAIIC E-Banker extracts, pack 9: results review

Dupleix Institute. Review of the 14 files in this Export Results folder, received 14 October 2026 at 09:09, against the RUN 1 counts, the 31 July 2024 take-on postings in the ledger, the July 2024 loan book and the pack 7 ledger copy.
